## 1. The crate DAG

Dependency direction is one-way, enforced by review and by keeping worker-only features (entropy activation, `getrandom` "js") in the worker crate alone.

```
cachet-core   ← cachet-crypto ← cachet-worker
cachet-push   ← cachet-cli
cachet-core   ← cachet-crypto ← cachet-cli (login needs the key format + base32)
```

| Crate | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `cachet-core` | Pure domain logic: narinfo parse/serialize and canonicalization, store-path and NAR key validation, Nix base32, lease and generation and upload-record documents, multipart part-plan math, GC mark/sweep/gates/plan over callbacks, OIDC claim-check policy over a decoded JWT, JWKS cache policy, OAuth and device-flow payload shapes, the error-code table and RFC 9457 types, the Clock/Rng traits. No I/O, no ambient clock, no worker types. |
| `cachet-crypto` | Primitives and wire crypto: SHA-256 (sha2), NothHash format conversions (base16/base32/base64), ed25519 sign/verify and key generation (ed25519-dalek), constant-time compare (subtle), JWT decode plus RS256 verification of a JWKS (WebCrypto through web_sys on wasm; the pure-rust `rsa`+`sha2` pair as the spike-decided alternative), the Nix narinfo fingerprint construction. Wasm-clean by construction; `ring`/`aws-lc-rs` banned and cargo-deny-enforced. |
| `cachet-worker` | The deployable leaf: route table, RFC 9457 error boundary, R2/KV/Cache-API adapters, JWKS fetcher with per-isolate cache, GitHub API client for user-token verdicts, config parsing, structured logging, cron entry and the resumable GC driver, the SSR UI, OpenAPI serving (utoipa). The only crate with `getrandom` "js" and `worker` dependencies; compiles only to wasm32. |
| `cachet-push` | The push pipeline as a native library: store snapshot, snapshot diff, upstream filter (HEAD probes at 16 concurrency), staging through `nix copy --to file://?compression=zstd`, upload plan (single vs multipart), NARs-before-narinfos upload with fresh OIDC per request, lease renewal, never-fail-the-job semantics. Shells to `nix` through std::process. Consumed by the CLI and, as a binary, by the public GitHub Action. |
| `cachet-cli` | The native binary (`cachet`): `login` (GitHub device flow), `setup` (managed nix.conf block + netrc), `keygen` (bootstrap key generation), `push` (dry-run by default off the runner, full push in CI). clap + reqwest(rustls) + nix-archive + nix-derivation + nix-flake-lock. Built by cargo-dist for four triples. |

## 2. The worker module layout

`crates/cachet-worker/src/` keeps every route a thin adapter over `cachet-core`: validate the path, authorize, call core, translate the result. All I/O lives in `edge/`.

```
lib.rs            #[event(fetch)] dispatch, #[event(scheduled)] GC entry
config.rs         env parsing; deployment identity from vars, never from source
error.rs          ClientError -> RFC 9457 problem+json; invariant panics -> 500
log.rs            one JSON object per line; no credential fields, ever
http/
  router.rs       the route table as one match; query-string modifiers for multipart
  problem.rs      RFC 9457 body construction
  openapi.rs      utoipa spec assembly, GET /api/openapi.json
  ui.rs           SSR login page + post-login instruction page (string templates)
routes/
  health.rs       GET /nix-cache-info, unauthenticated inline constant
  read.rs         GET/HEAD narinfo and NAR, generation-scoped edge cache
  write.rs        PUT narinfo (with verification + signing), PUT NAR
  multipart.rs    POST ?uploads, PUT ?uploadId&partNumber, POST ?uploadId, DELETE ?uploadId
  roots.rs        POST /roots/{project}, GET /roots, GET /roots/{project}
  admin.rs        GET /api/cache-info, /api/stats, /api/projects, /api/leases/{project}
  browser.rs      GET /login, /auth/github/callback, /logout, GET / (UI)
edge/
  bucket.rs       R2 binding adapter (get/put/head/list/delete, multipart APIs)
  kv.rs           sessions + verdicts; the only KV users
  cache_api.rs    worker::Cache adapter; generation-scoped keys; HEAD bypasses
  jwks.rs         per-isolate JWKS holder; fetch through worker Fetch; Clock-injected policy from core
  github.rs       api.github.com client: /user, org membership, with verdict hashing
  clock.rs        js_sys::Date::now() sampled once per request into the Clock trait
  rng.rs          getrandom-backed Rng leaf; the only ambient entropy in the tree
gc/
  driver.rs       stage runner with the cursor document; deadline-aware batching
  stages.rs       enum of stage transitions persisting artifacts under gc-runs/{runId}/
signing.rs        the verify-then-sign pipeline over routes/write.rs inputs
```

## 3. The key spaces

R2 is the only persistent cache-data store. KV holds exactly two kinds of volatile state.

| R2 key | Writer | Reader | Content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{hash32}.narinfo` | write route (after verification, with Sig appended) | read route, closure walk | canonicalized narinfo text |
| `nar/{fileHash52}.nar[{suffix}]` | NAR PUT or multipart complete | read route, narinfo verification | NAR bytes |
| `meta/generation` | GC destructive sweep end | read path | `{"generation":N,"bumpedAtMs":M}\n` |
| `roots/{project}` | POST /roots/{project} | GET leases, GC, UI | lease JSON, 2-space, keys in fixed order |
| `uploads/{uploadId}` | multipart create | multipart part/complete/abort, stale-upload reaper | bookkeeping JSON |
| `gc-runs/{runId}/{stage}` | GC driver | reports, operator debugging | stage artifacts + cursor document |
| `gc-reports/{runId}.json` | GC final stage | admin API, operators | run report JSON |

| KV namespace / key | TTL | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions/{sessionId}` | 12 hours (rolling on use) | browser session: GitHub login, avatar, admin flag |
| `verdicts/{sha256(accessToken)}` | 5 minutes | GitHub user-token verdict: `{login, orgMember, admin}` |

The internal prefixes (`meta/`, `roots/`, `uploads/`, `gc-runs/`, `gc-reports/`) are unreachable from a request by construction (the two client key shapes are the only admitted patterns) and refused a second time by the GC candidate filter (paired enforcement). The KV token itself is never stored, only its digest.

## 4. The three auth flows

Read auth accepts an OIDC token (Bearer or Basic password) or a validated GitHub user token (Basic password or Bearer). Write auth accepts OIDC-Bearer only. The check order on every route is: key validation, then config validation, then authorization, then body and shape guards, then the work. A malformed key is 400 even unauthenticated; an unauthenticated well-formed write is 401.

**Browser OAuth (UI sessions).** `GET /login` redirects to `https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize` with the deployment's OAuth App client id and a one-time `state` stored in KV with a 10-minute TTL. The callback at `/auth/github/callback` exchanges the code at `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` with the client secret, fetches `/user`, checks org membership through `/user/memberships/orgs/{org}` (requires `read:org`), mints a 128-bit random session id, writes `sessions/{id}` with a 12-hour TTL, and sets `Set-Cookie: session=<id>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`. The session carries login plus `admin: login ∈ CACHET_ADMINS`. Sessions never appear in URLs, never in logs.

**CLI device flow.** `cachet login --url <url>` POSTs `https://github.com/login/device/code` with the deployment's OAuth App client id (fetched from `GET /api/cache-info`, which is unauthenticated and carries the public config: cache public key, OAuth client id, org slug) and scope `read:org`. The user opens the verification URI and enters the code; the CLI polls `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` until approval, then stores the resulting GitHub user token in an 0600 file under `~/.config/cachet/` (keyring optional later). The worker never participates in the flow; it validates the resulting token per request: sha256 the presented token, read `verdicts/{digest}` from KV, on a miss call `api.github.com/user` and the org-membership endpoint, cache the verdict for 5 minutes. Revocation convergence and exfiltration exposure are both bounded by that TTL.

**GitHub OIDC (CI).** Bearer JWT. RS256 verified against `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com/.well-known/jwks`; the JWKS cache is per-isolate with a 10-minute TTL, one forced refetch per request on an unknown `kid`, stale fallback on fetch failure, 503 `auth_unavailable` with no cached document. Claim policy in core: algorithm pinned RS256 by construction (never read from the header), `iss` exact, `aud` exact-string equality (an array aud is rejected), `repository_owner` exact membershp against `CACHET_ORGS`, `exp`/`nbf`/`iat` against the injected clock with a small tolerance, required claims present (`exp`, `iat`, `aud`, `iss`, `repository`, `repository_owner`, `ref`). Lease renewal additionally requires `ref == CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF` (403 `forbidden_ref`), and `POST /roots/{project}` requires `project` to equal the `repository` claim with `/` replaced by `-` (403 `forbidden_project`, the fix for the old multi-tenancy hole). `run_id` and `sha` land in the lease as provenance, defaulting to `"unknown"`.

## 5. The signing pipeline

Narinfo PUT, after key validation and write auth and the 411/413 guards:

```
body = read at most NARINFO_BYTES_MAX
doc  = parseNarinfo(body)                               else 400 malformed_narinfo
check storePathHash(doc.StorePath) == request key hash  else 400
url  = doc.URL
check suffix(url) ∈ {"", ".zst"}                        else 400 unsupported_compression
nar = bucket.head(url)                                  else 409 narinfo_nar_missing
bytes = bucket.get(url) streaming
if suffix == ".zst":
    plain  = stream through ruzstd decoder
    FileHash must == "sha256:" ++ b16(sha256(compressed stream))   else 400 file_hash_mismatch
    FileSize must == compressed byte count                          else 400 file_hash_mismatch
    NarHash  must == "sha256:" ++ b16(sha256(decompressed stream)) else 400 nar_hash_mismatch
    NarSize  must == decompressed byte count                        else 400 nar_hash_mismatch
else:
    NarHash == sha256(bytes), NarSize == len(bytes), FileHash/FileSize if present agree
canon = canonicalize(doc): fixed field order, Sig lines kept in input order,
        unknown lines preserved verbatim in order
assert verification ran before any signing call      (crate-level typestate)
fp   = sha256("1;" ++ StorePath ++ ";" ++ NarHash ++ ";" ++ NarSize ++ ";" ++ join(References, ","))
sig  = ed25519_sign(deployment secret, fp)
out  = canon + "Sig: {CACHET_KEY_NAME}:{base64(sig)}\n"   (existing Sig lines kept)
bucket.put(key, out)
```

The verify-then-sign order is enforced by construction: the function that produces the `Sig` line takes a `VerifiedNar` newtype that only the verification stage constructs. The worker never accepts a narinfo whose verified hashes disagree. NAR PUTs stream into R2 while a running SHA-256 accumulates over the body, so a later narinfo's FileHash is checked against what the cache actually stored.

## 6. The GC algorithm

Cron-fires (`0 5 * * *`), armed from day one, resumable across invocations. One scheduled invocation has a wall-clock budget of 13 minutes and a binding-op budget of 900; the driver persists a cursor document at each stage boundary and exits cleanly when either budget is within a named headroom constant, resuming on the next cron tick.

1. **Start**: read or create `gc-runs/{runId}/cursor.json` (`{runId, stage, stageCursor}`).
2. **Leases**: list `roots/` paginated (bounded pages; truncation is a gate), read each lease, drop expired ones (`nowMs - renewedAtMs >= 30d`), collect and validate root hashes. Unparseable lease or root is a gate.
3. **Mark**: iterative BFS with a visited set capped at 100k paths; one `readNarinfo` callback per newly visited path, asserting reads == visits. Unreadable root narinfo is a gate; unreadable deep narinfo marks the node, stops descent, and is counted. Budget exhaustion is a gate.
4. **Inventory**: list the bucket paginated with continuation cursors persisted in the cursor document. Candidates exclude reserved prefixes and `roots/`, `uploads/` etc. Unmarked and older than the 14-day grace window goes into the sweep set.
5. **Gates**: sweep fraction over 0.25, unreadable root, unparseable root, walk budget, truncated inventory, truncated leases, corrupt `meta/generation`. Any trip aborts; the run writes its report and deletes nothing.
6. **Sweep (gated proceed)**: delete unmarked narinfos first, persist progress, then delete unmarked NARs in bounded batches, persist per batch. NEVER-DANGLE holds at every instant.
7. **Bump**: write `meta/generation` with generation+1 and `bumpedAtMs`. GENERATION-AFTER-SWEEP bounds stale edge serves to 60 seconds.
8. **Report**: write `gc-reports/{runId}.json` with counts, gates, deletes, durations. Stale multipart uploads older than `UPLOAD_STALE_MAX_DAYS` are aborted in the same run.

Stage artifacts pass `{key, count, sha256}` rather than state, so the workflow-result-size problem of the TS design never reappears.

## 7. The alchemy stack

`alchemy.run.ts` exports the root stack; `infra/{stage,resources,secrets}.ts` are pure modules. Deploy verb: `bun alchemy deploy --yes --adopt --stage production`. State: `Cloudflare.state()` with `ALCHEMY_LOCAL_STATE=1` fallback. `tsconfig.alchemy.json` typecheck is a CI job frontier (inside `scripts` or its own verb). Exactly pinned: alchemy 2.0.0-beta.70 and effect 4.0.0-beta.102, bumped together.

```ts
// infra/stage.ts — stage grammar: "production" | "dev" | "dev-<name>"
//   parseCachetStage, resolveWorkerName("cachet", stage) -> "cachet" / "cachet-dev-<name>"
//   resolveCachetDomains(stage) -> { cache: "pkg-cache.example.org" } from env; none on dev
export default Alchemy.Stack("cachet", {
  providers: Cloudflare.providers(),
  state: process.env.ALCHEMY_LOCAL_STATE ? Alchemy.localState() : Cloudflare.state(),
}, Effect.gen(function* () {
  const stage    = parseCachetStage(yield* Alchemy.Stage);
  const bucket   = yield* Cloudflare.R2Bucket("cache", { name: resolveName("bucket", stage) });
  const sessions = yield* Cloudflare.KVNamespace("sessions", { title: resolveName("sessions", stage) });
  const verdicts = yield* Cloudflare.KVNamespace("verdicts", { title: resolveName("verdicts", stage) });
  const secrets  = yield* createCachetSecrets(stage);   // Secrets Store: signing key, OAuth client secret
  const worker   = yield* Cloudflare.Worker("cachet", {
    name: resolveWorkerName("cachet", stage),
    main: "../crates/cachet-worker/build/index.js",     // worker-build output
    bundle: false,                                       // SPIKE T0
    bindings: { CACHE_BUCKET: bucket, SESSIONS: sessions, VERDICTS: verdicts, ...vars },
    secrets: [signingKey, oauthClientId, oauthClientSecret],
    domains: [domain], crons: ["0 5 * * *"], cpu: { limit_ms: 300000 },
  });
  return { worker };
}));
```

Vars: `CACHET_ORGS`, `CACHET_ADMINS`, `CACHET_AUDIENCE`, `CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF`, `CACHET_KEY_NAME`. Secrets (Secrets Store, created from `process.env` at deploy, prompted once by bootstrap): `CACHET_SIGNING_KEY`, `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`. The worker receives bindings only; there is no infisical anywhere. If SPIKE T0 fails, the fallback is documented: alchemy manages everything except the worker, which deploys by `wrangler deploy` against a generated `wrangler.jsonc` that adopts the same resources.

## 13. The threat model's ten scenarios

`docs/security/threat-model.md` writes each as: the attacker, the mechanism that defends, the lane that mechanically enforces it.

1. External stranger poisons the cache: write auth is OIDC-only with JWKS pinning and org membership; enforced by workerd auth tests and unit claim-policy tests.
2. Stolen GitHub user token: read-only scope, org-membership gate, verdict TTL bounds exposure, GitHub-side revocation; enforced by workerd token tests and a golden verdict-document test.
3. Forged or mis-scoped OIDC from an in-org repo: RS256 pin, exact aud, `iss` check, project equals `repository` claim; unit exhaustive negative cases, golden JWT vectors, the kani claim-check proof where bounded.
4. Forged narinfo signatures: key custody in Secrets Store, signing only after FileHash and NarHash verification over stored bytes; enforced by write-route workerd tests, the signing typestate, golden signature vectors against real `nix sign-paths` output, `nix store verify --sigs-needed 1` in smoke.
5. Tampered R2 bytes: hash-verified pipeline treats R2 as untrusted at rest; reads verify nothing (Nix does), writes verify everything; workerd tests corrupt a stored NAR and assert the narinfo write is refused.
6. Session theft: HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax cookies, 12-hour TTL, ids are 128-bit random, never in URLs or logs; workerd cookie-flag assertions plus the log-hygiene test (no token-shaped strings in emitted logs).
7. Laptop token exfiltrated from disk: token lives 0600, read-only, GitHub revokable, verdict TTL 5 minutes caps server-side staleness; enforced by CLI file-mode tests and verdict-TTL unit tests.
8. GC as deletion vector: leases bound to the repository claim, gates (sweep fraction, grace window, unreadable roots, truncations, budget) abort; property laws over the plan plus workerd gate-trip tests.
9. Supply chain: cargo deny policy, exact pins, no `ring`/`aws-lc-rs`, dependabot weekly, the wasm-hygiene gate scanning the compiled artifact.
10. Signing-key extraction: Workers secrets are never readable back, rotation is redeploy-and-rearm, the bootstrap env file is deleted after deploy; enforced by the bootstrap script test plus the wasm-hygiene bundle string scan.

## 15. v1 acceptance criteria

1. On a fresh Cloudflare account, `just bootstrap` produces a serving cache on a custom domain with no manual Cloudflare console steps after the checklist.

6. Every lane and gate is green as enumerated in section 9; the lanes.toml ⇔ docs ⇔ ci.yml ⇔ CLAUDE.md bijections hold.

8. The threat model's ten scenarios each name an existing passing test or job.
9. cargo-dist publishes the four-triple `cachet` binary on a tag; the action consumes exactly that artifact.
10. Bundle hygiene: the shipped wasm contains no `ring`, `aws-lc`, or `tokio` symbols and no secret-shaped strings; the compressed bundle fits its documented budget.

cachet-crypto    pure computation: ed25519-dalek signing, sha2 hashing, nix
                 base32/base64, ruzstd streaming decoder. Kani proofs colocated.
    ^
cachet-api       the route table derived from the checked-in spec, RFC 9457
                 shapes from the spec's components, spec serving, SSR page.
    ^
cachet-worker    the deployable leaf: workers-rs entry (fetch + scheduled),
                 R2/KV/Cache/GitHub adapters, JWKS per-isolate cache, signing-key
                 custody. The only crate with getrandom/js enabled (seam rule).

cachet-push      the push algorithm as a native library: snapshot, diff,
                 upstream filter, staging, upload, lease renewal. nix-archive,
                 nix-derivation, nix-flake-lock live here, never on wasm.
    ^
cachet-cli       the `cachet` binary (clap): login, setup, push, keygen, doctor.
                 Uses cachet-push and cachet-core (shared constants and key
                 validation, so client and server cannot disagree about a limit).
```

| Crate | One-sentence responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `cachet-core` | Every protocol decision as a total function over injected values: narinfo grammar, key validation, leases and roots payloads, generation document, multipart part planning, GC mark/sweep/gates, OIDC claim policy, verdict-cache policy, the code→status table. |
| `cachet-crypto` | All hashing, signing, and decoding the signing pipeline needs, as pure functions of bytes: ed25519 sign/verify, SHA-256, nix base32/base64, ruzstd streaming decompression. |
| `cachet-api` | The HTTP surface bound to the checked-in `docs/openapi.yaml` (the spec is the source of truth): routes derive from its operations, handlers bind to operationIds, problem+json rendered from its error components, spec bytes served at `/api/openapi.json`; plus the SSR page. |
| `cachet-worker` | The only network surface: adapts Request/Env/R2/KV/Cache/GitHub endpoints into cachet-core calls and renders results; all ambient clock, entropy, and I/O live here behind seams. |
| `cachet-push` | The action's push pipeline as a library: store snapshot and diff, upstream filter at bounded concurrency, zstd staging via `nix copy --to file://`, NAR-before-narinfo upload with fresh OIDC per request, lease renewal. |
| `cachet-cli` | The user-facing binary: device-flow login against github.com, nix.conf and netrc setup, `cachet push` for dry-run and for the public action, bootstrap keygen helpers. |

## 2. Worker module layout

`crates/cachet-worker/src/`:

```
lib.rs, entry.rs   #[event(fetch)] router and #[event(scheduled)] GC entry; fetch
                   pipeline: validate -> authorize -> guards -> work; clock sampled
                   once per request and injected everywhere after that.
routes/{read,write_nar,multipart,roots,auth_flow,self_api,ui,openapi}.rs
edge/{bucket,cache_api,kv_store,github,jwks_fetch,config}.rs
sign/pipeline.rs   edge half of signing: streams the stored NAR through the
                   hash+decompress+hash check, then signs; never buffers a body.
gc/{run,stages}.rs budgeted cron driver over a resumable cursor document.
seams.rs           RealClock (js_sys::Date), RealRng (getrandom js).
log.rs             JSON events and the old level table.
```

Check order on every route, ported verbatim: key/project validation, then authorization (starting with config validation), then request-shape and size guards, then the work. Malformed key answers 400 before any credential is read; unauthenticated write answers 401 before any 411.

## 3. KV and R2 key tables

R2 (the only persistent cache state):

| Key class | Writer | Reader | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{hash32}.narinfo` | narinfo PUT (signed) | read path, GC mark | 32 chars of the nix base-32 alphabet. |
| `nar/{hash52}.nar[.xz/.zst/.bz2/.gz/.br/.lzip/.lz4]` | NAR PUT, multipart | read path | signing path validates only `none` and `.zst` in v1. |
| `meta/generation` | GC sweep | read path | corrupt means bypass edge cache, never assume zero. |
| `roots/{project}` | POST /roots/{project} | GC roots | last-write-wins; provenance from OIDC claims only. |
| `uploads/{uploadId}` | multipart create | part/complete/abort | key, totalBytes, expectedParts, createdAtMs. |
| `gc-runs/{runId}/...` | GC stages | GC stages | inventory parts, mark outcome, cursor. |
| `gc-reports/{runId}` | GC report | admin/self stats | golden-locked shape. |

Reserved prefixes unreachable from any request by construction; sweep's candidate filter refuses them a second time (paired enforcement).

KV (auth state only):

| Key | Value | TTL | Writer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `oauth-state/{state}` | callback nonce metadata | 600 s, deleted on consume | `/_auth/login` |
| `sess/{sessionId}` | `{ login, createdAtMs }` | 14 d absolute | `/_auth/callback` |
| `ghverdict/{sha256(token)}` | `{ login, orgMembership, allow, checkedAtMs }` | 600 s allow / 60 s deny | read/work auth when a non-JWT credential arrives |

KV eventual consistency is acceptable for every row: misses fail closed (re-login), and a stale positive verdict is bounded by the 600 s TTL, which the threat model records as the revocation window for a compromised laptop token.

## 4. Auth sequences

Browser OAuth (UI): `GET /_auth/login` writes `oauth-state/{state}` (600 s) and 302s to github.com with `client_id`, callback URL, `read:org read:user` scope, state. `GET /_auth/callback` consumes the state (fail closed on miss), exchanges code for a user token with the server-held client secret, does `GET /user` plus `GET /orgs/{org}/memberships/{login}` per configured org until one confirms, then mints a KV session (14 d) and sets `cachet_session=…; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`. `/api/self/*` additionally requires the login in `CACHET_ADMINS`.

Device flow (CLI): `cachet login --url` GETs the unauthenticated `/api/public/config` (`{ oauthClientId, orgs }`; the client id is public), then runs GitHub's device endpoints directly (device/code, verification URI, poll access_token with the device-code grant). The token never leaves the laptop. On read: non-JWT-shaped credentials are SHA-256'd, checked in `ghverdict/` KV, validated on miss against `GET /user` + org membership, verdict cached (600 s/60 s). Laptops hold READ scope only.

OIDC (CI, the only write credential): RS256 pinned by policy (never read from the token header), JWKS per-isolate cache (10 min TTL, one refetch on unknown kid, stale fallback, never a bypass), `iss` exact, `aud` exact single string (arrays refused), `repository_owner` exact match against `CACHET_ORGS`, `exp/nbf/iat` against the sampled clock, required claims `exp, iat, aud, iss, repository, repository_owner, ref` present and string-typed. Multi-tenancy fix: `POST /roots/{project}` requires `project == hyphenate(repository)` and the branch ref equals `CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF`. Admin tokens are read-only, so nobody renews outside their own repository. Read resolution order: JWT-shaped → OIDC; otherwise the verdict path. The old two-slot shared read token and Infisical are deleted from the design.

## 5. Signing pipeline (pseudo-code)

```
fn sign_and_store(body, key, cfg, bucket, clock) -> Status
    doc = parse_narinfo(body)                            // total; 400 on any failure
    require StorePath/URL/NarHash/NarSize
    require hash(doc.storePath) == key                   // path agreement -> 400
    require suffix(doc.url) in { "", ".zst" }            // -> unsupported_compression 400
    require bucket.head(doc.url).exists()                // NEVER-DANGLE -> 409
    measured = stream bucket.get(doc.url)
               |> tee(update(compressed_hasher),
                      through(ruzstd, update(nar_hasher), count))
    require measured.decompressed_count == doc.narSize   // bomb guard and truth
    require b32(measured.nar_hash) == doc.narHash        // -> nar_hash_mismatch 400
    if FileHash present: require b32(compressed) == it   // -> file_hash_mismatch 400
    require b32(compressed) == hash named in doc.url     // key-name truth
    out = canonicalize(doc, fill FileHash/FileSize)      // unknown lines preserved
    fingerprint = "{storePath};{narHash};{narSize};{refs.join(',')}"
    out += "Sig: {cfg.host}-1:{base64(ed25519_sign(cfg.key, fingerprint))}"
    bucket.put(key, out)                                 // 204
```

Laws named by tests: never sign before every hash comparison passes; canonicalization idempotent and unknown-field-preserving (kani + property + golden); emitted narinfo verifies under `nix store verify --sigs-needed 1` (golden + live smoke). CPU risk flagged: hashing a multi-hundred-MiB object in one request is work the TS worker never did, so T2 measures throughput in workerd and `limits.cpu_ms` is raised to the paid-plan request-class ceiling for the narinfo write path.

## 6. GC sketch

Cron `0 5 * * *`, driver budgeted and cursor-resumable (no Workflow), ARMED from day one; armed/grace/retention are vars with strong production defaults so staging can zero the grace window for the smoke without backdating R2 timestamps. Phases: inventory (paginated list, prefix-filtered, artifacts to `gc-runs/`), roots (lease listing and parse, active = renewed within 30 d computed forward), mark (iterative BFS over References, visited set cap 100k doubles as read cap, one read per visited asserted), gates (sweep fraction > 0.25, unreadable root, unparseable root, budget exhausted, inventory truncated, leases truncated, generation unreadable; any trip aborts), sweep (unmarked AND older than grace), delete (narinfos before NARs, bounded batches, stale `uploads/` reclaimed after 7 d), bump generation (every destructive sweep), report (`gc-runs/` + `gc-reports/`).

## 7. Alchemy stack sketch and SPIKE T0

Stage grammar (`infra/stage.ts`, pure): `production`, `staging`, `dev`, `dev-<name>`; suffix `""`/`-staging`/`-dev-<name>`; names `cachet-<base><suffix>`. The domain comes from the bootstrap-written env file (deployment identity), the grammar only decides the `staging.` prefix. No preview stages (ADR-0008).

Stack sketch:

```ts
Alchemy.Stack("cachet", {
  providers: Cloudflare.providers(),
  state: process.env.ALCHEMY_LOCAL_STATE ? Alchemy.localState() : Cloudflare.state(),
}, Effect.gen(function* () {
  const stage = parseCachetStage(yield* Alchemy.Stage);           // placeholder -> dev
  const secrets = yield* createCachetSecrets(stage);              // signing key, OAuth secret; Secrets Store per account, names per stage, Redacted at the boundary; absent on dev
  const bucket  = yield* Cloudflare.R2Bucket("store", {...});
  const authKv  = yield* Cloudflare.KVNamespace("auth", {...});
  yield* Cloudflare.Worker("cachet", {
    name, main: "build/worker/index.js", bundle: false /* SPIKE T0 */, assets: "assets/",
    kv_namespaces: [authKv], r2_buckets: [bucket],
    secrets: { CACHET_SIGNING_KEY, CACHET_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET },
    vars: { CACHET_ORGS, CACHET_ADMINS, CACHET_AUDIENCE, CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF,
            CACHET_HOST, CACHET_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID,
            CACHET_GC_ARMED, CACHET_GC_GRACE_MS, CACHET_LEASE_RETENTION_MS },
    domains: [stageDomain(stage)],          // custom domain only, never workers.dev
    crons: ["0 5 * * *"], cpu_ms: PAID_PLAN_CEILING,
  });
}));
```

Pins: `alchemy@2.0.0-beta.70` + `effect@4.0.0-beta.102`, bumped together. `tsconfig.alchemy.json` typechecked as a gate. Deploy verb: `bun alchemy deploy --yes --adopt --stage production`. SPIKE T0 ordered first: confirm alchemy v2 `bundle: false` ships the worker-build artifact unchanged; fallback is alchemy owning every resource except the worker, which `wrangler deploy` publishes from `build/worker`; either outcome is recorded in ADR-0008 and docs/DEPLOY.md.

# cachet v1: self-hosted nix binary cache, Rust on Cloudflare Workers

## Context

The existing cachet (`/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet`) is a working TypeScript Cloudflare Worker that serves as an org-wide nix binary cache, with `cachet-action` as its only writer. It works but carries platform-accident complexity, a documented trust regression (the signing key leaked into the worker environment via Infisical), a GC that has never deleted anything (SWEEP_ARMED=false), a multi-tenancy hole in lease renewal, and 471 lines of fragile login shell. The rewrite target `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/nox/cachet` is an empty git repo (PROSE.md already copied in from sesame). The goal: anyone can clone the repo, run one bootstrap flow, and get an org-scoped, authenticated nix binary cache in their own Cloudflare account, with a login UI, a device-flow CLI for laptops, and OIDC-authenticated CI pushes. Reference repos: `nox/sesame` (project hygiene), `nox/lynk` (alchemy-run orchestration). PROSE.md is binding law for all prose the repo ships.

## Locked decisions (from user)

The decisions below are final; everything else in this plan follows from them.

- Auth is GitHub only: browser OAuth for the UI, GitHub device flow for the CLI, GitHub OIDC for CI. No magic link, no passwords, no infisical, no Postgres, no sesame-as-IdP.
- One deployment serves exactly one configured GitHub org (CACHET_ORGS comma list). Nobody outside the org can authenticate at all.
- Signing is server-side: the worker holds a per-deployment ed25519 key (generated at bootstrap, Cloudflare Secrets Store). The user verified the FlakeHub Cache pattern (GitHub OIDC authenticates CI, the service signs) and it is feasible; poison resistance lives in write-path hash verification, not in a reproducibility verifier, which is dropped entirely.
- Laptops are read-only. Writes are OIDC-only. `POST /roots/{project}` requires project == hyphenated `repository` claim (closes the old lease-clobbering hole) plus ref == CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF.
- UI is minimal SSR in v1 (landing, login, instruction page); a separate SPA comes later. Hard requirement now: OpenAPI-first (`docs/openapi.yaml` authored before handlers, served at /api/openapi.json, drift-locked by a golden test) and RFC 9457 problem+json errors.
- No DST/sim harness. Lanes are exactly: unit, property (hegel), golden, kani, workerd, live-smoke. Gates: fmt, clippy, deny, doc-manifest, lane-manifest, actionlint, scripts, wasm-hygiene, alchemy-types.
- GC is armed from day one. The old collector never swept; this one ships armed, gated, and cursor-resumable.
- Store: R2 only for cache data (ported layout), KV only for sessions/verdicts/oauth-state. No D1.

## Crate DAG

Workspace resolver 2, `[lints] workspace = true`, publish=false version 0.0.1, Apache-2.0, exact toolchain pin (1.95.0, wasm32-unknown-unknown + four native triples). Direction is one-way; path deps only.

| Crate | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `cachet-core` | Pure domain: narinfo grammar and canonical serialization, store-path/NAR key validation, nix base32, lease/generation/upload-record documents, multipart part-plan math, GC mark/sweep/gates/plan over injected callbacks, OIDC claim policy, verdict policy, error-code table. Clock/Rng traits defined here, no I/O, no ambient entropy. |
| `cachet-crypto` | Pure computation: sha2, ed25519-dalek (sign/verify/keygen), narinfo fingerprint, RS256 verify (WebCrypto via web_sys or pure-rust rsa+sha2; SPIKE decides), ruzstd streaming decode. Kani proofs colocated. |
| `cachet-api` | HTTP surface bound to `docs/openapi.yaml`: routes derive from operations, problem+json from spec components, spec bytes served verbatim, SSR page. |
| `cachet-worker` | Deployable leaf: `#[event(fetch)]` + `#[event(scheduled)]`, R2/KV/Cache/GitHub adapters, per-isolate JWKS cache, signing pipeline over streams, GC driver. The only crate with `worker` deps and getrandom/js. |
| `cachet-push` | Push pipeline as a native library: snapshot/diff, upstream filter at concurrency 16, `nix copy --to file://?compression=zstd` staging (unsigned), NARs-before-narinfos upload with fresh OIDC per request, lease renewal, never-fail-the-job semantics. nix-archive, nix-derivation, nix-flake-lock live here (native only). |
| `cachet-cli` | The `cachet` binary (clap): `login` (device flow), `setup` (managed nix.conf block + netrc), `push [--dry-run]`, `keygen`, `doctor` (401-vs-404 probe). reqwest+rustls. Released by cargo-dist for four triples. |

nix-flake-lock's concrete job: during push, parse the repo's flake.lock, record the pinned root revision in lease metadata (UI display), and validate the follows-graph. nix-derivation parses .drv/store paths client-side. nix-archive verifies/encodes NARs client-side; it cannot go to wasm (libc+rustix unconditional deps) and is not needed there because the worker computes hashes over bytes, which sha2+ruzstd cover; upstreaming a unix-feature gate is a nice-to-have spike, not a blocker.

## Auth flows

Check order on every route, ported from the TS worker: key validation, config validation, authorization, body/shape guards, work. Malformed key is 400 before any credential read; unauthenticated write is 401 before any 411.

1. Browser OAuth: `GET /_auth/login` writes `oauth-state/{state}` (KV, 600s, single-use) and 302s to github.com (scope `read:org read:user`, deployment client id). `/_auth/callback` exchanges the code with the server-held client secret, checks `GET /user` + org membership, mints a 128-bit session id, writes `sess/{id}` (KV, 12h), sets `cachet_session=…; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`. `/api/self/*` also requires login ∈ CACHET_ADMINS.
2. CLI device flow: `cachet login --url` GETs unauthenticated `/api/public/config` (`{oauthClientId, orgs, host}`), runs github.com device endpoints directly, stores the GitHub user token at 0600 under `~/.config/cachet/`. The worker never sees the flow; it validates the token per request: sha256(token) → KV `ghverdict/` (600s allow / 60s deny), miss → `GET /user` + org membership via GitHub API. Verdict TTL is the documented revocation window (ADR).
3. GitHub OIDC (the only write credential): RS256 pinned by policy, JWKS per-isolate cache (10min TTL, one refetch on unknown kid, stale fallback, 503 `auth_unavailable` cold), `iss`/`aud` exact (aud arrays refused), `repository_owner` ∈ CACHET_ORGS, required claims `exp,iat,aud,iss,repository,repository_owner,ref`, exp/nbf/iat against the injected clock. Lease renewal additionally: ref == CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF (403 forbidden_ref), project == hyphenated repository claim (403 forbidden_project, new code).

## Signing pipeline

Narinfo PUT after validation, auth, and 411/413 guards. Verify-then-sign is enforced by construction: the signing function takes a VerifiedNar newtype only the verifier constructs. Wire hash format is nix base32 with `sha256:` prefix; the fingerprint is `"1;<storePath>;<narHash>;<narSize>;<refs joined by ,>"` signed directly with ed25519 (no outer pre-hash). The Sig line is `Sig: {CACHET_HOST}-1:<base64>`, existing Sig lines preserved. Steps: parse (total, 400), required StorePath/URL/NarHash/NarSize, StorePath hash == URL key (400), suffix ∈ {"", ".zst"} (400 unsupported_compression), bucket.head(URL) (409 narinfo_nar_missing), stream the stored NAR through tee(compressed-sha256, ruzstd→nar-sha256+count), NarSize == decompressed count (bomb guard), NarHash/NarSize/FileHash/FileSize agreement (400 nar_hash_mismatch / file_hash_mismatch), compressed hash == hash named in URL key, canonicalize preserving unknown fields, append Sig, bucket.put, 204. CPU: this path hashes multi-hundred-MiB objects, so deployments require a paid plan (`cpu_ms=300000`); SPIKE T2 measures ruzstd+sha2 throughput in workerd and records the number in ADR-0022/docs/contracts.md.

## GC

Cron `0 5 * * *` (staging configurable), cursor-resumable, no Cloudflare Workflow. Budgets: 13-minute wall clock, 900 binding ops per invocation, named headroom constants, cursor persisted at stage boundaries, resume next tick. Stages: inventory (paginated R2 list), roots (leases: active = renewed within 30d; unparseable is a gate), mark (iterative BFS over References, visited cap 100k paths, one narinfo read per visit asserted), gates (sweep fraction >0.25, unreadable/unparseable root, budget exhaustion, truncated inventory or leases, corrupt meta/generation; any trip aborts and reports), sweep (unmarked AND older than 14d grace), delete narinfos before NARs in bounded batches (NEVER-DANGLE holds at every instant), bump meta/generation, write gc-runs artifacts + gc-reports report, reap `uploads/` older than 7 days. Armed/grace/retention are vars with production defaults so staging can zero grace for the smoke test without backdating R2 timestamps.

## Storage layout

R2 keys: `{hash32}.narinfo`, `nar/{hash52}.nar[.xz|.zst|.bz2|.gz|.br|.lzip|.lz4]` (reads suffix-agnostic; signing path accepts only `""` and `.zst` in v1), `meta/generation`, `roots/{project}`, `uploads/{uploadId}`, `gc-runs/{runId}/…`, `gc-reports/{runId}.json`. Internal prefixes are unreachable from requests by construction and refused a second time by the sweep candidate filter. KV keys: `oauth-state/{state}` (600s, consumed on use), `sess/{id}` (12h), `ghverdict/{sha256}` (600s/60s). Tokens themselves are never persisted server-side beyond their digest.

Edge caching keeps the TS design: generation-scoped synthetic keys (`https://cachet-edge.invalid/g{N}{path}`), 30d immutable positive TTL, 30s negative caching, HEAD bypasses edge cache, objects >512MB stream uncached, GC's generation bump invalidates globally within 60s. Requires a custom domain (Cache API is inert on workers.dev); workers.dev hostname disabled.

## Infra and bootstrap (alchemy-run)

Alchemy v2 (pinned `alchemy@2.0.0-beta.70` + `effect@4.0.0-beta.102`, bumped together), modeled on lynk: root `alchemy.run.ts` Effect-generator stack, pure `infra/{stage,resources,secrets}.ts` modules with unit tests, `tsconfig.alchemy.json` as a CI gate, state via `Cloudflare.state()` with ALCHEMY_LOCAL_STATE=1 fallback, deploy verb `bun alchemy deploy --yes --adopt --stage production`, Secrets Store for CACHET_SIGNING_KEY + GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET (workers get bindings only), vars carry CACHET_ORGS/ADMINS/AUDIENCE/DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF/HOST/GC knobs, custom domain via the `domain` prop, cron binding. Stage grammar: production / staging / dev / dev-<name>; no preview stages.

The wasm seam is **SPIKE T0, ordered before all other work**: `Cloudflare.Worker { main: "<worker-build output>/index.js", bundle: false, assets }` (bundle:false merged Jun 2026, alchemy-run/alchemy-effect#592; additional modules incl. *.wasm are globbed wrangler-style). ## Context

The existing cachet (`/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet`) is a working TypeScript Cloudflare Worker that serves as an org-wide nix binary cache, with `cachet-action` as its only writer. It works but carries platform-accident complexity, a documented trust regression (the signing key leaked into the worker environment via Infisical), a GC that has never deleted anything (SWEEP_ARMED=false), a multi-tenancy hole in lease renewal, and 471 lines of fragile login shell. The rewrite target `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/nox/cachet` is an empty git repo (PROSE.md already copied in from sesame). The goal: anyone can clone the repo, run one bootstrap flow, and get an org-scoped, authenticated nix binary cache in their own Cloudflare account, with a login UI, a device-flow CLI for laptops, and OIDC-authenticated CI pushes. Reference repos: `nox/sesame` (project hygiene), `nox/lynk` (alchemy-run orchestration). PROSE.md is binding law for all prose the repo ships.

## Locked decisions (from user)

The decisions below are final; everything else in this plan follows from them.

- Auth is GitHub only: browser OAuth for the UI, GitHub device flow for the CLI, GitHub OIDC for CI. No magic link, no passwords, no infisical, no Postgres, no sesame-as-IdP.
- One deployment serves exactly one configured GitHub org (CACHET_ORGS comma list). Nobody outside the org can authenticate at all.
- Signing is server-side: the worker holds a per-deployment ed25519 key (generated at bootstrap, Cloudflare Secrets Store). The user verified the FlakeHub Cache pattern (GitHub OIDC authenticates CI, the service signs) and it is feasible; poison resistance lives in write-path hash verification, not in a reproducibility verifier, which is dropped entirely.
- Laptops are read-only. Writes are OIDC-only. `POST /roots/{project}` requires project == hyphenated `repository` claim (closes the old lease-clobbering hole) plus ref == CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF.
- UI is minimal SSR in v1 (landing, login, instruction page); a separate SPA comes later. Hard requirement now: OpenAPI-first (`docs/openapi.yaml` authored before handlers, served at /api/openapi.json, drift-locked by a golden test) and RFC 9457 problem+json errors.
- No DST/sim harness. Lanes are exactly: unit, property (hegel), golden, kani, workerd, live-smoke. Gates: fmt, clippy, deny, doc-manifest, lane-manifest, actionlint, scripts, wasm-hygiene, alchemy-types.
- GC is armed from day one. The old collector never swept; this one ships armed, gated, and cursor-resumable.
- Store: R2 only for cache data (ported layout), KV only for sessions/verdicts/oauth-state. No D1.

## Crate DAG

Workspace resolver 2, `[lints] workspace = true`, publish=false version 0.0.1, Apache-2.0, exact toolchain pin (1.95.0, wasm32-unknown-unknown + four native triples). Direction is one-way; path deps only.

| Crate | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `cachet-core` | Pure domain: narinfo grammar and canonical serialization, store-path/NAR key validation, nix base32, lease/generation/upload-record documents, multipart part-plan math, GC mark/sweep/gates/plan over injected callbacks, OIDC claim policy, verdict policy, error-code table. | `cachet-crypto` | Pure computation: sha2, ed25519-dalek (sign/verify/keygen), narinfo fingerprint, RS256 verify (WebCrypto via web_sys or pure-rust rsa+sha2; SPIKE decides), ruzstd streaming decode. Kani proofs colocated. |
| `cachet-api` | HTTP surface bound to `docs/openapi.yaml`: routes derive from operations, problem+json from spec components, spec bytes served verbatim, SSR page. |

## Security deliverables

`docs/security/threat-model.md` covers ten scenarios, each written as attacker → defending mechanism → the lane/test that enforces it: external stranger poisoning (OIDC+org pinning), stolen user token (read-only scope + verdict TTL), forged/mis-scoped OIDC (RS256 pin, exact aud, project binding), forged signatures (Secrets Store custody, sign-only-after-verify typestate), tampered R2 bytes (hash-verified write pipeline), session theft (cookie flags, TTL, no tokens in logs; log-hygiene test), laptop token exfiltration (0600 file, GitHub revocation, TTL), GC as deletion vector (lease binding, gates), supply chain (cargo deny, pins, dependabot, wasm-hygiene), signing-key extraction (never readable back, rotate via dual trusted-public-key window). Plus subsections: upload-id bearer semantics, JWKS stale-fallback reasoning, OAuth state single-use. Root SECURITY.md: disclosure channel, scope, supported versions.

## Docs layout

Root: README.md, CLAUDE.md (constitution + @-import manifest), SECURITY.md, PROSE.md (verbatim), LICENSE. docs/: contracts.md, DEPLOY.md, operations.md, openapi.yaml, design/{architecture,worker,signing,auth,gc,cli,action,bootstrap,wire-formats}.md, security/threat-model.md, testing/{lanes.toml + unit,property,golden,kani,workerd,live-smoke}.md, adr/0001-0022.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On a fresh Cloudflare account, `just bootstrap` produces a serving cache on a custom domain with no console steps beyond the printed checklists.
2. A laptop runs `cachet login --url` + `cachet setup`; a nix build substitutes from the deployment with signature verification on.
3. The action pushes from an org repo; an out-of-org repo and a mis-scoped audience are refused with the documented codes; pushes unsigned, arrives signed, `nix store verify --sigs-needed 1` passes with only the deployment public key.
4. Narinfo writes refuse hash-mismatched documents with the 400 codes in openapi.yaml; every rejection-matrix entry is spec'd and workerd-tested.
5. GC runs armed in staging; a zeroed-grace run deletes only unmarked grace-expired objects narinfo-first, bumps generation, writes run + report artifacts; every gate trip has a test.
6. All lanes/gates green; wasm bundle free of ring/aws-lc/tokio symbols and secret strings; both manifest bijections green.
7. /api/openapi.json validates and is byte-equal to docs/openapi.yaml rendered; all error bodies RFC 9457.
8. Each of the ten threat-model scenarios names a passing mechanical check.
9. A tag publishes the four-triple `cachet` binary via cargo-dist; the action consumes exactly that artifact.
10. Live smoke: 126 MiB round trip through push + pull-verify on staging, GC armed; T2 CPU numbers recorded in ADR-0022.

Out of v1 scope: reproducibility verifier, SPA, D1 or any database, per-user accounts, S3 emulation, laptop push in the normal path, preview stages, Cloudflare Workflows, upstream write-through proxying (clients keep cache.nixos.org as their second substituter; no server-side upstream fetch).

## Migration note

Key grammar and narinfo semantics are unchanged, so an existing deployment cuts over by redeploying against the same bucket and domain. Old narinfos keep client-signed Sig lines and stay valid; the trusted key set during transition includes both the old cache key and the new deployment key. Old roots/leases carry forward as-is; the first armed GC run is the first deletion a TS-cachet bucket has ever seen, so its gates matter.

## Context

The existing cachet (`/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet`) is a working TypeScript Cloudflare Worker that serves as an org-wide nix binary cache, with `cachet-action` as its only writer. It works but carries platform-accident complexity, a documented trust regression (the signing key leaked into the worker environment via Infisical), a GC that has never deleted anything (SWEEP_ARMED=false), a multi-tenancy hole in lease renewal, and 471 lines of fragile login shell. The rewrite target `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/nox/cachet` is an empty git repo (PROSE.md already copied in from sesame). The goal: anyone can clone the repo, run one bootstrap flow, and get an org-scoped, authenticated nix binary cache in their own Cloudflare account, with a login UI, a device-flow CLI for laptops, and OIDC-authenticated CI pushes. Reference repos: `nox/sesame` (project hygiene), `nox/lynk` (alchemy-run orchestration). PROSE.md is binding law for all prose the repo ships.

## Locked decisions (from user)

The decisions below are final; everything else in this plan follows from them.

- Auth is GitHub only: browser OAuth for the UI, GitHub device flow for the CLI, GitHub OIDC for CI. No magic link, no passwords, no infisical, no Postgres, no sesame-as-IdP.
- One deployment serves exactly one configured GitHub org (CACHET_ORGS comma list). Nobody outside the org can authenticate at all.
- Signing is server-side: the worker holds a per-deployment ed25519 key (generated at bootstrap, Cloudflare Secrets Store). The user verified the FlakeHub Cache pattern (GitHub OIDC authenticates CI, the service signs) and it is feasible; poison resistance lives in write-path hash verification, not in a reproducibility verifier, which is dropped entirely.
- Laptops are read-only. Writes are OIDC-only. `POST /roots/{project}` requires project == hyphenated `repository` claim (closes the old lease-clobbering hole) plus ref == CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF.
- UI is minimal SSR in v1 (landing, login, instruction page); a separate SPA comes later. Hard requirement now: OpenAPI-first (`docs/openapi.yaml` authored before handlers, served at /api/openapi.json, drift-locked by a golden test) and RFC 9457 problem+json errors.
- No DST/sim harness. Lanes are exactly: unit, property (hegel), golden, kani, workerd, live-smoke. Gates: fmt, clippy, deny, doc-manifest, lane-manifest, actionlint, scripts, wasm-hygiene, alchemy-types.
- GC is armed from day one. The old collector never swept; this one ships armed, gated, and cursor-resumable.
- Store: R2 only for cache data (ported layout), KV only for sessions/verdicts/oauth-state. No D1.

## Crate DAG

Workspace resolver 2, `[lints] workspace = true`, publish=false version 0.0.1, Apache-2.0, exact toolchain pin (1.95.0, wasm32-unknown-unknown + four native triples). Direction is one-way; path deps only.

| Crate | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `cachet-core` | Pure domain: narinfo grammar and canonical serialization, store-path/NAR key validation, nix base32, lease/generation/upload-record documents, multipart part-plan math, GC mark/sweep/gates/plan over injected callbacks, OIDC claim policy, verdict policy, error-code table. Clock/Rng traits defined here, no I/O, no ambient entropy. |
| `cachet-crypto` | Pure computation: sha2, ed25519-dalek (sign/verify/keygen), narinfo fingerprint, RS256 verify (WebCrypto via web_sys or pure-rust rsa+sha2; SPIKE decides), ruzstd streaming decode. Kani proofs colocated. |
| `cachet-api` | HTTP surface bound to `docs/openapi.yaml`: routes derive from operations, problem+json from spec components, spec bytes served verbatim, SSR page. |
| `cachet-worker` | Deployable leaf: `#[event(fetch)]` + `#[event(scheduled)]`, R2/KV/Cache/GitHub adapters, per-isolate JWKS cache, signing pipeline over streams, GC driver. The only crate with `worker` deps and getrandom/js. |
| `cachet-push` | Push pipeline as a native library: snapshot/diff, upstream filter at concurrency 16, `nix copy --to file://?compression=zstd` staging (unsigned), NARs-before-narinfos upload with fresh OIDC per request, lease renewal, never-fail-the-job semantics. nix-archive, nix-derivation, nix-flake-lock live here (native only). |
| `cachet-cli` | The `cachet` binary (clap): `login` (device flow), `setup` (managed nix.conf block + netrc), `push [--dry-run]`, `keygen`, `doctor` (401-vs-404 probe). reqwest+rustls. Released by cargo-dist for four triples. |

nix-flake-lock's concrete job: during push, parse the repo's flake.lock, record the pinned root revision in lease metadata (UI display), and validate the follows-graph. nix-derivation parses .drv/store paths client-side. nix-archive verifies/encodes NARs client-side; it cannot go to wasm (libc+rustix unconditional deps) and is not needed there because the worker computes hashes over bytes, which sha2+ruzstd cover; upstreaming a unix-feature gate is a nice-to-have spike, not a blocker.

## Auth flows

Check order on every route, ported from the TS worker: key validation, config validation, authorization, body/shape guards, work. Malformed key is 400 before any credential read; unauthenticated write is 401 before any 411.

1. Browser OAuth: `GET /_auth/login` writes `oauth-state/{state}` (KV, 600s, single-use) and 302s to github.com (scope `read:org read:user`, deployment client id). `/_auth/callback` exchanges the code with the server-held client secret, checks `GET /user` + org membership, mints a 128-bit session id, writes `sess/{id}` (KV, 12h), sets `cachet_session=…; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`. `/api/self/*` also requires login ∈ CACHET_ADMINS.

P10 security + docs: threat-model.md, SECURITY.md, all ADRs, final CLAUDE.md, README, PROSE pass.

0001 R2-only storage, no database (carried). 0002 Writes through the worker; custom multipart (64MiB parts, 1000-part cap, 94371800-byte single cap, x-cachet-upload-bytes). 0003 Server-side signing; write-path hash verification is poison resistance. 0004 GitHub-only auth (OAuth + device + OIDC); no shared read tokens, no Infisical. 0005 KV for auth state only. 0006 Pure-rust/WebCrypto on wasm; ring/aws-lc/zstd-C banned with the wasm-hygiene gate. 0007 workers-rs; port contracts, not code. 0008 alchemy IaC, stage grammar, bundle:false seam + wrangler fallback. 0009 cargo-dist releases; action wraps the released binary. 0010 Server canonicalizes and signs narinfos after verification. 0011 GC armed from day one; cursor-resumable cron driver. 0012 Edge-cache generation (carried). 0013 Deployment identity is configuration; key name `{host}-1`. 0014 RFC 9457 problem+json; error table extended, old codes byte-stable. 0015 OpenAPI-first: spec is source of truth, served bytes golden-locked. 0016 The flake is the interface; just verbs are CI parity. 0017 project == repository claim (hole fix). 0018 Verdict-cache TTLs = revocation window. 0019 Laptops read-only; push lives in CLI + action. 0020 Upstream filter + file:// staging (carried). 0021 Signing-key custody: Secrets Store, rotate-by-redeploy, bootstrap env file 0600+gitignored. 0022 CPU budget for hash verification (records T2 measurements).

`docs/security/threat-model.md` covers ten scenarios, each written as attacker → defending mechanism → the lane/test that enforces it: external stranger poisoning (OIDC+org pinning), stolen user token (read-only scope + verdict TTL), forged/mis-scoped OIDC (RS256 pin, exact aud, project binding), forged signatures (Secrets Store custody, sign-only-after-verify typestate), tampered R2 bytes (hash-verified write pipeline), session theft (cookie flags, TTL, no tokens in logs; log-hygiene test), laptop token exfiltration (0600 file, GitHub revocation, TTL), GC as deletion vector (lease binding, gates), supply chain (cargo deny, pins, dependabot, wasm-hygiene), signing-key extraction (never readable back, rotate via dual trusted-public-key window). ## Docs layout

Root: README.md, CLAUDE.md (constitution + @-import manifest), SECURITY.md, PROSE.md (verbatim), LICENSE. docs/: contracts.md, DEPLOY.md, operations.md, openapi.yaml, design/{architecture,worker,signing,auth,gc,cli,action,bootstrap,wire-formats}.md, security/threat-model.md, testing/{lanes.toml + unit,property,golden,kani,workerd,live-smoke}.md, adr/0001-0022.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On a fresh Cloudflare account, `just bootstrap` produces a serving cache on a custom domain with no console steps beyond the printed checklists.
2. A laptop runs `cachet login --url` + `cachet setup`; a nix build substitutes from the deployment with signature verification on.
3. The action pushes from an org repo; an out-of-org repo and a mis-scoped audience are refused with the documented codes; pushes unsigned, arrives signed, `nix store verify --sigs-needed 1` passes with only the deployment public key.
4. Narinfo writes refuse hash-mismatched documents with the 400 codes in openapi.yaml; every rejection-matrix entry is spec'd and workerd-tested.
5. GC runs armed in staging; a zeroed-grace run deletes only unmarked grace-expired objects narinfo-first, bumps generation, writes run + report artifacts; every gate trip has a test.
6. All lanes/gates green; wasm bundle free of ring/aws-lc/tokio symbols and secret strings; both manifest bijections green.
7. /api/openapi.json validates and is byte-equal to docs/openapi.yaml rendered; all error bodies RFC 9457.
8. Each of the ten threat-model scenarios names a passing mechanical check.
9. A tag publishes the four-triple `cachet` binary via cargo-dist; the action consumes exactly that artifact.
10. Live smoke: 126 MiB round trip through push + pull-verify on staging, GC armed; T2 CPU numbers recorded in ADR-0022.

Out of v1 scope: reproducibility verifier, SPA, D1 or any database, per-user accounts, S3 emulation, laptop push in the normal path, preview stages, Cloudflare Workflows, upstream write-through proxying (clients keep cache.nixos.org as their second substituter; no server-side upstream fetch).

## Migration note

Key grammar and narinfo semantics are unchanged, so an existing deployment cuts over by redeploying against the same bucket and domain. Old narinfos keep client-signed Sig lines and stay valid; the trusted key set during transition includes both the old cache key and the new deployment key. Old roots/leases carry forward as-is; the first armed GC run is the first deletion a TS-cachet bucket has ever seen, so its gates matter.

- `cachet login --url` on headless machines: device flow already covers it; confirm verification URI display UX.
- Whether KV verdict caching needs a second namespace per session/verdict (naming decision in infra/resources.ts).

# cachet v1: self-hosted nix binary cache, Rust on Cloudflare Workers

## Context

The existing cachet (TypeScript on Cloudflare Workers, plus its GitHub Action) is a working org-wide nix binary cache. It carries platform-accident complexity, a documented signing-key trust regression, a GC that has never deleted anything, a lease-clobbering hole, and 471 lines of login shell. The rewrite target is a fresh git repo (currently holding only a copied PROSE.md, which is binding law for all prose the repo ships). The goal: anyone clones the repo, runs one bootstrap flow, and gets an org-scoped, authenticated nix binary cache in their own Cloudflare account. CI pushes sign server-side; laptops authenticate by GitHub device flow; the whole repo is OSS under Apache-2.0 including the GitHub Action. No repo artifact (code, comments, docs, ADRs) references the internal template projects; conventions are copied, never cited.

## Locked decisions (from user)

- Auth is GitHub only. CI: OIDC. Humans on laptops: GitHub device flow. No magic link, no passwords, no external secrets manager, no database.
- One deployment serves exactly one configured GitHub org (CACHET_ORGS comma list). Nobody outside the org can authenticate at all.
- Signing is server-side. The worker holds a per-deployment ed25519 key in Cloudflare Secrets Store, generated at bootstrap. This matches how FlakeHub Cache authenticates CI (GitHub OIDC) while the service owns signing; poison resistance lives in write-path hash verification.
- Laptops are read-only. Writes are OIDC-only. `POST /roots/{project}` requires project == hyphenated `repository` claim plus ref == CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF.
- v1 ships the backend only. No pages, no browser OAuth, no sessions. The SPA comes later as its own phase; v1 already serves every endpoint the SPA will need (public config, stats, projects, GC reports). The CLI prints the nix.conf snippet itself, sourced from /api/public/config.
- OpenAPI: the code is the source of truth. Route handlers in `cachet-api` carry utoipa derive macros; `just openapi` regenerates the committed `docs/openapi.yaml` from the code and CI fails on drift; the worker serves the committed bytes at /api/openapi.json (served == generated, golden test). No code generation from the spec, ever.
- Error bodies are RFC 9457 problem+json; the old code → status table is preserved exactly and only extended.
- The GitHub Action lives in this repo under `action/` (composite wrapper + nested node24 post action), consuming the `cachet` binary from this repo's own GitHub Releases. Consumers use `<org>/cachet/action@v1`.
- GC is armed from day one, runs entirely inside Cloudflare (cron trigger in the same worker, cursor-resumable across invocations), and every run emits report objects that the API serves; the later SPA renders them.
- No DST/sim harness. Lanes: unit, property (hegel), golden, kani, workerd, integration. Gates: fmt, clippy, deny, doc-manifest, lane-manifest, actionlint, scripts, wasm-hygiene, openapi-drift.
- Store: R2 for cache data (ported key layout), one KV namespace for token-validation verdicts only. No D1.

## Crate DAG

Workspace resolver 2, `[lints] workspace = true`, publish=false version 0.0.1, Apache-2.0, exact toolchain pin (wasm32-unknown-unknown + four native triples). Direction is one-way; path deps only.

| Crate | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `cachet-core` | Pure domain: narinfo grammar and canonical serialization, store-path/NAR key validation, nix base32, lease/generation/upload-record documents, multipart part-plan math, GC mark/sweep/gates/plan over injected callbacks, OIDC claim policy, GitHub-token verdict policy, error-code table. Clock/Rng traits defined here; no I/O, no ambient entropy. |
| `cachet-crypto` | Pure computation: sha2, ed25519-dalek (sign/verify/keygen), narinfo fingerprint, RS256 verify (WebCrypto via web_sys or pure-rust rsa+sha2; a spike decides), ruzstd streaming decode. Kani proofs colocated. |
| `cachet-api` | HTTP surface as typed route handlers with utoipa derive macros: the OpenAPI YAML is generated from this code, and problem+json bodies come from the shared error taxonomy. No SSR. |
| `cachet-worker` | Deployable leaf: `#[event(fetch)]` + `#[event(scheduled)]`, R2/KV/Cache/GitHub adapters, per-isolate JWKS cache, signing pipeline over streams, GC driver. The only crate with `worker` deps and getrandom/js. |
| `cachet-push` | Push pipeline as a native library: snapshot/diff, upstream filter at concurrency 16, `nix copy --to file://?compression=zstd` staging (unsigned), NARs-before-narinfos upload with fresh OIDC per request, lease renewal, never-fail-the-job semantics. nix-archive, nix-derivation, nix-flake-lock live here (native targets only). |
| `cachet-cli` | The `cachet` binary (clap): `login` (device flow), `setup` (managed nix.conf block + netrc), `push [--dry-run]`, `keygen`, `doctor` (401-vs-404 probe). reqwest+rustls. Released by cargo-dist for four triples. |

nix-flake-lock's concrete job: during push, parse the repo's flake.lock, record the pinned root revision in lease metadata (surfaced later in the SPA), and validate the follows-graph. nix-derivation parses .drv and store paths client-side. nix-archive verifies/encodes NARs client-side; it cannot go to wasm (unconditional libc+rustix deps) and the worker does not need it because verification hashes bytes with sha2+ruzstd. Upstreaming a unix-feature gate is an optional spike, not a blocker.

## Auth flows (v1: two, both UI-free)

Check order on every route, ported from the previous worker: key validation, config validation, authorization, body/shape guards, work. Malformed key is 400 before any credential read; unauthenticated write is 401 before any 411.

1. GitHub OIDC (the only write credential): RS256 pinned by policy, JWKS per-isolate cache (10-minute TTL, one refetch on unknown kid, stale fallback, 503 `auth_unavailable` when cold), `iss`/`aud` exact (aud arrays refused), `repository_owner` ∈ CACHET_ORGS, required claims `exp,iat,aud,iss,repository,repository_owner,ref`, times against the injected clock. Lease renewal additionally requires ref == CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF (403 forbidden_ref) and project == hyphenated repository claim (403 forbidden_project, new code).
2. Device-flow GitHub token (read, laptops and admins): `cachet login --url <url>` GETs unauthenticated `/api/public/config` (`{oauthClientId, orgs, host, publicKey}`), runs github.com's device endpoints directly, stores the GitHub user token 0600 under `~/.config/cachet/`. The worker never participates in the flow. On each request: sha256 the presented token, look up `ghverdict/` KV (600s allow / 60s deny), on miss call `GET /user` + org membership against the GitHub API, cache the verdict. Verdict TTL is the documented revocation window. Admin requests (under /api/self/) additionally require the login ∈ CACHET_ADMINS, where the login comes from the validated verdict.

Deferred to the SPA phase (designed now, built later): browser OAuth code flow, sessions KV keys, login/logout routes. The ADRs record the design so the SPA lands without re-litigation.

## Signing pipeline

Narinfo PUT after validation, auth, and 411/413 guards. Verify-then-sign is enforced by construction: the signing function takes a `VerifiedNar` newtype only the verifier constructs. Wire hash format is nix base32 with `sha256:` prefix. The signature input is the nix fingerprint `"1;<storePath>;<narHash>;<narSize>;<refs joined by ,>"`, signed directly with ed25519 (no outer hash). Appended line: `Sig: {CACHET_HOST}-1:<base64>`; pre-existing Sig lines are preserved. Steps: parse (total, 400), required StorePath/URL/NarHash/NarSize present, StorePath hash == URL key (400), suffix ∈ {"", ".zst"} (400 unsupported_compression), bucket.head(URL) exists (409 narinfo_nar_missing), stream the stored NAR through tee(compressed-sha256, ruzstd → nar-sha256 + byte count), NarSize == decompressed count (bomb guard), NarHash/NarSize agreement (400 nar_hash_mismatch), FileHash/FileSize agreement when present (400 file_hash_mismatch), compressed sha256 == hash named in the NAR key, canonicalize preserving unknown fields, append Sig, bucket.put, 204. This path hashes multi-hundred-MiB objects, so deployments require a paid plan (`cpu_ms = 300000`, recorded in DEPLOY.md). A spike measures ruzstd+sha2 throughput under workerd and lands the number in the CPU-budget ADR.

## GC (inside Cloudflare, reportable)

Cron binding on the same worker (`0 5 * * *`; staging configurable). One invocation has a wall-clock budget of 13 minutes and a binding-op budget of 900; the driver persists a cursor document at each stage boundary and exits cleanly within a named headroom, resuming on the next cron tick, so caches of any size sweep inside Cloudflare without an external runner. Stages: inventory (paginated R2 list), roots (leases active when renewed within 30 days; unparseable lease is a gate), mark (iterative BFS over narinfo References, visited cap 100k paths, one read per visit asserted), gates (sweep fraction > 0.25, unreadable or unparseable root, budget exhaustion, truncated inventory or leases, corrupt meta/generation; any trip aborts the run and writes the report), sweep (unmarked AND older than 14-day grace), delete narinfos before NARs in bounded batches so NEVER-DANGLE holds at every instant, bump meta/generation, write `gc-runs/{runId}/` stage artifacts and `gc-reports/{runId}.json`, reap stale `uploads/` older than 7 days. Armed/grace/retention are vars with production defaults; staging zeroes grace for the integration lane without backdating R2 timestamps.

UI-reportability: runs and reports are first-class API data. `/api/self/gc-runs` (paginated run list) and `/api/self/gc-runs/{runId}` (full report: stages, gates, counts, durations, deletions) serve the same `gc-reports/` objects the driver writes, so the later SPA renders history without touching R2 directly. `/api/self/stats` derives current cache totals from the latest report.

## Storage layout

R2 keys: `{hash32}.narinfo`, `nar/{hash52}.nar[.xz|.zst|.bz2|.gz|.br|.lzip|.lz4]` (reads suffix-agnostic; signing accepts only `""` and `.zst` in v1), `meta/generation`, `roots/{project}`, `uploads/{uploadId}`, `gc-runs/{runId}/…`, `gc-reports/{runId}.json`. Internal prefixes are unreachable from requests by construction and refused a second time by the sweep candidate filter. KV keys: `ghverdict/{sha256}` (600s allow / 60s deny). Tokens are never persisted beyond their digest.

Edge caching keeps the previous design: generation-scoped synthetic keys (`https://cachet-edge.invalid/g{N}{path}`), 30-day immutable positive TTL, 30s negative caching, HEAD bypasses edge cache, objects > 512 MB stream uncached, the GC generation bump invalidates globally within 60s. Requires a custom domain (Cache API is inert on workers.dev); workers.dev hostname disabled.

## Infra and bootstrap (alchemy)

Alchemy v2 (exact pins for alchemy + effect, bumped together). Root `alchemy.run.ts` Effect-generator stack, pure `infra/{stage,resources,secrets}.ts` modules with unit tests, `tsconfig.alchemy.json` typechecked as a CI gate, state via `Cloudflare.state()` with ALCHEMY_LOCAL_STATE=1 fallback, deploy verb `bun alchemy deploy --yes --adopt --stage production`. Secrets Store holds CACHET_SIGNING_KEY and GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET (workers receive bindings only). # cachet v1: self-hosted nix binary cache, Rust on Cloudflare Workers

## Context

The existing cachet (TypeScript on Cloudflare Workers, plus its GitHub Action) is a working org-wide nix binary cache. It carries platform-accident complexity, a documented signing-key trust regression, a GC that has never deleted anything, a lease-clobbering hole, and 471 lines of login shell. The rewrite target is a fresh git repo (currently holding only a copied PROSE.md, which is binding law for all prose the repo ships). The goal: anyone clones the repo, runs one bootstrap flow, and gets an org-scoped, authenticated nix binary cache in their own Cloudflare account. CI pushes sign server-side; laptops authenticate by GitHub device flow; the whole repo is OSS under Apache-2.0 including the GitHub Action. No repo artifact (code, comments, docs, ADRs) references the internal template projects; conventions are copied, never cited.

## Locked decisions (from user)

- Auth is GitHub only. CI: OIDC. Humans on laptops: GitHub device flow. No magic link, no passwords, no external secrets manager, no database.
- One deployment serves exactly one configured GitHub org (CACHET_ORGS comma list). Nobody outside the org can authenticate at all.
- Signing is server-side. The worker holds a per-deployment ed25519 key in Cloudflare Secrets Store, generated at bootstrap. This matches how FlakeHub Cache authenticates CI (GitHub OIDC) while the service owns signing; poison resistance lives in write-path hash verification.
- Laptops are read-only. Writes are OIDC-only. `POST /roots/{project}` requires project == hyphenated `repository` claim plus ref == CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF.
- v1 ships the backend only. No pages, no browser OAuth, no sessions. The SPA comes later as its own phase; v1 already serves every endpoint the SPA will need (public config, stats, projects, GC reports). The CLI prints the nix.conf snippet itself, sourced from /api/public/config.
- OpenAPI: the code is the source of truth. Route handlers in `cachet-api` carry utoipa derive macros; `just openapi` regenerates the committed `docs/openapi.yaml` from the code and CI fails on drift; the worker serves the committed bytes at /api/openapi.json (served == generated, golden test). No code generation from the spec, ever.
- Error bodies are RFC 9457 problem+json; the old code → status table is preserved exactly and only extended.
- The GitHub Action lives in this repo under `action/` (composite wrapper + nested node24 post action), consuming the `cachet` binary from this repo's own GitHub Releases. Consumers use `<org>/cachet/action@v1`.
- GC is armed from day one, runs entirely inside Cloudflare (cron trigger in the same worker, cursor-resumable across invocations), and every run emits report objects that the API serves; the later SPA renders them.
- No DST/sim harness. Lanes: unit, property (hegel), golden, kani, workerd, integration. Gates: fmt, clippy, deny, doc-manifest, lane-manifest, actionlint, scripts, wasm-hygiene, openapi-drift.
- Store: R2 for cache data (ported key layout), one KV namespace for token-validation verdicts only. No D1.

## Crate DAG

Workspace resolver 2, `[lints] workspace = true`, publish=false version 0.0.1, Apache-2.0, exact toolchain pin (wasm32-unknown-unknown + four native triples). Direction is one-way; path deps only.

| Crate | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `cachet-core` | Pure domain: narinfo grammar and canonical serialization, store-path/NAR key validation, nix base32, lease/generation/upload-record documents, multipart part-plan math, GC mark/sweep/gates/plan over injected callbacks, OIDC claim policy, GitHub-token verdict policy, error-code table. Clock/Rng traits defined here; no I/O, no ambient entropy. |
| `cachet-crypto` | Pure computation: sha2, ed25519-dalek (sign/verify/keygen), narinfo fingerprint, RS256 verify (WebCrypto via web_sys or pure-rust rsa+sha2; a spike decides), ruzstd streaming decode. Kani proofs colocated. |
| `cachet-api` | HTTP surface as typed route handlers with utoipa derive macros: the OpenAPI YAML is generated from this code, and problem+json bodies come from the shared error taxonomy. No SSR. |
| `cachet-worker` | Deployable leaf: `#[event(fetch)]` + `#[event(scheduled)]`, R2/KV/Cache/GitHub adapters, per-isolate JWKS cache, signing pipeline over streams, GC driver. The only crate with `worker` deps and getrandom/js. |
| `cachet-push` | Push pipeline as a native library: snapshot/diff, upstream filter at concurrency 16, `nix copy --to file://?compression=zstd` staging (unsigned), NARs-before-narinfos upload with fresh OIDC per request, lease renewal, never-fail-the-job semantics. nix-archive, nix-derivation, nix-flake-lock live here (native targets only). |
| `cachet-cli` | The `cachet` binary (clap): `login` (device flow), `setup` (managed nix.conf block + netrc), `push [--dry-run]`, `keygen`, `doctor` (401-vs-404 probe). reqwest+rustls. Released by cargo-dist for four triples. |

nix-flake-lock's concrete job: during push, parse the repo's flake.lock, record the pinned root revision in lease metadata (surfaced later in the SPA), and validate the follows-graph. nix-derivation parses .drv and store paths client-side. nix-archive verifies/encodes NARs client-side; it cannot go to wasm (unconditional libc+rustix deps) and the worker does not need it because verification hashes bytes with sha2+ruzstd. ## Security deliverables

`docs/security/threat-model.md` covers ten scenarios, each written as attacker → defending mechanism → the lane or test that enforces it: external stranger poisoning (OIDC + org pinning), stolen user token (read-only scope + verdict TTL), forged or mis-scoped OIDC (RS256 pin, exact aud, project binding), forged signatures (Secrets Store custody, sign-only-after-verify typestate), tampered R2 bytes (hash-verified write pipeline), token exfiltration from a laptop disk (0600 file, GitHub revocation, verdict TTL), log exfiltration (logs carry no credential fields; log-hygiene test scans emitted lines), GC as a deletion vector (lease binding, gates, grace window), supply chain (cargo deny, exact pins, dependabot, wasm-hygiene scan), signing-key extraction (Secrets Store never readable back; rotation via a dual trusted-public-key window). Subsections for upload-id bearer semantics and JWKS stale-fallback reasoning. Root SECURITY.md: disclosure channel, scope, supported versions.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On a fresh Cloudflare account, `just bootstrap` produces a serving cache on a custom domain with no console steps beyond the printed checklists.
2. A laptop runs `cachet login --url` + `cachet setup`; a nix build substitutes from the deployment with signature verification on.
3. The in-repo action pushes from an org repo; an out-of-org repo and a mis-scoped audience are refused with the documented codes; pushes arrive unsigned, are stored signed, and `nix store verify --sigs-needed 1` passes with only the deployment public key.
4. Narinfo writes refuse hash-mismatched documents with the 400 codes in the spec; every rejection-matrix entry is generated into the spec and workerd-tested.
5. GC runs armed in staging on the Cloudflare cron; a zeroed-grace run deletes only unmarked grace-expired objects narinfo-first, bumps generation, and its reports are served by the API; every gate trip has a test.
6. All lanes and gates green; the wasm bundle free of ring/aws-lc/tokio symbols and secret-shaped strings; both manifest bijections green; `just openapi --check` clean.
7. /api/openapi.json validates and is byte-equal to the committed generated yaml; all error bodies RFC 9457.
8. Each of the ten threat-model scenarios names a passing mechanical check.
9. A tag publishes the four-triple `cachet` binary via cargo-dist; `action/` consumes exactly that artifact.
10. Integration lane on staging: the 126 MiB round trip through push and pull-verify passes with GC armed; the throughput measurement lands in ADR-0022.

Out of v1 scope: any UI, browser OAuth and sessions, the reproducibility verifier, D1 or any database, per-user accounts, S3 emulation, laptop push in the normal path, preview stages, Cloudflare Workflows, upstream write-through proxying (clients keep cache.nixos.org as a second substituter).

## Migration note

Key grammar and narinfo semantics are unchanged, so an existing deployment cuts over by redeploying against the same bucket and domain. Old narinfos keep their client-signed Sig lines and stay valid; laptop configs trust both the old key and the new deployment key during transition. Leases carry forward as-is; the first armed GC run is the first deletion such a bucket has ever seen, so its gates matter.
