# The workerd lane

The workerd lane runs the built worker bundle under `wrangler dev --local`,
which is miniflare over the real workerd binary: R2, KV, the Cache API,
waitUntil draining, and the module-pipeline semantics are the runtime's
own rather than a mock's. Assertions reach the worker over real HTTP from
`workerd/check.mjs`, a node script with no npm dependencies (the
devshell's node 22 supplies fetch and child_process).

Each scenario gets its own persistence directory: the driver seeds the
local R2 with `wrangler r2 object put --local`, boots the worker on a
free port, asserts, and kills it. Cache behavior is not observed by
introspecting miniflare internals: the worker emits events
(read.edge_hit, read.bucket_hit, read.miss, generation.document_corrupt)
and the driver matches them in the wrangler log stream, so a cache that
silently never stores surfaces as a failure the way it would in
production.

Outbound calls have the same treatment. The driver runs a stub server
that plays three roles: the OIDC JWKS endpoint, holding a per-run RSA
keypair; the OAuth web endpoint, exchanging one known code for a member
token and one for an outsider token; and the GitHub API endpoints the
verdict path calls (`/user` and org membership), counting hits so the
scenarios can prove the KV verdict cache serves repeat reads. The worker
reaches them through the `CACHET_JWKS_URL`, `CACHET_GITHUB_API_URL`, and
`CACHET_GITHUB_WEB_URL` variables, which the driver passes with
`wrangler dev --var`; auth scenarios mint RS256 tokens against the
stub's private key, so a verification that silently skips would fail the
matrix. The lane's ed25519 signing secret and the OAuth client secret
enter as `.dev.vars`, the same way a deployment's secrets enter as
bindings; the file is written before the write scenarios, deleted when
the lane ends, and gitignored.

The lane covers the read path, the write path, and the API surface so
far: the handshake body and its headers; narinfo and NAR serving with
wire headers; positive and negative edge caching through the
generation-scoped key space; HEAD semantics; problem+json rejections by
shape and by exact bytes; the corrupt-generation bypass; generation-zero
behavior on an empty bucket; the OIDC rejection matrix (wrong org, alg
confusion, staleness, expired tokens); guard ordering (411 before 413,
401 before 411); the verify-then-sign pipeline end to end, from a NAR
upload through a signed narinfo with both signatures and the file facts;
the multipart quartet with its record, part-size enforcement, replay, and
abort; read verdicts cached in KV for both the admit and the deny
direction; lease renewal bound to the token's own claims with
forbidden_ref and forbidden_project refusals; the project listing; the
public config document; and the browser login flow, from the login
redirect's exact parameters through state consumption (a replayed state
never reaches the exchange), the outsider's forbidden_org refusal, the
session cookie's attributes, and logout's session deletion. GC scenarios
join it with the collector.

Run it: `just workerd`.

1	//! The collector's pure algorithm (CLAUDE.md §4): closure walk, gates,
2	//! deletion planning, and the run report. Everything destructive is decided
3	//! here as data, over injected inputs, so every catastrophic shape has a
4	//! test before it has a deployment: the driver in cachet-worker only
5	//! executes what these functions return.
6	//!
7	//! The laws: marked is never swept, reserved keys are never swept, narinfos
8	//! delete before NARs, and any gate trip aborts the run with nothing
9	//! deleted.
10	
11	use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, VecDeque};
12	
13	use crate::constants::{
14	    CLOSURE_WALK_PATHS_MAX, SWEEP_MAX_FRACTION_DENOMINATOR, SWEEP_MAX_FRACTION_NUMERATOR,
15	};
16	use crate::keys::{NarKey, is_reserved_key};
17	use crate::narinfo::Narinfo;
18	use crate::types::{StorePathHash, UnixMillis};
19	
20	/// A gate trip: the run aborts and deletes nothing. Any of these means the
21	/// picture of the cache was untrustworthy in a way that makes deletion
22	/// unsafe, and the report names it so the run is debuggable.
23	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
24	pub enum GateTrip {
25	    /// A root store path whose narinfo could not be read: the walk would
26	    /// see less than one lease protects.
27	    UnreadableRootNarinfo {
28	        /// The root hash that failed to read.
29	        hash: StorePathHash,
30	    },
31	    /// A lease document that will not parse: its protection is unknown.
32	    UnparseableLease {
33	        /// The lease's bucket key.
34	        key: String,
35	    },
36	    /// The R2 listing could not be fully enumerated in this run.
37	    InventoryTruncated,
38	    /// The project lease listing could not be fully enumerated.
39	    LeasesTruncated,
40	    /// The closure walk hit its visited-path cap.
41	    WalkBudgetExhausted {
42	        /// The number of paths visited when the cap tripped.
43	        visited: usize,
44	    },
45	    /// Deleting the candidates would remove more than the configured
46	    /// fraction of the path universe.
47	    SweepFractionExceeded {
48	        /// Candidate narinfo count.
49	        deletions: usize,
50	        /// Total narinfo inventory.
51	        inventory: usize,
52	    },
53	    /// The generation document is corrupt: sweeping without a reliable
54	    /// epoch would leave the edge serving deleted objects.
55	    GenerationCorrupt,
56	}
57	
58	impl core::fmt::Display for GateTrip {
59	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
60	        match self {
61	            Self::UnreadableRootNarinfo { hash } => write!(f, "unreadable root narinfo {hash}"),
62	            Self::UnparseableLease { key } => write!(f, "unparseable lease {key}"),
63	            Self::InventoryTruncated => f.write_str("inventory truncated"),
64	            Self::LeasesTruncated => f.write_str("leases truncated"),
65	            Self::WalkBudgetExhausted { visited } => {
66	                write!(f, "walk budget exhausted at {visited} paths")
67	            }
68	            Self::SweepFractionExceeded {
69	                deletions,
70	                inventory,
71	            } => write!(
72	                f,
73	                "sweep of {deletions}/{inventory} paths exceeds the fraction gate"
74	            ),
75	            Self::GenerationCorrupt => f.write_str("generation document corrupt"),
76	        }
77	    }
78	}
79	
80	impl GateTrip {
81	    /// The stable name the report records: machine-matchable, unlike the
82	    /// Display text, which carries occurrence specifics.
83	    pub const fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
84	        match self {
85	            Self::UnreadableRootNarinfo { .. } => "unreadable_root_narinfo",
86	            Self::UnparseableLease { .. } => "unparseable_lease",
87	            Self::InventoryTruncated => "inventory_truncated",
88	            Self::LeasesTruncated => "leases_truncated",
89	            Self::WalkBudgetExhausted { .. } => "walk_budget_exhausted",
90	            Self::SweepFractionExceeded { .. } => "sweep_fraction_exceeded",
91	            Self::GenerationCorrupt => "generation_corrupt",
92	        }
93	    }
94	}

96	/// Why a narinfo read failed during the walk.
97	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
98	pub enum WalkReadError {
99	    /// The narinfo object is absent (a dangling root or reference).
100	    Absent,
101	    /// The object exists but does not parse.
102	    Unparseable,
103	}
104	
105	/// The pure outcome of the closure walk over one root set.
106	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
107	pub struct WalkOutcome {
108	    /// Every reachable store-path hash.
109	    pub marked: BTreeSet<StorePathHash>,
110	    /// For each readable marked path, the NAR key its narinfo named. The
111	    /// URL set derived from this map is what makes shared-NAR sweeps safe:
112	    /// a NAR survives if any marked narinfo still names it.
113	    pub marked_urls: BTreeMap<StorePathHash, NarKey>,
114	    /// Deep references whose own narinfo could not be read: they are
115	    /// marked without descent and counted for the report.
116	    pub unreadable_deep: usize,
117	    /// The gate a run aborts on, when one tripped.
118	    pub gate: Option<GateTrip>,
119	}
120	
121	/// The closure walk as an incremental state machine: `next` names the
122	/// path whose narinfo must be read, `answer` applies the read. The worker
123	/// awaits one bucket read per step this way, and a run can freeze the
124	/// walker into its cursor and resume the next tick with the visited set,
125	/// the frontier order, and the marks bit-identical.
126	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
127	pub struct ClosureWalker {
128	    roots: BTreeSet<StorePathHash>,
129	    visited: BTreeSet<StorePathHash>,
130	    queue: VecDeque<StorePathHash>,
131	    outcome: WalkOutcome,
132	}

134	impl ClosureWalker {
135	    /// Start a walk from the root set, sorted so the walk order never
136	    /// depends on how the roots arrived.
137	    pub fn new(roots: &[StorePathHash]) -> Self {
138	        let mut walker = Self {

140	            visited: BTreeSet::new(),
141	            queue: VecDeque::new(),
142	            outcome: WalkOutcome::default(),

144	        let mut sorted = roots.to_vec();

146	        walker.queue.extend(sorted);

148	    }

# The workerd lane

The workerd lane runs the built worker bundle under `wrangler dev --local`,
which is miniflare over the real workerd binary: R2, KV, the Cache API,
waitUntil draining, and the module-pipeline semantics are the runtime's
own rather than a mock's. Assertions reach the worker over real HTTP from
`workerd/check.mjs`, a node script with no npm dependencies (the
devshell's node 22 supplies fetch and child_process).

Each scenario gets its own persistence directory: the driver seeds the
local R2 with `wrangler r2 object put --local`, boots the worker on a
free port, asserts, and kills it. Cache behavior is not observed by
introspecting miniflare internals: the worker emits events
(read.edge_hit, read.bucket_hit, read.miss, generation.document_corrupt)
and the driver matches them in the wrangler log stream, so a cache that
silently never stores surfaces as a failure the way it would in
production.

Outbound calls have the same treatment. The driver runs a stub server
that plays three roles: the OIDC JWKS endpoint, holding a per-run RSA
keypair; the OAuth web endpoint, exchanging one known code for a member
token and one for an outsider token; and the GitHub API endpoints the
verdict path calls (`/user` and org membership), counting hits so the
scenarios can prove the KV verdict cache serves repeat reads. The worker
reaches them through the `CACHET_JWKS_URL`, `CACHET_GITHUB_API_URL`, and
`CACHET_GITHUB_WEB_URL` variables, which the driver passes with
`wrangler dev --var`; auth scenarios mint RS256 tokens against the
stub's private key, so a verification that silently skips would fail the
matrix. The lane's ed25519 signing secret and the OAuth client secret
enter as `.dev.vars`, the same way a deployment's secrets enter as
bindings; the file is written before the write scenarios, deleted when
the lane ends, and gitignored.

The lane covers the read path, the write path, and the API surface so
far: the handshake body and its headers; narinfo and NAR serving with
wire headers; positive and negative edge caching through the
generation-scoped key space; HEAD semantics; problem+json rejections by
shape and by exact bytes; the corrupt-generation bypass; generation-zero
behavior on an empty bucket; the OIDC rejection matrix (wrong org, alg
confusion, staleness, expired tokens); guard ordering (411 before 413,
401 before 411); the verify-then-sign pipeline end to end, from a NAR
upload through a signed narinfo with both signatures and the file facts;
the multipart quartet with its record, part-size enforcement, replay, and
abort; read verdicts cached in KV for both the admit and the deny
direction; lease renewal bound to the token's own claims with
forbidden_ref and forbidden_project refusals; the project listing; the
public config document; and the browser login flow, from the login
redirect's exact parameters through state consumption (a replayed state
never reaches the exchange), the outsider's forbidden_org refusal, the
session cookie's attributes, and logout's session deletion. The served
OpenAPI document is asserted byte-identical to the committed one, which is
the served half of the drift bijection (CLAUDE.md §8). GC scenarios join
it with the collector.

Run it: `just workerd`.

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
The GC driver: cron-scheduled, cursor-resumed, gate-aborting

cachet-core's collector now runs over state, not just plans: the
closure walk became ClosureWalker, an incremental machine with
next_read/answer, so the worker awaits one bucket read per path and a
run freezes bit-identical between ticks; sweep_candidates names the
one predicate the planner and the URL collector must agree on; and
the run's documents (GcReport, GcCursor with its mark/collect/sweep
halves) serialize stable and golden-locked, because ticks read each
other's bytes.

cachet-worker gains gc.rs and the scheduled entry point. Each tick
recomputes inventory and leases, then marks, collects candidate URLs,
plans, sweeps, and reports, freezing meta/gc-cursor at every stage
boundary and spending against a 900-operation and 13-minute envelope
in the open. Deletion stays ordered narinfos before NARs at every
instant, batches of 128 per binding call, and the generation bumps
only when deletion happened, exactly once per applied plan. Stale
uploads abort and run artifacts prune inside the remaining budget.
Any gate aborts the run with its report written and the cursor
deleted: exception is enumeration over budget, which trips
inventory_truncated/leases_truncated as the alarm channel rather than
pausing silently every tick.

The lane caught a real substrate defect proving this: R2 list()
returns metadata-only objects, and the leases stage (and the upload
reaper) read bodies that were never there, folding every lease into
unparseable_lease. Both stages now get by key, and the two lane
scenarios run the collector over wrangler's scheduled endpoint with
grace zeroed: a happy sweep with report, artifacts, reap, cursor
removal, and generation bump asserted against the bucket itself, and
the fraction gate aborting wholesale deletion with the cache intact.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git push origin main

2	//! of these codes with a fixed HTTP status; the worker renders it as an RFC
3	//! 9457 problem+json body. The table only grows: previous codes and their

8	/// A client-reachable failure with its wire vocabulary. One enum, one
9	/// table: the mapping from a code to its status is a single reviewable
10	/// fact, and a condition a client can cause lands here rather than in an
11	/// assertion.
12	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
13	pub enum ClientError {
14	    /// Key length or format rejected; also the path-traversal guard.

# The workerd lane

The workerd lane runs the built worker bundle under `wrangler dev --local`,
which is miniflare over the real workerd binary: R2, KV, the Cache API,
scheduled invocations, and the module-pipeline semantics are the runtime's
own rather than a mock's. Assertions reach the worker over real HTTP from
`workerd/check.mjs`, a node script with no npm dependencies (the
devshell's node 22 supplies fetch and child_process).

Each scenario gets its own persistence directory: the driver seeds the
local R2 with `wrangler r2 object put --local`, boots the worker on a
free port, asserts, and kills it. Cache behavior is not observed by
introspecting miniflare internals: the worker emits events
(read.edge_hit, read.bucket_hit, read.miss, generation.document_corrupt)
and the driver matches them in the wrangler log stream, so a cache that
silently never stores surfaces as a failure the way it would in
production.

Outbound calls have the same treatment. The driver runs a stub server
that plays three roles: the OIDC JWKS endpoint, holding a per-run RSA
keypair; the OAuth web endpoint, exchanging one known code for a member
token and one for an outsider token; and the GitHub API endpoints the
verdict path calls (`/user` and org membership), counting hits so the
scenarios can prove the KV verdict cache serves repeat reads. The worker
reaches them through the `CACHET_JWKS_URL`, `CACHET_GITHUB_API_URL`, and
`CACHET_GITHUB_WEB_URL` variables, which the driver passes with
`wrangler dev --var`; auth scenarios mint RS256 tokens against the
stub's private key, so a verification that silently skips would fail the
matrix. The lane's ed25519 signing secret and the OAuth client secret
enter as `.dev.vars`, the same way a deployment's secrets enter as
bindings; the file is written before the write scenarios, deleted when
the lane ends, and gitignored.

The lane covers the read path, the write path, and the API surface so
far: the handshake body and its headers; narinfo and NAR serving with
wire headers; positive and negative edge caching through the
generation-scoped key space; HEAD semantics; problem+json rejections by
shape and by exact bytes; the corrupt-generation bypass; generation-zero
behavior on an empty bucket; the OIDC rejection matrix (wrong org, alg
confusion, staleness, expired tokens); guard ordering (411 before 413,
401 before 411); the verify-then-sign pipeline end to end, from a NAR
upload through a signed narinfo with both signatures and the file facts;
the multipart quartet with its record, part-size enforcement, replay, and
abort; read verdicts cached in KV for both the admit and the deny
direction; lease renewal bound to the token's own claims with
forbidden_ref and forbidden_project refusals; the project listing; the
public config document; and the browser login flow, from the login
redirect's exact parameters through state consumption (a replayed state
never reaches the exchange), the outsider's forbidden_org refusal, the
session cookie's attributes, and logout's session deletion. The served
OpenAPI document is asserted byte-identical to the committed one, which is
the served half of the drift bijection (CLAUDE.md §8). The GC scenarios
invoke the scheduled handler over wrangler's dev endpoint with grace

# This is the published, public copy of the cachet-setup action. GitHub blocks a public repository
# from consuming an action that lives in a private one, and cachet is private, so a public consumer
# (for example agx-runtime/substrate-kernels) needs the action to live in a public repository. The
# canonical source and the build that produces post/dist/*.cjs live in the private agx-runtime/cachet
# repository under action/; a change is made there and copied here, so any drift is traceable to that
# one source.
name: cachet-setup
description: >-
    Install Determinate Nix, wire this job into the cachet binary cache, and push what the job builds.
author: loopholelabs
# A composite action cannot declare a post step, which is why the push lives in a nested JavaScript
# action below. This is the same shape cachix/cachix-action uses, for the same reason.

inputs:
    roots:
        description: >-
            Flake installables whose closures this project needs. Their outputs are pushed unconditionally
            and, on the default branch, become the project's garbage-collection lease.
        required: false
        default: ''
    signing-key:
        description: >-
            The NAR signing key, and the only org-level secret cachet needs. Pass the
            CACHET_SIGNING_KEY secret. Nix signs with it on this runner; it never reaches the cache.
        required: true
    cache-url:
        description: The cache's base URL.
        required: false
        # A metadata default, which is the one place a deployment hostname may appear (ADR 0013).
        default: https://pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io
    audience:
        description: The OIDC audience the cache requires.
        required: false
        default: cachet
    project:
        description: >-
            The lease name for this repository. Defaults to the owner and name joined by a hyphen
            (`my-org-my-repo`), which is unique across the organisations this cache serves — two
            repositories sharing a name would otherwise share a lease and overwrite each other's.
        required: false
        default: ''
    upstream-url:
        description: The upstream cache to filter against before pushing.
        required: false
        default: https://cache.nixos.org
    default-branch-ref:
        description: >-
            The ref permitted to renew the lease. The cache enforces this itself; this input only avoids a
            request that would be refused.
        required: false
        default: refs/heads/main
    trusted-public-key:
        description: >-
            The public half of the signing key, in Nix's `name:base64` form, so this job can verify what it
            substitutes from the cache.
        required: false
        # A metadata default, like `cache-url` above: the public key is deployment identity, not a
        # secret, and ADR 0013 makes action metadata the one place deployment identity may appear.
        # Without a default here every consuming repository would have to learn and paste the key,
        # and one that forgot would fail signature verification on every substitution — which Nix
        # reports as a cache miss, so the job would silently compile from source while the cache
        # looked healthy. The login script bakes in the same value (`public_key_default` in
        # scripts/cache-login.sh), so a laptop and a runner learn the key the same way.
        default: pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io-1:JC2XK3HyAUXteubthi/pUEM0iokE6YyOGFURMB4hsRE=
    push:
        description: Set to false to use the cache read-only.
        required: false
        default: 'true'
    determinate-nix-action-version:
        description: Which release of the Determinate Nix installer action to use.
        required: false
        default: v3

runs:
    using: composite
    steps:
        # Provision the cache read credential BEFORE Determinate is installed and its daemon starts.
        # Determinate synthesizes the netrc the daemon reads (/nix/var/determinate/netrc) at daemon start,
        # merging every file listed under authentication.additionalNetrcSources — and that start-up
        # synthesis is the only reliable one on these runners. A later re-synthesis is gated on the FlakeHub
        # login, whose transient failures otherwise leave cache reads at 401 and every build recompiling
        # from source. Writing the credential and the config here, before the daemon exists, means its
        # start-up synthesis merges the credential and the FlakeHub failure never gets to gate it
        # (docs.determinate.systems, migrate-to-flakehub-cache).
        - name: Provision the cachet read credential before Determinate starts
          shell: bash
          env:
              CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
              CACHET_AUDIENCE: ${{ inputs.audience }}
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail

              # The OIDC token authenticates this job; nothing is stored and the runner is authorised
              # because it is provably ours (docs/contracts.md). This is minted here, without Nix, because
              # Determinate is not installed yet.
              if [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ]; then
                echo "cachet: this job cannot mint an OIDC token." >&2
                echo "  Add 'permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }' to the job." >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              token="$(curl -fsSL \
                -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}" \
                "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=${CACHET_AUDIENCE}" | jq -r '.value')"
              host="$(printf '%s' "${CACHET_CACHE_URL}" | sed -e 's#^https\?://##' -e 's#/.*$##')"

              # The credential file: real, outside the Nix store, 0600, root-owned, as Determinate requires.
              sudo mkdir -p /etc/nix /etc/determinate
              printf 'machine %s login cachet password %s\n' "${host}" "${token}" \
                | sudo tee /etc/nix/netrc >/dev/null
              sudo chmod 600 /etc/nix/netrc

              # Register it under authentication.additionalNetrcSources. Determinate is not installed yet,
              # so the config usually does not exist; merge with jq when it does so anything the installer
              # pre-seeds survives.
              if [ -f /etc/determinate/config.json ]; then
                sudo cat /etc/determinate/config.json \
                  | jq '.authentication.additionalNetrcSources = ((.authentication.additionalNetrcSources // []) + ["/etc/nix/netrc"] | unique)' \
                  | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp >/dev/null
                sudo mv /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp /etc/determinate/config.json
              else
                printf '{"authentication":{"additionalNetrcSources":["/etc/nix/netrc"]}}\n' \
                  | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json >/dev/null
              fi
              echo "cachet: read credential provisioned before Determinate starts"

        # Determinate Nix is the one distribution everywhere, including on laptops (ADR 0008).
        - uses: DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@v3.21.9
          with:
              # Add the cache and its trusted key at install time, so the daemon starts already knowing
              # them. Adding them afterwards in the Configure step proved ineffective — the daemon never
              # queried cachet at all — because a substituter and its trusted key reach the daemon only when
              # it reads its config at start. extra-substituters and extra-trusted-public-keys accumulate
              # (they use the extra- prefix), so this adds cachet alongside cache.nixos.org rather than
              # replacing it.
              extra-conf: |
                  extra-substituters = ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
                  extra-trusted-public-keys = ${{ inputs.trusted-public-key }}

        # Log out of FlakeHub, which the determinate-nix-action step above logged into on its own. On a
        # runner granting id-token: write — which this action requires to mint its own cachet OIDC token —
        # Determinate mints a second OIDC token for FlakeHub and logs in, and that login adds
        # https://cache.flakehub.com to the daemon's active substituters. This deployment is not a FlakeHub
        # Cache customer, so every narinfo lookup then answers 401 ("User is not authorized for this
        # resource") before it falls through to cachet: an error-level log line and a wasted round trip on
        # every request, on a build that still succeeds. Logging out returns the substituter set to the
        # logged-out state, in which cache.flakehub.com is absent — verified against a local Determinate
        # install, where `determinate-nixd status` reports logged-out and `nix config show substituters`
        # omits FlakeHub. cachet's own read credential is the netrc merged from additionalNetrcSources and
        # is independent of the FlakeHub login, so the Configure step's auth probe below still reports 404.
        - name: Log out of FlakeHub Cache, which this deployment does not use
          shell: bash
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              # `|| true`: a job without id-token never logged in, so logout is a no-op there rather than a
              # failure, and this action must not fail a build over a cache it does not even use.
              sudo determinate-nixd auth logout || true
              echo "cachet: FlakeHub login status after logout:"
              sudo determinate-nixd status || true

        - name: Configure cachet
          shell: bash
          env:
              CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
              CACHET_AUDIENCE: ${{ inputs.audience }}
              CACHET_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ inputs.trusted-public-key }}
              CACHET_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ inputs.signing-key }}
              CACHET_PROJECT: ${{ inputs.project }}
              CACHET_ROOTS: ${{ inputs.roots }}
              CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL: ${{ inputs.upstream-url }}
              CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF: ${{ inputs.default-branch-ref }}
              CACHET_PUSH: ${{ inputs.push }}
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail

              # The read credential and its Determinate config were provisioned before the daemon started
              # (the first step of this action), so the daemon's start-up synthesis already merged the
              # credential into the netrc it reads. There is nothing to do here for the netrc.

              # The substituter and trusted key are added at install time now (the extra-conf on the
              # determinate-nix-action step above), so the daemon starts already knowing them. They are not
              # written here: a substituter added after the daemon has started is never consulted, which is
              # why the last run authenticated yet never queried cachet.

              # Confirm the daemon's netrc authenticates against cachet, so a regression surfaces in the log
              # rather than as a silent rebuild: a 404 means the credential is present and authenticated —
              # the probed path is simply absent — while a 401 means it is not.
              daemon_netrc="$(nix config show netrc-file 2>/dev/null || echo /nix/var/determinate/netrc)"
              probe_code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --netrc-file "${daemon_netrc}" \
                "${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}/0000000000000000000000000000000a.narinfo" 2>/dev/null || echo 000)"
              echo "cachet: read auth probe returned ${probe_code} (404 = authenticated, 401 = not)"

              # The signing key is written where only this runner can read it, and never leaves it (ADR 0004).
              key_file="${RUNNER_TEMP}/cachet-signing.key"
              printf '%s' "${CACHET_SIGNING_KEY}" > "${key_file}"
              chmod 600 "${key_file}"
              echo "CACHET_SIGNING_KEY_FILE=${key_file}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"

              # Everything the post step reads is exported to the job environment here, and this is the
              # only place any of it is resolved. A step-level `env:` block is scoped to the step it sits
              # on, so passing these to the nested action as `with:` inputs left the post step reading
              # empty strings and declining to push, silently, on every run.
              #
              # The project name defaults to owner-and-name rather than the bare repository name.
              #
              # why: this cache serves more than one organisation, so two repositories can share a name.
              # A lease is filed under the project name and a renewal replaces the previous document
              # wholesale, so two same-named repositories defaulting to one project would overwrite each
              # other's lease — and each would then stop protecting the other's closure, making live
              # paths collectable (Invariant GC-NEVER-EATS-THE-LIVING). Including the owner makes the
              # default unique by construction rather than by everyone remembering to pass `project`.
              project="${CACHET_PROJECT}"
              if [ -z "${project}" ]; then
                project="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY//\//-}"
              fi
              # why: the heredoc form rather than `NAME=value`. `roots` takes several installables and the
              # post step splits it on any whitespace, so a caller writing them one per line with a YAML
              # block scalar is using the documented shape — and a bare `NAME=value` line cannot express
              # a newline. GitHub rejects the whole file with "Invalid format" when it sees the
              # continuation, which fails the step for a reason that points nowhere near the cause.
              #
              # The delimiter is fixed and long enough not to occur in a flake installable, and the
              # values here are action inputs rather than anything a request supplies.
              env_file() {
                printf '%s<<CACHET_EOF_1c7f\n%s\nCACHET_EOF_1c7f\n' "$1" "$2" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
              }
              env_file CACHET_CACHE_URL "${CACHET_CACHE_URL}"
              env_file CACHET_AUDIENCE "${CACHET_AUDIENCE}"
              env_file CACHET_PROJECT "${project}"
              env_file CACHET_ROOTS "${CACHET_ROOTS}"
              env_file CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL "${CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL}"
              env_file CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF "${CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF}"
              env_file CACHET_PUSH "${CACHET_PUSH}"

              echo "cachet: configured ${CACHET_CACHE_URL} as a substituter for project ${project}"

        # The nested JavaScript action: its main step snapshots the store, and its post step, on success
        # only, does the push. It takes no inputs, because the step above resolved all of them into the
        # job environment.
        # why: the full owner/repo/path@ref form rather than `./post`. A composite action resolves a
        # relative `./post` against the consumer's GITHUB_WORKSPACE rather than this action's own
        # directory, so a cross-repo consumer looked for `<workspace>/post` and failed with "Can't find
        # 'action.yml' under .../post". Naming the repository resolves the nested action independently of
        # where the consumer checked out. It is pinned to the v1 major tag, which every release in the 1.x
        # line moves forward, so the composite and its post action always come from the same line.
        - uses: agx-runtime/cachet-action/post@v1
action.yml

name: cachet-push
description: >-
    Snapshots the Nix store, then on job success pushes what was added and renews the lease. Not meant to
    be used directly — the cachet-setup composite action wraps it.

# why: no inputs. The cachet-setup composite resolves every value and exports it to the job environment,
# which is what both this action's steps read. Declaring them here as well would give the post step a
# second, differently-named source of the same configuration (GitHub exposes an input as `INPUT_<NAME>`,
# not as the name the code reads), and that mismatch is exactly the bug that made this step decline to
# push on every run while reporting success.

runs:
    using: node24
    main: dist/main.cjs
    post: dist/post.cjs
    # why: on success only. A failed build must never populate the cache or refresh a lease — that is what
    # keeps a broken artifact from becoming the one everybody substitutes.
    post-if: success()

Roots arrive via `CACHET_ROOTS`, split on `/\s+/` with empty entries dropped (so a YAML heredoc with one installable per line works).

`resolveRootPaths` loops installables in order and runs `nix path-info <installable>` (no `--all`, no extra flags) for each. stdout is parsed with the same `parseSnapshot` grammar and every parsed path is appended. There is no dedup and no cross-check that the installable resolved to exactly one path.

Per-installable failure writes `cachet: could not resolve ${installable}; it will not be a lease root\n` to stderr and continues with the rest. The unresolved installable string still appears in the lease's `installables` array later; only its store paths are missing.

`stageAndUpload` in `post.ts`:
- Staging root: `mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'cachet-staging-'))`.
- Destination URI: `` `file://${stagingRoot}?compression=zstd&secret-key=${inputs.signingKeyFile}` `` (signing key path from `CACHET_SIGNING_KEY_FILE`).
- Command: `nix copy --to <destination> ...paths` with all surviving paths as trailing argv entries, in `toUpload` order.

If `sizeBytes <= UPLOAD_SINGLE_MAX_BYTES` (`94_371_840`, i.e., 90 MiB; the comparison is `<=`) → single PUT. **Single PUT** (`putWhole`): the whole file is read into memory. Each attempt mints a fresh token, then:
- `PUT ${url(key)}`
- Headers: `Authorization: Bearer ${token}`, `Content-Length: ${sizeBytes}` (decimal string).
- Body: the full file bytes.
- Success: any 2xx (the Worker answers 204). Failure message: `${status} ${await response.text()}`.

**Retry policy** (`withRetries` in `retry.ts`, shared by every request kind): `UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX` = `3` total attempts. A thrown error is treated identically to a returned failure (`error.message` or `String(error)`). Between attempts: sleep `UPLOAD_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS * (tries + 1)` with base `500` — so 500 ms after attempt 1, 1000 ms after attempt 2, no sleep after the final attempt. Final failure message: `${what} failed after 3 attempts: ${last}`, where `what` is a per-operation label like `PUT ${key}`, `begin ${key}`, `part ${n} of ${key}`, `complete ${key}`, or `renew the lease for ${project}`.

**Conditions** (all must hold):
1. `CACHET_PUSH` is not exactly `'false'` (default `'true'`; any value other than the literal string `'false'` enables pushing).
2. None of `CACHET_CACHE_URL`, `CACHET_PROJECT`, `CACHET_AUDIENCE` is empty.

Concrete rule: the post step never exits non-zero and never uses `setFailed`. Both entry points wrap everything in `.catch(...)` writing a stderr line. The distinction vocabulary:

Trigger: `sizeBytes > 94_371_840` bytes. Part layout: every part except the last is exactly `67_108_864` bytes; the last is the remainder (always ≥ 1 byte by construction). Max 1000 parts (≈ 64 TiB ceiling; refusal before any byte moves). 1. **Begin**: `POST ${url(key, '?uploads')}` with `Authorization` and `x-cachet-upload-bytes: ${sizeBytes}` (header name from `UPLOAD_TOTAL_BYTES_HEADER`). Success body parsed as `{uploadId: string, expectedParts: number}`; the client trusts it (no cross-check against its own plan).

Best effort: no retries, fetch errors swallowed via `.catch(() => undefined)`, and a token-mint failure skips the abort silently. The server-side collector reclaims abandoned uploads regardless.

Begin, each part, and complete are each wrapped in the standard 3-attempt retry. A part failing all attempts triggers abort, then the failure propagates (push aborts, no lease renewal).

## 10. Other behavior worth porting

- **Sequential everything across objects**; the only concurrency in the whole pipeline is the two bounded probe pools (16 in flight).
- **Dedup** exists only in `storeDiff` (collapses repeated paths in the after-snapshot). `resolveRootPaths` does not dedup; filters preserve input order.
- **The roots exception is pass-1-only**: a root path already held by cachet is not re-uploaded (pass 2 drops it), and the lease protects it regardless because renewal is unconditional on filter/upload success.
- **No explicit timeouts** on any fetch; hung connections rely on runtime defaults. Retries are the only mitigation.
- **Memory shape**: single PUT and multipart both buffer the entire object in memory (multipart slices from the buffered bytes). A 64 GiB multipart object is legal by the part-count cap and would be held in memory whole.
- **`execFile` maxBuffer 256 MiB** on all nix invocations; a snapshot larger than that fails the command rather than truncating.
- **Early-return asymmetry** (the subtle one): zero candidates after the diff → no lease renewal at all. Non-zero candidates that all filter out → renewal proceeds. Port this exactly; the comment notes the renewal must happen when nothing was new because "a fully-cached rebuild uploads nothing yet must still keep its closure alive," while a job that produced nothing has no closure to keep.
- **`run()` error envelope**: every failing subprocess becomes `${argv.join(' ')} failed: ${message}`, so nix's stderr is absent unless it lands in `error.message` (Node's execFile error message includes stderr text).
- **Environment inventory**: `RUNNER_TEMP`, `GITHUB_REF`, `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL`, `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`, `CACHET_CACHE_URL`, `CACHET_AUDIENCE`, `CACHET_PROJECT`, `CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL`, `CACHET_SIGNING_KEY_FILE`, `CACHET_ROOTS`, `CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF`, `CACHET_PUSH`.

One caveat for the port: this old pipeline does client-side signing (`?secret-key=` on the `nix copy` destination), whereas the new repo's constitution (CLAUDE.md §1) specifies server-side signing after NAR verification. Exhaustive negative corpus unit tests + hegel properties.

Do it together, do it complete, or don't do it"; `entire` CLI session capture wired. Security-critical invariants: attacker-reachable inputs never panic (typed errors only); secrets never logged nor returned; the signing-key never leaves custody; the 1Password-backed signed-commit requirement must NOT be bypassed (no --no-gpg-sign) without explicit permission.

# cachet v1: self-hosted nix binary cache, Rust on Cloudflare Workers

## Context

The existing cachet (TypeScript on Cloudflare Workers, plus its GitHub Action) is a working org-wide nix binary cache. It carries platform-accident complexity, a documented signing-key trust regression, a GC that has never deleted anything, a lease-clobbering hole, and 471 lines of login shell. The rewrite target is a fresh git repo (currently holding only a copied PROSE.md, which is binding law for all prose the repo ships). The goal: anyone clones the repo, runs one bootstrap flow, and gets an org-scoped, authenticated nix binary cache in their own Cloudflare account. CI pushes sign server-side; laptops authenticate by GitHub device flow; the whole repo is OSS under Apache-2.0 including the GitHub Action. No repo artifact (code, comments, docs, ADRs) references the internal template projects; conventions are copied, never cited.

## Locked decisions (from user)

- Auth is GitHub only. CI: OIDC. Humans on laptops: GitHub device flow. No magic link, no passwords, no external secrets manager, no database.
- One deployment serves exactly one configured GitHub org (CACHET_ORGS comma list). Nobody outside the org can authenticate at all.
- Signing is server-side. The worker holds a per-deployment ed25519 key in Cloudflare Secrets Store, generated at bootstrap. This matches how FlakeHub Cache authenticates CI (GitHub OIDC) while the service owns signing; poison resistance lives in write-path hash verification.
- Laptops are read-only. Writes are OIDC-only. `POST /roots/{project}` requires project == hyphenated `repository` claim plus ref == CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF.
- v1 ships the backend only; there is no rendered UI. The browser OAuth code flow and sessions ARE in scope because they are backend work: `/_auth/login`, `/_auth/callback`, `/logout` exist and are workerd-tested, the callback issues the session cookie and 302s to an optional CACHET_UI_ORIGIN (204 when unset). v1 also serves every endpoint the later SPA needs (public config, stats, projects, GC reports). The CLI prints the nix.conf snippet itself, sourced from /api/public/config.
- OpenAPI: the code is the source of truth. Route handlers in `cachet-api` carry utoipa derive macros; `just openapi` regenerates the committed `docs/openapi.yaml` from the code and CI fails on drift; the worker serves the committed bytes at /api/openapi.json (served == generated, golden test). No code generation from the spec, ever.
- Error bodies are RFC 9457 problem+json; the old code → status table is preserved exactly and only extended.
- The GitHub Action lives in this repo under `action/` (composite wrapper + nested node24 post action), consuming the `cachet` binary from this repo's own GitHub Releases. Consumers use `<org>/cachet/action@v1`.
- GC is armed from day one, runs entirely inside Cloudflare (cron trigger in the same worker, cursor-resumable across invocations), and every run emits report objects that the API serves; the later SPA renders them.
- No DST/sim harness. Lanes: unit, property (hegel), golden, kani, workerd, integration. Gates: fmt, clippy, deny, doc-manifest, lane-manifest, actionlint, scripts, wasm-hygiene, openapi-drift.
- Store: R2 for cache data (ported key layout), one KV namespace for token-validation verdicts only. No D1.

## Crate DAG

Workspace resolver 2, `[lints] workspace = true`, publish=false version 0.0.1, Apache-2.0, exact toolchain pin (wasm32-unknown-unknown + four native triples). Direction is one-way; path deps only.

| Crate | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `cachet-core` | Pure domain: narinfo grammar and canonical serialization, store-path/NAR key validation, nix base32, lease/generation/upload-record documents, multipart part-plan math, GC mark/sweep/gates/plan over injected callbacks, OIDC claim policy, GitHub-token verdict policy, error-code table. Clock/Rng traits defined here; no I/O, no ambient entropy. |
| `cachet-crypto` | Pure computation: sha2, ed25519-dalek (sign/verify/keygen), narinfo fingerprint, RS256 verify (WebCrypto via web_sys or pure-rust rsa+sha2; a spike decides), ruzstd streaming decode. Kani proofs colocated. |
| `cachet-api` | HTTP surface as typed route handlers with utoipa derive macros: the OpenAPI YAML is generated from this code, and problem+json bodies come from the shared error taxonomy. No SSR. |
| `cachet-worker` | Deployable leaf: `#[event(fetch)]` + `#[event(scheduled)]`, R2/KV/Cache/GitHub adapters, per-isolate JWKS cache, signing pipeline over streams, GC driver. The only crate with `worker` deps and getrandom/js. |
| `cachet-push` | Push pipeline as a native library: snapshot/diff, upstream filter at concurrency 16, `nix copy --to file://?compression=zstd` staging (unsigned), NARs-before-narinfos upload with fresh OIDC per request, lease renewal, never-fail-the-job semantics. nix-archive, nix-derivation, nix-flake-lock live here (native targets only). |
| `cachet-cli` | The `cachet` binary (clap): `login` (device flow), `setup` (managed nix.conf block + netrc), `push [--dry-run]`, `keygen`, `doctor` (401-vs-404 probe). reqwest+rustls. Released by cargo-dist for four triples. |

nix-flake-lock's concrete job: during push, parse the repo's flake.lock, record the pinned root revision in lease metadata (surfaced later in the SPA), and validate the follows-graph. nix-derivation parses .drv and store paths client-side. nix-archive verifies/encodes NARs client-side; it cannot go to wasm (unconditional libc+rustix deps) and the worker does not need it because verification hashes bytes with sha2+ruzstd. Upstreaming a unix-feature gate is an optional spike, not a blocker.

## Auth flows (three; only OIDC writes)

Check order on every route, ported from the previous worker: key validation, config validation, authorization, body/shape guards, work. Malformed key is 400 before any credential read; unauthenticated write is 401 before any 411.

1. GitHub OIDC (the only write credential): RS256 pinned by policy, JWKS per-isolate cache (10-minute TTL, one refetch on unknown kid, stale fallback, 503 `auth_unavailable` when cold), `iss`/`aud` exact (aud arrays refused), `repository_owner` ∈ CACHET_ORGS, required claims `exp,iat,aud,iss,repository,repository_owner,ref`, times against the injected clock. Lease renewal additionally requires ref == CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF (403 forbidden_ref) and project == hyphenated repository claim (403 forbidden_project, new code).
2. Device-flow GitHub token (read, laptops and admins): `cachet login --url <url>` GETs unauthenticated `/api/public/config` (`{oauthClientId, orgs, host, publicKey}`), runs github.com's device endpoints directly, stores the GitHub user token 0600 under `~/.config/cachet/`. The worker never participates in the flow. On each request: sha256 the presented token, look up `ghverdict/` KV (600s allow / 60s deny), on miss call `GET /user` + org membership against the GitHub API, cache the verdict. Verdict TTL is the documented revocation window. Admin requests (under /api/self/) additionally require the login ∈ CACHET_ADMINS, where the login comes from the validated verdict or the session.
3. Browser OAuth code flow (backend only; the SPA consumes it later): `GET /_auth/login` writes `oauth-state/{state}` (KV, 600s, single-use) and 302s to github.com (scope `read:org read:user`, deployment client id, callback URL, state). `GET /_auth/callback` consumes the state (fail closed on miss), exchanges the code with the server-held client secret, checks `GET /user` + org membership, mints a 128-bit session id, writes `sess/{id}` (KV, 14-day TTL), sets `cachet_session=…; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`, then 302s to CACHET_UI_ORIGIN when configured and otherwise answers 204. `POST /logout` deletes the session and expires the cookie. Session-authenticated requests resolve exactly like verdict-authenticated ones for read/admin purposes; they never get write scope.

## Signing pipeline

Narinfo PUT after validation, auth, and 411/413 guards. Verify-then-sign is enforced by construction: the signing function takes a `VerifiedNar` newtype only the verifier constructs. Wire hash format is nix base32 with `sha256:` prefix. The signature input is the nix fingerprint `"1;<storePath>;<narHash>;<narSize>;<refs joined by ,>"`, signed directly with ed25519 (no outer hash). Appended line: `Sig: {CACHET_HOST}-1:<base64>`; pre-existing Sig lines are preserved. Steps: parse (total, 400), required StorePath/URL/NarHash/NarSize present, StorePath hash == URL key (400), suffix ∈ {"", ".zst"} (400 unsupported_compression), bucket.head(URL) exists (409 narinfo_nar_missing), stream the stored NAR through tee(compressed-sha256, ruzstd → nar-sha256 + byte count), NarSize == decompressed count (bomb guard), NarHash/NarSize agreement (400 nar_hash_mismatch), FileHash/FileSize agreement when present (400 file_hash_mismatch), compressed sha256 == hash named in the NAR key, canonicalize preserving unknown fields, append Sig, bucket.put, 204. This path hashes multi-hundred-MiB objects, so deployments require a paid plan (`cpu_ms = 300000`, recorded in DEPLOY.md). A spike measures ruzstd+sha2 throughput under workerd and lands the number in the CPU-budget ADR.

## GC (inside Cloudflare, reportable)

Cron binding on the same worker (`0 5 * * *`; staging configurable). One invocation has a wall-clock budget of 13 minutes and a binding-op budget of 900; the driver persists a cursor document at each stage boundary and exits cleanly within a named headroom, resuming on the next cron tick, so caches of any size sweep inside Cloudflare without an external runner. Stages: inventory (paginated R2 list), roots (leases active when renewed within 30 days; unparseable lease is a gate), mark (iterative BFS over narinfo References, visited cap 100k paths, one read per visit asserted), gates (sweep fraction > 0.25, unreadable or unparseable root, budget exhaustion, truncated inventory or leases, corrupt meta/generation; any trip aborts the run and writes the report), sweep (unmarked AND older than 14-day grace), delete narinfos before NARs in bounded batches so NEVER-DANGLE holds at every instant, bump meta/generation, write `gc-runs/{runId}/` stage artifacts and `gc-reports/{runId}.json`, reap stale `uploads/` older than 7 days. Armed/grace/retention are vars with production defaults; staging zeroes grace for the integration lane without backdating R2 timestamps.

UI-reportability: runs and reports are first-class API data. `/api/self/gc-runs` (paginated run list) and `/api/self/gc-runs/{runId}` (full report: stages, gates, counts, durations, deletions) serve the same `gc-reports/` objects the driver writes, so the later SPA renders history without touching R2 directly. `/api/self/stats` derives current cache totals from the latest report.

## Storage layout

R2 keys: `{hash32}.narinfo`, `nar/{hash52}.nar[.xz|.zst|.bz2|.gz|.br|.lzip|.lz4]` (reads suffix-agnostic; signing accepts only `""` and `.zst` in v1), `meta/generation`, `roots/{project}`, `uploads/{uploadId}`, `gc-runs/{runId}/…`, `gc-reports/{runId}.json`. Internal prefixes are unreachable from requests by construction and refused a second time by the sweep candidate filter. KV keys: `oauth-state/{state}` (600s, consumed on use), `sess/{sessionId}` (14-day TTL), `ghverdict/{sha256}` (600s allow / 60s deny). Tokens are never persisted beyond their digest.

Edge caching keeps the previous design: generation-scoped synthetic keys (`https://cachet-edge.invalid/g{N}{path}`), 30-day immutable positive TTL, 30s negative caching, HEAD bypasses edge cache, objects > 512 MB stream uncached, the GC generation bump invalidates globally within 60s. Requires a custom domain (Cache API is inert on workers.dev); workers.dev hostname disabled.

## Infra and bootstrap (alchemy)

Alchemy v2 (exact pins for alchemy + effect, bumped together). Root `alchemy.run.ts` Effect-generator stack, pure `infra/{stage,resources,secrets}.ts` modules with unit tests, `tsconfig.alchemy.json` typechecked as a CI gate, state via `Cloudflare.state()` with ALCHEMY_LOCAL_STATE=1 fallback, deploy verb `bun alchemy deploy --yes --adopt --stage production`. Secrets Store holds CACHET_SIGNING_KEY and GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET (workers receive bindings only). Vars carry CACHET_ORGS, CACHET_ADMINS, CACHET_AUDIENCE, CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF, CACHET_HOST, CACHET_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, and the GC knobs. Custom domain via the domain prop; workers.dev off; cron binding for GC. Stage grammar: production / staging / dev / dev-<name>; no preview stages.

The wasm seam is SPIKE T0, ordered before all product work: `Cloudflare.Worker { main: "<worker-build output>/index.js", bundle: false }` (bundle:false merged upstream in June 2026; additional modules including *.wasm are globbed wrangler-style). Fallback, documented in the ADR and DEPLOY.md: alchemy owns every resource except the worker, which `wrangler deploy` publishes from the build output.

Bootstrap UX: clone → `nix develop` (flake provides bun, just, wrangler, worker-build, miniflare) → `just bootstrap` (interactive: Cloudflare token + scope checklist; GitHub OAuth App checklist including enabling Device Flow, with the settings URL opened; org slug; admin logins; domain; signing keypair generated locally via `cachet keygen`, secret written 0600 into gitignored `.deploy/env.<stage>`; alchemy deploy; prints the deployment URL, the `<host>-1:<base64>` public key line, and the `cachet login --url` command).

Deploy CI: `deploy-staging` on main after green ci, `deploy-production` environment-gated with required reviewers, guarded by `vars.CACHET_DEPLOY_ENABLED` so forks are inert.

## Testing lanes and gates

The lane machinery: `docs/testing/lanes.toml` registry; `scripts/check-lane-manifest.sh` enforces lanes.toml ⇔ docs/testing/*.md ⇔ ci.yml job ids; `scripts/check-doc-manifest.sh` enforces CLAUDE.md @-imports ⇔ the doc set; nextest ci profile with retries=0 (a flake is a bug).

- unit (nextest over the locked closure): every pure function, the full auth negative corpus (alg confusion, unknown kid, expired, aud array, wrong org, missing/mistyped claims), the check-order matrix.
- property (hegel): narinfo round-trip and parser totality over a hostile corpus, key grammar against `..`, `%2e%2e`, confusables, overlong inputs, part-plan math, lease totality, GC laws (walk termination on cycles, narinfo-before-NAR ordering, marked ∩ sweep = ∅, reserved prefixes never swept).
- golden: committed vectors generated against real nix output (narinfo canonical bytes, signed narinfo verified against a real `nix-store --generate-binary-cache-key` pair, fingerprint vectors, /nix-cache-info body, problem+json bodies, lease/generation/upload records), plus served-spec == generated yaml byte equality.
- kani (`#[cfg(kani)]` colocated, grep-discovered): store-path base32 round-trip, canonicalization fixed point with unknown-field preservation, part-plan invariants, fingerprint determinism, mark/sweep disjointness.
- workerd (miniflare over the built bundle, real R2/KV/Cache semantics, real stub JWKS and GitHub API servers as outbound services): every route, multipart against real part rules, Cache API behavior, GC two-tick through the cursor, the full rejection matrix.
- integration (`just integration`, nightly + post-deploy on staging): ~126 MiB incompressible closure through the real action path, `nix-store --delete`, `nix copy --from`, `nix store verify --sigs-needed 1` against the deployment public key; missing credentials fail loudly with instructions, never skip.
- wasm-hygiene gate: `wasm-tools print` + string scan of the shipped bundle fails on ring/aws-lc/tokio symbols and on secret-shaped strings.
- openapi-drift gate: `just openapi --check` regenerates the spec from code and fails on any diff from the committed file.

CI: one job per gate/lane with job id == just verb, every step `nix develop --command just <verb>` after SHA-pinned checkout and the DeterminateSystems nix action; concurrency cancel-in-progress off main; permissions contents:read. dependabot weekly: cargo, flake.lock, github-actions. Release: tag-triggered cargo-dist, four triples plus a shasum manifest on GitHub Releases.

## Execution order (phases)

**P0, spikes first, SPIKE T0 before anything else:** alchemy bundle:false against a trivial worker-build artifact (decides the deploy story); fallback recorded. Then repo skeleton: workspace pins, flake + crane + treefmt, deny.toml (license allowlist, bans ring/aws-lc-rs/aws-lc-sys/zstd-C, crates.io only), clippy.toml (no ambient clock/threads, BTree over Hash), nextest profile, manifest scripts, ci.yml skeleton, LICENSE, README stub, CLAUDE.md skeleton. Remaining spikes land as their gates approach: Cache API adapter, workers-rs R2 multipart/streaming shape, ed25519 entropy scoping + `Secret<SigningKey>`, RS256 crypto choice (WebCrypto vs rsa+sha2), getrandom/js containment, cron under miniflare, device flow on a scratch OAuth App, ruzstd+sha2 throughput (before P5), utoipa derive overhead in the wasm bundle (before P6).

**P1 cachet-core:** types, key grammar, narinfo grammar, lease/generation/upload-record/part-plan, error taxonomy, GC pure algorithm. Lanes: unit, property, golden, kani.

**P2 cachet-crypto:** sha256/base32/base64, ed25519 with golden key vectors, ruzstd streamer; RS256 per the spike. Lanes: unit, property, golden, kani.

**P3 auth core:** OIDC claim policy, JWKS cache policy, verdict policy, forbidden_project binding; exhaustive negative corpus. Lanes: unit, property.

**P4 worker spine and read path:** config, error boundary (RFC 9457), logging with no credential fields, generation/edge adapter, narinfo and NAR GET+HEAD, workerd lane scaffold.

**P5 write path:** NAR PUT streaming with running sha256, multipart quartet with uploads bookkeeping, the signing pipeline with VerifiedNar typestate, full rejection matrix enumerated in the generated spec.

**P6 API surface:** roots routes (project binding, ref gate), /api/public/config, /api/self/* (stats, projects, gc-runs, gc-runs/{runId}), browser OAuth endpoints (/_auth/login, /_auth/callback, /logout) with the KV state and session flow, utoipa-derived /api/openapi.json served from the committed generated yaml, openapi-drift verb.

**P7 GC:** driver, cursor, stages, armed defaults, stale-upload reaper, report endpoints wired to `gc-reports/`.

**P8 push, CLI, action:** cachet-push library, cachet CLI (login setup push keygen doctor), cargo-dist, in-repo `action/` (presteps retained from the previous action: Determinate install with extra-conf, OIDC netrc provisioned before the daemon starts, FlakeHub logout; post step downloads the pinned released `cachet` binary and runs `cachet push`; never fails the job).

**P9 infra and bootstrap:** full alchemy stack, deploy.yml, just bootstrap, docs/DEPLOY.md.

**P10 security and docs:** docs/security/threat-model.md, SECURITY.md, all ADRs, final CLAUDE.md, README, PROSE pass.

**P11 completion:** workerd full matrix, staging integration lane with GC armed, acceptance sign-off.

## ADRs to write

0001 R2-only storage, no database (carried). 0002 Writes through the worker; custom multipart (64 MiB parts, 1000-part cap, 94371800-byte single cap, x-cachet-upload-bytes header). 0003 Server-side signing; write-path hash verification is poison resistance. 0004 GitHub-only auth: OIDC for writes, device flow for laptops, browser OAuth + sessions as backend-only endpoints consumed by the later SPA; no shared read tokens. 0005 KV for auth verdicts only. 0006 Pure-rust/WebCrypto on wasm; ring/aws-lc/zstd-C banned with the wasm-hygiene gate. 0007 workers-rs; port contracts, not code. 0008 alchemy IaC, stage grammar, bundle:false seam + wrangler fallback. 0009 cargo-dist releases; the in-repo action wraps the released binary. 0010 Server canonicalizes and signs narinfos after verification. 0011 GC armed from day one; cursor-resumable cron driver; reports as API data. 0012 Edge-cache generation (carried). 0013 Deployment identity is configuration; key name `{host}-1`. 0014 RFC 9457 problem+json; error table extended, previous codes byte-stable. 0015 OpenAPI generated from code with derive macros; code is truth, yaml is committed and drift-checked, served bytes golden-locked. 0016 The flake is the interface; just verbs are CI parity. 0017 project == repository claim (hole fix). 0018 Verdict-cache TTLs define the revocation window. 0019 Laptops read-only; push lives in CLI + in-repo action. 0020 Upstream filter + file:// staging (carried). 0021 Signing-key custody: Secrets Store, rotate-by-redeploy, bootstrap env file 0600 + gitignored. 0022 CPU budget for hash verification (records the throughput measurement).

## Security deliverables

`docs/security/threat-model.md` covers ten scenarios, each written as attacker → defending mechanism → the lane or test that enforces it: external stranger poisoning (OIDC + org pinning), stolen user token (read-only scope + verdict TTL), forged or mis-scoped OIDC (RS256 pin, exact aud, project binding), forged signatures (Secrets Store custody, sign-only-after-verify typestate), tampered R2 bytes (hash-verified write pipeline), token exfiltration from a laptop disk (0600 file, GitHub revocation, verdict TTL), session theft (HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax cookie, 14-day TTL, 128-bit random ids, single-use oauth state, replay-refused callback; workerd cookie-flag and state-replay tests), log exfiltration (logs carry no credential fields; log-hygiene test scans emitted lines), GC as a deletion vector (lease binding, gates, grace window), supply chain (cargo deny, exact pins, dependabot, wasm-hygiene scan), signing-key extraction (Secrets Store never readable back; rotation via a dual trusted-public-key window). Subsections for upload-id bearer semantics and JWKS stale-fallback reasoning. Root SECURITY.md: disclosure channel, scope, supported versions.

## Docs layout

Root: README.md, CLAUDE.md (constitution + @-import manifest), SECURITY.md, PROSE.md (verbatim), LICENSE, JUSTFILE. docs/: contracts.md, DEPLOY.md, operations.md, openapi.yaml (generated), design/{architecture,worker,signing,auth,gc,cli,action,bootstrap,wire-formats}.md, security/threat-model.md, testing/{lanes.toml, unit,property,golden,kani,workerd,integration}.md, adr/0001-0022. None of these mention the template projects.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On a fresh Cloudflare account, `just bootstrap` produces a serving cache on a custom domain with no console steps beyond the printed checklists.
2. A laptop runs `cachet login --url` + `cachet setup`; a nix build substitutes from the deployment with signature verification on.
3. The in-repo action pushes from an org repo; an out-of-org repo and a mis-scoped audience are refused with the documented codes; pushes arrive unsigned, are stored signed, and `nix store verify --sigs-needed 1` passes with only the deployment public key. The browser OAuth flow is workerd-tested end to end against a stub GitHub: state replay refused, org gate enforced, cookie attributes correct, logout deletes the session.
4. Narinfo writes refuse hash-mismatched documents with the 400 codes in the spec; every rejection-matrix entry is generated into the spec and workerd-tested.
5. GC runs armed in staging on the Cloudflare cron; a zeroed-grace run deletes only unmarked grace-expired objects narinfo-first, bumps generation, and its reports are served by the API; every gate trip has a test.
6. All lanes and gates green; the wasm bundle free of ring/aws-lc/tokio symbols and secret-shaped strings; both manifest bijections green; `just openapi --check` clean.
7. /api/openapi.json validates and is byte-equal to the committed generated yaml; all error bodies RFC 9457.
8. Each of the ten threat-model scenarios names a passing mechanical check.
9. A tag publishes the four-triple `cachet` binary via cargo-dist; `action/` consumes exactly that artifact.
10. Integration lane on staging: the 126 MiB round trip through push and pull-verify passes with GC armed; the throughput measurement lands in ADR-0022.

Out of v1 scope: any rendered UI, the reproducibility verifier, D1 or any database, per-user accounts, S3 emulation, laptop push in the normal path, preview stages, Cloudflare Workflows, upstream write-through proxying (clients keep cache.nixos.org as a second substituter).

## Migration note

Key grammar and narinfo semantics are unchanged, so an existing deployment cuts over by redeploying against the same bucket and domain. Old narinfos keep their client-signed Sig lines and stay valid; laptop configs trust both the old key and the new deployment key during transition. Leases carry forward as-is; the first armed GC run is the first deletion such a bucket has ever seen, so its gates matter.

content.content:
1	//! cachet-api is the HTTP surface, expressed as typed bodies plus the
2	//! route descriptors the OpenAPI document is derived from (CLAUDE.md §1,
3	//! docs/openapi.yaml). The code is the source of truth: `just openapi`
4	//! regenerates docs/openapi.yaml from this crate and CI fails on drift.
5	//!
6	//! The response bodies the worker serializes live here as types so the
7	//! served wire and the published spec share one definition.
8	
9	#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
10	
11	pub mod routes;
12	
13	/// The `GET /api/public/config` body: everything a client needs to reach
14	/// the deployment's auth and verify its signatures, none of it secret.
15	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, utoipa::ToSchema)]
16	pub struct PublicConfig {
17	    /// The GitHub OAuth App's client id: a public value.
18	    #[serde(rename = "oauthClientId")]
19	    pub oauth_client_id: String,
20	    /// The GitHub orgs this deployment serves.
21	    pub orgs: Vec<String>,
22	    /// The deployment's host name, which is also its signing-key name
23	    /// prefix.
24	    pub host: String,
25	    /// The deployment's ed25519 public key in nix's `name:base64` form.
26	    #[serde(rename = "publicKey")]
27	    pub public_key: String,
28	}
29	
30	/// The `GET /roots` body: the projects currently holding leases.
31	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, utoipa::ToSchema)]
32	pub struct ProjectList {
33	    /// The hyphenated `owner-repo` project names.
34	    pub projects: Vec<String>,
35	}
36	
37	impl ProjectList {
38	    /// Serialize the listing. Stable bytes matter for the same reason the
39	    /// lease document's do: a diff between two runs must stay legible, so
40	    /// the keys emit in a fixed shape with a trailing newline.
41	    pub fn serialize(&self) -> String {
42	        let mut body = serde_json::to_string_pretty(self).expect("the listing serializes");
43	        body.push('\n');
44	        body
45	    }
46	}
47	
48	/// The `POST /roots/{project}` body: the store paths a project keeps
49	/// alive plus the installables that produced them.
50	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, utoipa::ToSchema)]
51	pub struct RenewalBody {
52	    /// The flake installables the job built.
53	    pub installables: Vec<String>,
54	    /// Full nix store paths whose closures must stay alive.
55	    #[serde(rename = "storePaths")]
56	    pub store_paths: Vec<String>,
57	}
58	
59	/// The `POST /nar/{key}?uploads` body: the new upload's bearer id and the
60	/// part plan the declaration bound.
61	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, utoipa::ToSchema)]
62	pub struct UploadCreated {
63	    /// The upload id: a bearer token naming one in-flight upload.
64	    #[serde(rename = "uploadId")]
65	    pub upload_id: String,
66	    /// How many parts the declared total implies.
67	    #[serde(rename = "expectedParts")]
68	    pub expected_parts: u64,
69	}
70	
71	/// The `PUT /nar/{key}?uploadId&partNumber` body: the stored part's
72	/// coordinates, which the completion body echoes back.
73	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, utoipa::ToSchema)]
74	pub struct UploadedPartBody {
75	    /// The one-based part number just stored.
76	    #[serde(rename = "partNumber")]
77	    pub part_number: u16,
78	    /// The storage layer's part etag.
79	    pub etag: String,
80	}
81	
82	/// `GET /api/self/gc-runs`: one page of run ids, oldest first.
83	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, utoipa::ToSchema)]
84	pub struct GcRunList {
85	    /// The run ids in chronological order.
86	    pub runs: Vec<String>,
87	    /// The cursor for the next page, when more runs exist.
88	    #[serde(
89	        rename = "nextCursor",
90	        default,
91	        skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"
92	    )]
93	    pub next_cursor: Option<String>,
94	}
95	
96	/// `GET /api/self/stats`: the cache's current shape, derived from the
97	/// newest completed report rather than recomputed live.
98	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, utoipa::ToSchema)]
99	pub struct StatsBody {
100	    /// The run the numbers came from.
101	    #[serde(rename = "basedOnRunId")]
102	    pub based_on_run_id: String,
103	    /// Narinfos in the bucket at that run's inventory.
104	    #[serde(rename = "inventoryPaths")]
105	    pub inventory_paths: u64,
106	    /// Narinfos its sweep deleted.
107	    #[serde(rename = "narinfosDeleted")]
108	    pub narinfos_deleted: u64,
109	    /// NAR objects its sweep deleted.
110	    #[serde(rename = "narsDeleted")]
111	    pub nars_deleted: u64,
112	    /// Bytes the sweep freed.
113	    #[serde(rename = "bytesFreed")]
114	    pub bytes_freed: u64,
115	    /// The gate the run aborted on, when one tripped.
116	    pub gate: Option<String>,
117	    /// When that run finished.
118	    #[serde(rename = "finishedAtMs")]
119	    pub finished_at_ms: u64,
120	}
121	
122	/// The RFC 9457 problem document every non-2xx answer carries. Described
123	/// here rather than serialized from it: the worker emits cachet-core's
124	/// problem writer, whose byte shape is golden-locked, and this type is
125	/// the document's schema for readers.
126	#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, utoipa::ToSchema)]
127	pub struct ProblemBody {
128	    /// Always `about:blank`.
129	    #[serde(rename = "type")]
130	    pub type_: String,

unsafe_code = "forbid"

missing_docs = "warn"
unused_must_use = "warn"
# why: `cfg(kani)` gates bounded-proof harnesses (docs/testing/kani.md) that

unexpected_cfgs = { level = "warn", check-cfg = ['cfg(kani)'] }

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
