# This is the published, public copy of the cachet-setup action. GitHub blocks a public repository
# from consuming an action that lives in a private one, and cachet is private, so a public consumer
# (for example agx-runtime/substrate-kernels) needs the action to live in a public repository. The
# canonical source and the build that produces post/dist/*.cjs live in the private agx-runtime/cachet
# repository under action/; a change is made there and copied here, so any drift is traceable to that
# one source.
name: cachet-setup
description: >-
    Install Determinate Nix, wire this job into the cachet binary cache, and push what the job builds.
author: loopholelabs
# A composite action cannot declare a post step, which is why the push lives in a nested JavaScript
# action below. This is the same shape cachix/cachix-action uses, for the same reason.

inputs:
    roots:
        description: >-
            Flake installables whose closures this project needs. Their outputs are pushed unconditionally
            and, on the default branch, become the project's garbage-collection lease.
        required: false
        default: ''
    signing-key:
        description: >-
            The NAR signing key, and the only org-level secret cachet needs. Pass the
            CACHET_SIGNING_KEY secret. Nix signs with it on this runner; it never reaches the cache.
        required: true
    cache-url:
        description: The cache's base URL.
        required: false
        # A metadata default, which is the one place a deployment hostname may appear (ADR 0013).
        default: https://pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io
    audience:
        description: The OIDC audience the cache requires.
        required: false
        default: cachet
    project:
        description: >-
            The lease name for this repository. Defaults to the owner and name joined by a hyphen
            (`my-org-my-repo`), which is unique across the organisations this cache serves — two
            repositories sharing a name would otherwise share a lease and overwrite each other's.
        required: false
        default: ''
    upstream-url:
        description: The upstream cache to filter against before pushing.
        required: false
        default: https://cache.nixos.org
    default-branch-ref:
        description: >-
            The ref permitted to renew the lease. The cache enforces this itself; this input only avoids a
            request that would be refused.
        required: false
        default: refs/heads/main
    trusted-public-key:
        description: >-
            The public half of the signing key, in Nix's `name:base64` form, so this job can verify what it
            substitutes from the cache.
        required: false
        # A metadata default, like `cache-url` above: the public key is deployment identity, not a
        # secret, and ADR 0013 makes action metadata the one place deployment identity may appear.
        # Without a default here every consuming repository would have to learn and paste the key,
        # and one that forgot would fail signature verification on every substitution — which Nix
        # reports as a cache miss, so the job would silently compile from source while the cache
        # looked healthy. The login script bakes in the same value (`public_key_default` in
        # scripts/cache-login.sh), so a laptop and a runner learn the key the same way.
        default: pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io-1:JC2XK3HyAUXteubthi/pUEM0iokE6YyOGFURMB4hsRE=
    push:
        description: Set to false to use the cache read-only.
        required: false
        default: 'true'
    determinate-nix-action-version:
        description: Which release of the Determinate Nix installer action to use.
        required: false
        default: v3

runs:
    using: composite
    steps:
        # Provision the cache read credential BEFORE Determinate is installed and its daemon starts.
        # Determinate synthesizes the netrc the daemon reads (/nix/var/determinate/netrc) at daemon start,
        # merging every file listed under authentication.additionalNetrcSources — and that start-up
        # synthesis is the only reliable one on these runners. A later re-synthesis is gated on the FlakeHub
        # login, whose transient failures otherwise leave cache reads at 401 and every build recompiling
        # from source. Writing the credential and the config here, before the daemon exists, means its
        # start-up synthesis merges the credential and the FlakeHub failure never gets to gate it
        # (docs.determinate.systems, migrate-to-flakehub-cache).
        - name: Provision the cachet read credential before Determinate starts
          shell: bash
          env:
              CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
              CACHET_AUDIENCE: ${{ inputs.audience }}
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail

              # The OIDC token authenticates this job; nothing is stored and the runner is authorised
              # because it is provably ours (docs/contracts.md). This is minted here, without Nix, because
              # Determinate is not installed yet.
              if [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ]; then
                echo "cachet: this job cannot mint an OIDC token." >&2
                echo "  Add 'permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }' to the job." >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              token="$(curl -fsSL \
                -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}" \
                "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=${CACHET_AUDIENCE}" | jq -r '.value')"
              host="$(printf '%s' "${CACHET_CACHE_URL}" | sed -e 's#^https\?://##' -e 's#/.*$##')"

              # The credential file: real, outside the Nix store, 0600, root-owned, as Determinate requires.
              sudo mkdir -p /etc/nix /etc/determinate
              printf 'machine %s login cachet password %s\n' "${host}" "${token}" \
                | sudo tee /etc/nix/netrc >/dev/null
              sudo chmod 600 /etc/nix/netrc

              # Register it under authentication.additionalNetrcSources. Determinate is not installed yet,
              # so the config usually does not exist; merge with jq when it does so anything the installer
              # pre-seeds survives.
              if [ -f /etc/determinate/config.json ]; then
                sudo cat /etc/determinate/config.json \
                  | jq '.authentication.additionalNetrcSources = ((.authentication.additionalNetrcSources // []) + ["/etc/nix/netrc"] | unique)' \
                  | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp >/dev/null
                sudo mv /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp /etc/determinate/config.json
              else
                printf '{"authentication":{"additionalNetrcSources":["/etc/nix/netrc"]}}\n' \
                  | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json >/dev/null
              fi
              echo "cachet: read credential provisioned before Determinate starts"

        # Determinate Nix is the one distribution everywhere, including on laptops (ADR 0008).
        - uses: DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@v3.21.9
          with:
              # Add the cache and its trusted key at install time, so the daemon starts already knowing
              # them. Adding them afterwards in the Configure step proved ineffective — the daemon never
              # queried cachet at all — because a substituter and its trusted key reach the daemon only when
              # it reads its config at start. extra-substituters and extra-trusted-public-keys accumulate
              # (they use the extra- prefix), so this adds cachet alongside cache.nixos.org rather than
              # replacing it.
              extra-conf: |
                  extra-substituters = ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
                  extra-trusted-public-keys = ${{ inputs.trusted-public-key }}

        # Log out of FlakeHub, which the determinate-nix-action step above logged into on its own. On a
        # runner granting id-token: write — which this action requires to mint its own cachet OIDC token —
        # Determinate mints a second OIDC token for FlakeHub and logs in, and that login adds
        # https://cache.flakehub.com to the daemon's active substituters. This deployment is not a FlakeHub
        # Cache customer, so every narinfo lookup then answers 401 ("User is not authorized for this
        # resource") before it falls through to cachet: an error-level log line and a wasted round trip on
        # every request, on a build that still succeeds. Logging out returns the substituter set to the
        # logged-out state, in which cache.flakehub.com is absent — verified against a local Determinate
        # install, where `determinate-nixd status` reports logged-out and `nix config show substituters`
        # omits FlakeHub. cachet's own read credential is the netrc merged from additionalNetrcSources and
        # is independent of the FlakeHub login, so the Configure step's auth probe below still reports 404.
        - name: Log out of FlakeHub Cache, which this deployment does not use
          shell: bash
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              # `|| true`: a job without id-token never logged in, so logout is a no-op there rather than a
              # failure, and this action must not fail a build over a cache it does not even use.
              sudo determinate-nixd auth logout || true
              echo "cachet: FlakeHub login status after logout:"
              sudo determinate-nixd status || true

        - name: Configure cachet
          shell: bash
          env:
              CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
              CACHET_AUDIENCE: ${{ inputs.audience }}
              CACHET_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ inputs.trusted-public-key }}
              CACHET_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ inputs.signing-key }}
              CACHET_PROJECT: ${{ inputs.project }}
              CACHET_ROOTS: ${{ inputs.roots }}
              CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL: ${{ inputs.upstream-url }}
              CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF: ${{ inputs.default-branch-ref }}
              CACHET_PUSH: ${{ inputs.push }}
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail

              # The read credential and its Determinate config were provisioned before the daemon started
              # (the first step of this action), so the daemon's start-up synthesis already merged the
              # credential into the netrc it reads. There is nothing to do here for the netrc.

              # The substituter and trusted key are added at install time now (the extra-conf on the
              # determinate-nix-action step above), so the daemon starts already knowing them. They are not
              # written here: a substituter added after the daemon has started is never consulted, which is
              # why the last run authenticated yet never queried cachet.

              # Confirm the daemon's netrc authenticates against cachet, so a regression surfaces in the log
              # rather than as a silent rebuild: a 404 means the credential is present and authenticated —
              # the probed path is simply absent — while a 401 means it is not.
              daemon_netrc="$(nix config show netrc-file 2>/dev/null || echo /nix/var/determinate/netrc)"
              probe_code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --netrc-file "${daemon_netrc}" \
                "${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}/0000000000000000000000000000000a.narinfo" 2>/dev/null || echo 000)"
              echo "cachet: read auth probe returned ${probe_code} (404 = authenticated, 401 = not)"

              # The signing key is written where only this runner can read it, and never leaves it (ADR 0004).
              key_file="${RUNNER_TEMP}/cachet-signing.key"
              printf '%s' "${CACHET_SIGNING_KEY}" > "${key_file}"
              chmod 600 "${key_file}"
              echo "CACHET_SIGNING_KEY_FILE=${key_file}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"

              # Everything the post step reads is exported to the job environment here, and this is the
              # only place any of it is resolved. A step-level `env:` block is scoped to the step it sits
              # on, so passing these to the nested action as `with:` inputs left the post step reading
              # empty strings and declining to push, silently, on every run.
              #
              # The project name defaults to owner-and-name rather than the bare repository name.
              #
              # why: this cache serves more than one organisation, so two repositories can share a name.
              # A lease is filed under the project name and a renewal replaces the previous document
              # wholesale, so two same-named repositories defaulting to one project would overwrite each
              # other's lease — and each would then stop protecting the other's closure, making live
              # paths collectable (Invariant GC-NEVER-EATS-THE-LIVING). Including the owner makes the
              # default unique by construction rather than by everyone remembering to pass `project`.
              project="${CACHET_PROJECT}"
              if [ -z "${project}" ]; then
                project="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY//\//-}"
              fi
              # why: the heredoc form rather than `NAME=value`. `roots` takes several installables and the
              # post step splits it on any whitespace, so a caller writing them one per line with a YAML
              # block scalar is using the documented shape — and a bare `NAME=value` line cannot express
              # a newline. GitHub rejects the whole file with "Invalid format" when it sees the
              # continuation, which fails the step for a reason that points nowhere near the cause.
              #
              # The delimiter is fixed and long enough not to occur in a flake installable, and the
              # values here are action inputs rather than anything a request supplies.
              env_file() {
                printf '%s<<CACHET_EOF_1c7f\n%s\nCACHET_EOF_1c7f\n' "$1" "$2" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
              }
              env_file CACHET_CACHE_URL "${CACHET_CACHE_URL}"
              env_file CACHET_AUDIENCE "${CACHET_AUDIENCE}"
              env_file CACHET_PROJECT "${project}"
              env_file CACHET_ROOTS "${CACHET_ROOTS}"
              env_file CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL "${CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL}"
              env_file CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF "${CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF}"
              env_file CACHET_PUSH "${CACHET_PUSH}"

              echo "cachet: configured ${CACHET_CACHE_URL} as a substituter for project ${project}"

        # The nested JavaScript action: its main step snapshots the store, and its post step, on success
        # only, does the push. It takes no inputs, because the step above resolved all of them into the
        # job environment.
        # why: the full owner/repo/path@ref form rather than `./post`. A composite action resolves a
        # relative `./post` against the consumer's GITHUB_WORKSPACE rather than this action's own
        # directory, so a cross-repo consumer looked for `<workspace>/post` and failed with "Can't find
        # 'action.yml' under .../post". Naming the repository resolves the nested action independently of
        # where the consumer checked out. It is pinned to the v1 major tag, which every release in the 1.x
        # line moves forward, so the composite and its post action always come from the same line.
        - uses: agx-runtime/cachet-action/post@v1
```

description: >-
    Snapshots the Nix store, then on job success pushes what was added and renews the lease. Not meant to
    be used directly — the cachet-setup composite action wraps it.

# why: no inputs. The cachet-setup composite resolves every value and exports it to the job environment,
# which is what both this action's steps read. Declaring them here as well would give the post step a
# second, differently-named source of the same configuration (GitHub exposes an input as `INPUT_<NAME>`,
# not as the name the code reads), and that mismatch is exactly the bug that made this step decline to
# push on every run while reporting success.

runs:
    using: node24
    main: dist/main.cjs
    post: dist/post.cjs
    # why: on success only. A failed build must never populate the cache or refresh a lease — that is what
    # keeps a broken artifact from becoming the one everybody substitutes.
    post-if: success()
```

Ordering within a job:

1. **Main time** (`dist/main.cjs` runs when the nested action step executes, i.e. immediately after "Configure cachet" and **before any of the consumer's subsequent steps**): run `nix path-info --all`, write entire store listing to the snapshot file, print `cachet: store snapshot taken`.
2. Consumer's own steps run (the build).
3. **Post time** (`dist/post.cjs`, only if the whole job succeeded so far — `post-if: success()`): read config from env → bail early if `CACHET_PUSH == "false"` or required vars missing → read snapshot file (missing → treated as empty before-set) → `nix path-info --all` → `storeDiff` (order-preserving set difference) → cap at 4096 paths → mint one OIDC token for probes → resolve each root installable with `nix path-info <installable>` → filter candidates against upstream (HEAD probes) excluding root paths from filtering → filter against cachet itself (HEAD probes, Bearer token) → if anything remains, `nix copy --to file://<staging>?compression=zstd&secret-key=<keyfile>` → upload NARs first, then narinfos → if default branch, `POST /roots/<project>` to renew the lease.

---

## 3. The OIDC dance

Hand-rolled in both places — **`@actions/core.getIDToken` is not used anywhere**; the bundles have no `@actions/*` imports at all.

**Main/composite mint (bash, before Nix exists)** — fails the step hard if the env vars are absent:

```bash
if [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ]; then
  echo "cachet: this job cannot mint an OIDC token." >&2
  echo "  Add 'permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }' to the job." >&2
  exit 1
fi
token="$(curl -fsSL \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}" \
  "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=${CACHET_AUDIENCE}" | jq -r '.value')"
```

The token goes straight into the netrc: `machine <host> login cachet password <token>` where `host` is `cache-url` with scheme and path stripped via sed.

**Post-step mint (TS, per request)** — verbatim from `post/dist/post.cjs`:

```js
async function requestIdToken(audience, env) {
  const requestUrl = env["ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL"];
  const requestToken = env["ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN"];
  if (requestUrl === undefined || requestToken === undefined) {
    return fail("no OIDC token request variables. Add `permissions: { id-token: write }` to the job.");
  }
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`${requestUrl}&audience=${encodeURIComponent(audience)}`, {
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${requestToken}` }
    });
    if (!response.ok) {
      return fail(`the OIDC token request returned ${String(response.status)}`);
    }
    const body = await response.json();
    if (typeof body.value !== "string" || body.value.length === 0) {
      return fail("the OIDC token response carried no token");
    }
    return ok(body.value);
  } catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "unknown failure";
    return fail(`the OIDC token request failed: ${message}`);
  }
}
```

Audience handling: appended as `&audience=<audience>` (URL-encoded in the TS version, raw in the bash version); the audience value is the `audience` input / `CACHET_AUDIENCE` env, default `cachet`.

Crucially, tokens are **minted fresh per request attempt**, not once per push. The upload target is:

```js
const target = {
  cacheUrl: inputs.cacheUrl,
  mintToken: () => requestIdToken(inputs.audience, process.env)
};
```

and every retried closure (see §6) begins with `const token = await target.mintToken();` — so a retry after a 401/403 gets a brand-new JWT. One exception: the upstream/cachet HEAD-probe pass mints a single token (`probe`) reused for all cachet probes.

---

## 4. Snapshot mechanism (action-level wiring)

**No `save-state` / `STATE_*` mechanism is used at all** (confirmed by grep — zero occurrences). The hand-off between main and post is a plain file in `RUNNER_TEMP`, which persists for the whole job:

```js
// action/post/src/snapshot-path.ts (duplicated into both bundles)
function snapshotPath(env) {
  return import_node_path.join(env["RUNNER_TEMP"] ?? "/tmp", "cachet-store-before.txt");
}
```

Entire `post/dist/main.cjs` (main-time snapshotter), verbatim logic:

```js
async function main() {
  const snapshot = await run(["nix", "path-info", "--all"]);
  if (!snapshot.ok) {
    process.stderr.write(`cachet: could not snapshot the store — nothing will be pushed. ${snapshot.message}\n`);
    return;
  }
  await import_promises.writeFile(snapshotPath(process.env), snapshot.value, "utf8");
  process.stdout.write(`cachet: store snapshot taken\n`);
}
main().catch((error) => {
  process.stderr.write(`cachet: the snapshot step failed unexpectedly: ${String(error)}\n`);
});
```

Post-side diff wiring:

```js
const before = parseSnapshot(await readFileOrEmpty(snapshotPath(process.env)));  // missing file -> "" -> empty set
const afterOutput = await run(["nix", "path-info", "--all"]);
...
const candidates = boundCandidates(storeDiff(before, parseSnapshot(afterOutput.value)));
```

`parseSnapshot` splits on newlines, trims, drops empties. `storeDiff` is a set-difference preserving first-appearance order. `boundCandidates` fails (swallowed, see §8) if additions exceed `PUSH_PATHS_MAX = ROOTS_PATHS_MAX = 4096`. A missing snapshot file silently makes *everything* in the store a candidate (degenerate push-everything mode), because `readFileOrEmpty` swallows ENOENT.

Supporting constants (`post/dist/post.cjs` top): `UPLOAD_SINGLE_MAX_BYTES = 94371840` (90 MiB), `UPLOAD_PART_BYTES = 67108864` (64 MiB), `MULTIPART_PARTS_MAX = 1000`, `UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX = 3`, `UPLOAD_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS = 500`, `FILTER_CONCURRENCY_MAX = 16`, `UPLOAD_TOTAL_BYTES_HEADER = "x-cachet-upload-bytes"`, `NAR_KEY_PREFIX = "nar/"`, `GRACE_WINDOW_DAYS = 14`, `LEASE_RETENTION_DAYS = 30`.

---

## 5. Cache host/URL and upstream-filter configuration

- **Cache URL:** `cache-url` input, default `https://pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io`. Path: input → `CACHET_CACHE_URL` (step env) → `$GITHUB_ENV` → post reads `env["CACHET_CACHE_URL"]`. Also used in the composite for the netrc `machine` line (scheme/path stripped) and the auth probe. It appears as `extra-substituters` in the Determinate install step.
- **Upstream-filter URL:** `upstream-url` input, default `https://cache.nixos.org` → `CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL` env. There is a second hardcoded fallback inside the post bundle: `var UPSTREAM_URL_DEFAULT = "https://cache.nixos.org";` used when the env var is absent (relevant only when someone runs the post action standalone).
- **Trusted public key** (for substitution verification): `trusted-public-key` input with the deployment default baked into metadata, injected at install time as `extra-trusted-public-keys`.

The read-auth probe in the Configure step (verbatim, as it's behaviorally load-bearing):

```bash
daemon_netrc="$(nix config show netrc-file 2>/dev/null || echo /nix/var/determinate/netrc)"
probe_code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --netrc-file "${daemon_netrc}" \
  "${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}/0000000000000000000000000000000a.narinfo" 2>/dev/null || echo 000)"
echo "cachet: read auth probe returned ${probe_code} (404 = authenticated, 401 = not)"
```

---

## 6. Token exchange — none. Direct OIDC-JWT auth on the worker's write endpoints

The action **never calls a token/mint endpoint on the worker**. The GitHub OIDC JWT itself is the Bearer credential for every write and every authenticated probe. Exact requests (all verbatim from `real/upload.ts` section of `post/dist/post.cjs`):

**Whole-object PUT** (objects ≤ 90 MiB):

```js
const response = await fetch(objectUrl(target, plan.object.key), {
  method: "PUT",
  headers: authHeaders(token.value, { "Content-Length": String(plan.object.sizeBytes) }),
  body: new Uint8Array(bytes.value)
});
// objectUrl = `${target.cacheUrl.replace(/\/+$/, "")}/${key}${query}`
// authHeaders = { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, ...extra }
```

**Multipart** (objects > 90 MiB; parts of exactly 64 MiB, final part = remainder; >1000 parts rejected by `planParts`):

```js
// begin:   POST {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploads        header x-cachet-upload-bytes: <totalBytes> -> JSON { uploadId }
// part:    PUT  {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploadId=<id>&partNumber=<n>   Content-Length: <partLen>   -> JSON part descriptor, accumulated
// complete:POST {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploadId=<id>   Content-Type: application/json, body = JSON.stringify(parts)
// abort:   DELETE {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploadId=<id>   fire-and-forget: `.catch(() => { return; })`
```

**Lease renewal:**

```js
const response = await fetch(`${target.cacheUrl.replace(/\/+$/, "")}/roots/${project}`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: authHeaders(token.value, { "Content-Type": "application/json" }),
  body: JSON.stringify({ storePaths, installables })
});
```

**Probes:** `HEAD {upstreamUrl}/{hash}.narinfo` (no auth; 404 → false, 2xx → true, anything else/network error → `undefined` = "unknown"); `HEAD {cacheUrl}/{hash}.narinfo` with `Authorization: Bearer` (same tri-state).

**Staging:** objects are produced by `nix copy --to "file://${stagingRoot}?compression=zstd&secret-key=${inputs.signingKeyFile}"` where `stagingRoot` is `mkdtemp(os.tmpdir() + "cachet-staging-")` and the key file is `$RUNNER_TEMP/cachet-signing.key`. `readStagingDirectory` collects `*.narinfo` files at the root (kind `narinfo`, key = filename) and everything under `nar/` (kind `nar`, key = `nar/<basename>`). **Upload order is all NARs first, then all narinfos** (`uploadOrder`), so a narinfo never lands before its NAR. `planUpload` picks single vs multipart by size; uploads are sequential (one object at a time).

The worker's error vocabulary is mapped in `STATUS_BY_CODE`: `malformed_key/malformed_narinfo/malformed_roots/malformed_auth/part_number_invalid/part_size_mismatch/complete_parts_mismatch → 400`, `unauthorized → 401`, `forbidden_org/forbidden_ref → 403`, `not_found/upload_unknown → 404`, `narinfo_nar_missing → 409`, `length_required → 411`, `body_too_large → 413`, `auth_unavailable/storage_unavailable → 503` — useful for matching server responses in your rewrite.

---

## 7. Lease renewal

**Gating, two layers:**
- Syntactic: `post-if: success()` on the nested action — renewal (and pushing) happens only on a green job.
- Branch: exact string equality between `GITHUB_REF` and `CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF` (default `refs/heads/main`):

```js
isDefaultBranch: isSameRef(env["GITHUB_REF"], env["CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF"])
...
function isSameRef(actual, expected) {
  if (actual === undefined || expected === undefined) return false;
  if (actual.length === 0 || expected.length === 0) return false;
  return actual === expected;
}
```

PR runs (`GITHUB_REF = refs/pull/N/merge`) and tag pushes never match. The `default-branch-ref` input description notes the worker enforces the ref too; the client check "only avoids a request that would be refused."

**Sequence:** renewal happens *after* the upload succeeds, at the very end of `push()`:

```js
if (!inputs.isDefaultBranch) {
  process.stdout.write(`cachet: not the default branch, so the lease is not renewed\n`);
  return;
}
const renewed = await postRoots(target, inputs.project, rootPaths, inputs.rootInstallables);
if (!renewed.ok) {
  process.stderr.write(`cachet: ${renewed.message}\n`);
  return;
}
process.stdout.write(`cachet: lease renewed for ${inputs.project}\n`);
```

`postRoots` is wrapped in the same 3-attempt retry (`withRetriesUsingRealSleep("renew the lease for ${project}", ...)`), with a fresh OIDC token per attempt.

**Project naming:** if `CACHET_PROJECT` is empty the composite resolves `project="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY//\//-}"` (e.g. `my-org-my-repo`) and exports that; the TS side treats an empty `CACHET_PROJECT` as a configuration error (`missingInputs` lists it) and declines to run at all. Rationale in the YAML comments: a renewal replaces the lease document wholesale, so two same-named repos across orgs would clobber each other's leases and make live paths collectable ("Invariant GC-NEVER-EATS-THE-LIVING").

**Root paths:** each installable in `CACHET_ROOTS` (whitespace-split) is resolved with `nix `path-info <installable>`; failures only log `cachet: could not resolve <i>; it will not be a lease root` to stderr and skip. Root paths are **exempt from upstream filtering** (`filterAgainstUpstream` partitions candidates into `rootCandidates` kept unconditionally vs `probeable`). Server-side constants embedded in the bundle: grace window 14 days, lease retention 30 days, roots cap 4096.

---

## 8. Error-handling philosophy

**The post step can never fail the job.** There is no `setFailed`, no `process.exitCode = 1`, no thrown escape — every error path does `process.stderr.write(\`cachet: ...\`)` (or `stdout.write` for informational lines) and `return`. Even the top-level `.catch` only logs: `cachet: the push failed unexpectedly: ${String(error)}`. Same for `main.cjs`. Missing snapshot file → empty before-set. Missing OIDC env vars → log and return. Missing required config (`CACHET_CACHE_URL`, `CACHET_PROJECT`, `CACHET_AUDIENCE`) → the composed `missingInputsMessage`:

```js
`cachet: nothing pushed, because ${missing.join(", ")} ` + `${missing.length === 1 ? "is" : "are"} unset. The cachet-setup composite action exports these ` + `to the job environment; if you are running the post action directly, set them yourself.\n`
```

Log vocabulary is a bare lowercase `cachet:` prefix — **no `::warning::` / `::error::` workflow commands anywhere**. Distinct fixed messages: `cachet: store snapshot taken`, `cachet: the job added nothing to the store`, `cachet: N not upstream, M already upstream[, K probes failed (kept)]`, `cachet: N new to cachet, M already cached[, K probes failed (kept)]`, `cachet: uploaded N objects`, `cachet: not the default branch, so the lease is not renewed`, `cachet: lease renewed for <project>`, `cachet: pushing is disabled for this job`, and all failure lines starting `cachet: <message>`.

**The one deliberate exception:** the composite's first step hard-`exit 1`s if `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` is unset — that fails the job, with the remediation printed (`permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }`). FlakeHub logout is explicitly `|| true` ("must not fail a build over a cache it does not even use").

**Retry policy** (verbatim):

```js
async function withRetries(what, attempt, sleep) {
  let last = "no attempt was made";
  for (let tries = 0; tries < UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX; tries += 1) {
    let result;
    try { result = await attempt(); }
    catch (error) { result = fail(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)); }
    if (result.ok) { return result; }
    last = result.message;
    if (tries + 1 < UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX) { await sleep(UPLOAD_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS * (tries + 1)); }
  }
  return fail(`${what} failed after ${String(UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX)} attempts: ${last}`);
}
```

3 attempts, **linear** backoff 500 ms then 1000 ms (not exponential), and each attempt re-mints the OIDC token. Applied to: whole PUT, multipart begin/part/complete, and lease renewal. Multipart part failures also abort the upload (`DELETE ?uploadId=`) before returning the failure. Probe failures are fail-open *toward the cache*: an unparseable path or a network/5xx probe answer is `undefined`, counted as `probeFailures`, and the path is **kept** for upload rather than dropped. Store-diff size over 4096 added paths aborts the push with `this job added N store paths, more than the 4096 cap`.

- **dist is checked in.** `post/dist/main.cjs` (56 lines) and `post/dist/post.cjs` (755 lines) are esbuild-style bundles whose headers name the original TS entry points (`action/post/src/main.ts`, `action/post/src/post.ts`). There is **no build or release workflow in this repo** — `.github/` contains only `dependabot.yml`. Canonical source and the bundling live in private `agx-runtime/cachet` under `action/`; changes are copied here (stated in the action.yml header and README).

---

## 10. Install steps / CLI provisioning

- **No `cachet` binary is installed** — there is no CLI. All cache-write logic is the checked-in node24 bundle; tooling used on the runner is just `nix` (from Determinate), `curl`, `jq`, `sudo`, `determinate-nixd`, and coreutils.
- **Nix itself** is installed by `DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@v3.21.9` with this `extra-conf` (so the daemon starts already trusting cachet):

```yaml
extra-conf: |
    extra-substituters = ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
    extra-trusted-public-keys = ${{ inputs.trusted-public-key }}
```

No checksums anywhere — version pinning of the nested action and of the Determinate installer is by git tag only.

- The nested-action indirection exists *solely* because composite actions can't declare `post:`. If your replacement wraps a released binary, you can keep the same two-file shape (a tiny node wrapper or a composite that downloads the binary into `$RUNNER_TEMP` in `main` and re-invokes in `post`), but the state hand-off model here is deliberately a **file in `RUNNER_TEMP`** (`cachet-store-before.txt`) plus **`$GITHUB_ENV` exports** — reproduce those two mechanisms and everything downstream (post-if: success(), env-based config in `post.cjs`) stays identical.

        # reports as a cache miss, so the job would silently compile from source while the cache
        # looked healthy. The login script bakes in the same value (`public_key_default` in
        # scripts/cache-login.sh), so a laptop and a runner learn the key the same way.
        default: pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io-1:JC2XK3HyAUXteubthi/pUEM0iokE6YyOGFURMB4hsRE=
    push:
        description: Set to false to use the cache read-only.
        required: false
        default: 'true'
    determinate-nix-action-version:
        description: Which release of the Determinate Nix installer action to use.
        required: false
        default: v3

runs:
    using: composite
    steps:
        # Provision the cache read credential BEFORE Determinate is installed and its daemon starts.
        # Determinate synthesizes the netrc the daemon reads (/nix/var/determinate/netrc) at daemon start,
        # merging every file listed under authentication.additionalNetrcSources — and that start-up
        # synthesis is the only reliable one on these runners. A later re-synthesis is gated on the FlakeHub
        # login, whose transient failures otherwise leave cache reads at 401 and every build recompiling
        # from source. Writing the credential and the config here, before the daemon exists, means its
        # start-up synthesis merges the credential and the FlakeHub failure never gets to gate it
        # (docs.determinate.systems, migrate-to-flakehub-cache).
        - name: Provision the cachet read credential before Determinate starts
          shell: bash
          env:
              CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
              CACHET_AUDIENCE: ${{ inputs.audience }}
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail

              # The OIDC token authenticates this job; nothing is stored and the runner is authorised
              # because it is provably ours (docs/contracts.md). This is minted here, without Nix, because
              # Determinate is not installed yet.
              if [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ]; then
                echo "cachet: this job cannot mint an OIDC token." >&2
                echo "  Add 'permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }' to the job." >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              token="$(curl -fsSL \
                -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}" \
                "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=${CACHET_AUDIENCE}" | jq -r '.value')"
              host="$(printf '%s' "${CACHET_CACHE_URL}" | sed -e 's#^https\?://##' -e 's#/.*$##')"

              # The credential file: real, outside the Nix store, 0600, root-owned, as Determinate requires.
              sudo mkdir -p /etc/nix /etc/determinate
              printf 'machine %s login cachet password %s\n' "${host}" "${token}" \
                | sudo tee /etc/nix/netrc >/dev/null
              sudo chmod 600 /etc/nix/netrc

              # Register it under authentication.additionalNetrcSources. Determinate is not installed yet,
              # so the config usually does not exist; merge with jq when it does so anything the installer
              # pre-seeds survives.
              if [ -f /etc/determinate/config.json ]; then
                sudo cat /etc/determinate/config.json \
                  | jq '.authentication.additionalNetrcSources = ((.authentication.additionalNetrcSources // []) + ["/etc/nix/netrc"] | unique)' \
                  | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp >/dev/null
                sudo mv /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp /etc/determinate/config.json
              else
                printf '{"authentication":{"additionalNetrcSources":["/etc/nix/netrc"]}}\n' \
                  | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json >/dev/null
              fi
              echo "cachet: read credential provisioned before Determinate starts"

        # Determinate Nix is the one distribution everywhere, including on laptops (ADR 0008).
        - uses: DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@v3.21.9
          with:
              # Add the cache and its trusted key at install time, so the daemon starts already knowing
              # them. Adding them afterwards in the Configure step proved ineffective — the daemon never
              # queried cachet at all — because a substituter and its trusted key reach the daemon only when
              # it reads its config at start. extra-substituters and extra-trusted-public-keys accumulate
              # (they use the extra- prefix), so this adds cachet alongside cache.nixos.org rather than
              # replacing it.
              extra-conf: |
                  extra-substituters = ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
                  extra-trusted-public-keys = ${{ inputs.trusted-public-key }}

        # Log out of FlakeHub, which the determinate-nix-action step above logged into on its own. On a
        # runner granting id-token: write — which this action requires to mint its own cachet OIDC token —
        # Determinate mints a second OIDC token for FlakeHub and logs in, and that login adds
        # https://cache.flakehub.com to the daemon's active substituters. This deployment is not a FlakeHub
        # Cache customer, so every narinfo lookup then answers 401 ("User is not authorized for this
        # resource") before it falls through to cachet: an error-level log line and a wasted round trip on
        # every request, on a build that still succeeds. Logging out returns the substituter set to the
        # logged-out state, in which cache.flakehub.com is absent — verified against a local Determinate
        # install, where `determinate-nixd status` reports logged-out and `nix config show substituters`
        # omits FlakeHub. cachet's own read credential is the netrc merged from additionalNetrcSources and
        # is independent of the FlakeHub login, so the Configure step's auth probe below still reports 404.
        - name: Log out of FlakeHub Cache, which this deployment does not use
          shell: bash
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              # `|| true`: a job without id-token never logged in, so logout is a no-op there rather than a
              # failure, and this action must not fail a build over a cache it does not even use.
              sudo determinate-nixd auth logout || true
              echo "cachet: FlakeHub login status after logout:"
              sudo determinate-nixd status || true

        - name: Configure cachet
          shell: bash
          env:
              CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
              CACHET_AUDIENCE: ${{ inputs.audience }}
              CACHET_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ inputs.trusted-public-key }}
              CACHET_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ inputs.signing-key }}
              CACHET_PROJECT: ${{ inputs.project }}
              CACHET_ROOTS: ${{ inputs.roots }}
              CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL: ${{ inputs.upstream-url }}
              CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF: ${{ inputs.default-branch-ref }}
              CACHET_PUSH: ${{ inputs.push }}
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail

              # The read credential and its Determinate config were provisioned before the daemon started
              # (the first step of this action), so the daemon's start-up synthesis already merged the
              # credential into the netrc it reads. There is nothing to do here for the netrc.

              # The substituter and trusted key are added at install time now (the extra-conf on the
              # determinate-nix-action step above), so the daemon starts already knowing them. They are not
              # written here: a substituter added after the daemon has started is never consulted, which is
              # why the last run authenticated yet never queried cachet.

              # Confirm the daemon's netrc authenticates against cachet, so a regression surfaces in the log
              # rather than as a silent rebuild: a 404 means the credential is present and authenticated —
              # the probed path is simply absent — while a 401 means it is not.
              daemon_netrc="$(nix config show netrc-file 2>/dev/null || echo /nix/var/determinate/netrc)"
              probe_code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --netrc-file "${daemon_netrc}" \
                "${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}/0000000000000000000000000000000a.narinfo" 2>/dev/null || echo 000)"
              echo "cachet: read auth probe returned ${probe_code} (404 = authenticated, 401 = not)"

              # The signing key is written where only this runner can read it, and never leaves it (ADR 0004).
              key_file="${RUNNER_TEMP}/cachet-signing.key"
              printf '%s' "${CACHET_SIGNING_KEY}" > "${key_file}"
              chmod 600 "${key_file}"
              echo "CACHET_SIGNING_KEY_FILE=${key_file}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"

              # Everything the post step reads is exported to the job environment here, and this is the
              # only place any of it is resolved. A step-level `env:` block is scoped to the step it sits
              # on, so passing these to the nested action as `with:` inputs left the post step reading
              # empty strings and declining to push, silently, on every run.
              #
              # The project name defaults to owner-and-name rather than the bare repository name.
              #
              # why: this cache serves more than one organisation, so two repositories can share a name.
              # A lease is filed under the project name and a renewal replaces the previous document
              # wholesale, so two same-named repositories defaulting to one project would overwrite each
              # other's lease — and each would then stop protecting the other's closure, making live
              # paths collectable (Invariant GC-NEVER-EATS-THE-LIVING). Including the owner makes the
              # default unique by construction rather than by everyone remembering to pass `project`.
              project="${CACHET_PROJECT}"
              if [ -z "${project}" ]; then
                project="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY//\//-}"
              fi
              # why: the heredoc form rather than `NAME=value`. `roots` takes several installables and the
              # post step splits it on any whitespace, so a caller writing them one per line with a YAML
              # block scalar is using the documented shape — and a bare `NAME=value` line cannot express
              # a newline. GitHub rejects the whole file with "Invalid format" when it sees the
              # continuation, which fails the step for a reason that points nowhere near the cause.
              #
              # The delimiter is fixed and long enough not to occur in a flake installable, and the
              # values here are action inputs rather than anything a request supplies.
              env_file() {
                printf '%s<<CACHET_EOF_1c7f\n%s\nCACHET_EOF_1c7f\n' "$1" "$2" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
              }
              env_file CACHET_CACHE_URL "${CACHET_CACHE_URL}"
              env_file CACHET_AUDIENCE "${CACHET_AUDIENCE}"
              env_file CACHET_PROJECT "${project}"
              env_file CACHET_ROOTS "${CACHET_ROOTS}"
              env_file CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL "${CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL}"
              env_file CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF "${CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF}"
              env_file CACHET_PUSH "${CACHET_PUSH}"

              echo "cachet: configured ${CACHET_CACHE_URL} as a substituter for project ${project}"

        # The nested JavaScript action: its main step snapshots the store, and its post step, on success
        # only, does the push. It takes no inputs, because the step above resolved all of them into the
        # job environment.
        # why: the full owner/repo/path@ref form rather than `./post`. A composite action resolves a
        # relative `./post` against the consumer's GITHUB_WORKSPACE rather than this action's own
        # directory, so a cross-repo consumer looked for `<workspace>/post` and failed with "Can't find
        # 'action.yml' under .../post". Naming the repository resolves the nested action independently of
        # where the consumer checked out. It is pinned to the v1 major tag, which every release in the 1.x
        # line moves forward, so the composite and its post action always come from the same line.
        - uses: agx-runtime/cachet-action/post@v1
```

## 2. Nested post action structure and ordering

`/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet-action/post/action.yml` in full:

```yaml
name: cachet-push
description: >-
    Snapshots the Nix store, then on job success pushes what was added and renews the lease. Not meant to
    be used directly — the cachet-setup composite action wraps it.

# why: no inputs. The cachet-setup composite resolves every value and exports it to the job environment,
# which is what both this action's steps read. Declaring them here as well would give the post step a
# second, differently-named source of the same configuration (GitHub exposes an input as `INPUT_<NAME>`,
# not as the name the code reads), and that mismatch is exactly the bug that made this step decline to
# push on every run while reporting success.

runs:
    using: node24
    main: dist/main.cjs
    post: dist/post.cjs
    # why: on success only. A failed build must never populate the cache or refresh a lease — that is what
    # keeps a broken artifact from becoming the one everybody substitutes.
    post-if: success()
```

Ordering within a job:

1. **Main time** (`dist/main.cjs` runs when the nested action step executes, i.e. immediately after "Configure cachet" and **before any of the consumer's subsequent steps**): run `nix path-info --all`, write entire store listing to the snapshot file, print `cachet: store snapshot taken`.
2. Consumer's own steps run (the build).
3. **Post time** (`dist/post.cjs`, only if the whole job succeeded so far — `post-if: success()`): read config from env → bail early if `CACHET_PUSH == "false"` or required vars missing → read snapshot file (missing → treated as empty before-set) → `nix path-info --all` → `storeDiff` (order-preserving set difference) → cap at 4096 paths → mint one OIDC token for probes → resolve each root installable with `nix path-info <installable>` → filter candidates against upstream (HEAD probes) excluding root paths from filtering → filter against cachet itself (HEAD probes, Bearer token) → if anything remains, `nix copy --to file://<staging>?compression=zstd&secret-key=<keyfile>` → upload NARs first, then narinfos → if default branch, `POST /roots/<project>` to renew the lease.

## 3. The OIDC dance

Hand-rolled in both places — **`@actions/core.getIDToken` is not used anywhere**; the bundles have no `@actions/*` imports at all.

**Main/composite mint (bash, before Nix exists)** — fails the step hard if the env vars are absent:

```bash
if [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ]; then
  echo "cachet: this job cannot mint an OIDC token." >&2
  echo "  Add 'permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }' to the job." >&2
  exit 1
fi
token="$(curl -fsSL \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}" \
  "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=${CACHET_AUDIENCE}" | jq -r '.value')"
```

The token goes straight into the netrc: `machine <host> login cachet password <token>` where `host` is `cache-url` with scheme and path stripped via sed.

**Post-step mint (TS, per request)** — verbatim from `post/dist/post.cjs`:

```js
async function requestIdToken(audience, env) {
  const requestUrl = env["ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL"];
  const requestToken = env["ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN"];
  if (requestUrl === undefined || requestToken === undefined) {
    return fail("no OIDC token request variables. Add `permissions: { id-token: write }` to the job.");
  }
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`${requestUrl}&audience=${encodeURIComponent(audience)}`, {
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${requestToken}` }
    });
    if (!response.ok) {
      return fail(`the OIDC token request returned ${String(response.status)}`);
    }
    const body = await response.json();
    if (typeof body.value !== "string" || body.value.length === 0) {
      return fail("the OIDC token response carried no token");
    }
    return ok(body.value);
  } catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "unknown failure";
    return fail(`the OIDC token request failed: ${message}`);
  }
}
```

Audience handling: appended as `&audience=<audience>` (URL-encoded in the TS version, raw in the bash version); the audience value is the `audience` input / `CACHET_AUDIENCE` env, default `cachet`.

Crucially, tokens are **minted fresh per request attempt**, not once per push. The upload target is:

```js
const target = {
  cacheUrl: inputs.cacheUrl,
  mintToken: () => requestIdToken(inputs.audience, process.env)
};
```

and every retried closure (see §6) begins with `const token = await target.mintToken();` — so a retry after a 401/403 gets a brand-new JWT. One exception: the upstream/cachet HEAD-probe pass mints a single token (`probe`) reused for all cachet probes.

## 4. Snapshot mechanism (action-level wiring)

**No `save-state` / `STATE_*` mechanism is used at all** (confirmed by grep — zero occurrences). The hand-off between main and post is a plain file in `RUNNER_TEMP`, which persists for the whole job:

```js
// action/post/src/snapshot-path.ts (duplicated into both bundles)
function snapshotPath(env) {
  return import_node_path.join(env["RUNNER_TEMP"] ?? "/tmp", "cachet-store-before.txt");
}
```

Entire `post/dist/main.cjs` (main-time snapshotter), verbatim logic:

```js
async function main() {
  const snapshot = await run(["nix", "path-info", "--all"]);
  if (!snapshot.ok) {
    process.stderr.write(`cachet: could not snapshot the store — nothing will be pushed. ${snapshot.message}\n`);
    return;
  }
  await import_promises.writeFile(snapshotPath(process.env), snapshot.value, "utf8");
  process.stdout.write(`cachet: store snapshot taken\n`);
}
main().catch((error) => {
  process.stderr.write(`cachet: the snapshot step failed unexpectedly: ${String(error)}\n`);
});
```

Post-side diff wiring:

```js
const before = parseSnapshot(await readFileOrEmpty(snapshotPath(process.env)));  // missing file -> "" -> empty set
const afterOutput = await run(["nix", "path-info", "--all"]);
...
const candidates = boundCandidates(storeDiff(before, parseSnapshot(afterOutput.value)));
```

`parseSnapshot` splits on newlines, trims, drops empties. `storeDiff` is a set-difference preserving first-appearance order. `boundCandidates` fails (swallowed, see §8) if additions exceed `PUSH_PATHS_MAX = ROOTS_PATHS_MAX = 4096`. A missing snapshot file silently makes *everything* in the store a candidate (degenerate push-everything mode), because `readFileOrEmpty` swallows ENOENT.

Supporting constants (`post/dist/post.cjs` top): `UPLOAD_SINGLE_MAX_BYTES = 94371840` (90 MiB), `UPLOAD_PART_BYTES = 67108864` (64 MiB), `MULTIPART_PARTS_MAX = 1000`, `UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX = 3`, `UPLOAD_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS = 500`, `FILTER_CONCURRENCY_MAX = 16`, `UPLOAD_TOTAL_BYTES_HEADER = "x-cachet-upload-bytes"`, `NAR_KEY_PREFIX = "nar/"`, `GRACE_WINDOW_DAYS = 14`, `LEASE_RETENTION_DAYS = 30`.

## 5. Cache host/URL and upstream-filter configuration

- **Cache URL:** `cache-url` input, default `https://pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io`. Path: input → `CACHET_CACHE_URL` (step env) → `$GITHUB_ENV` → post reads `env["CACHET_CACHE_URL"]`. Also used in the composite for the netrc `machine` line (scheme/path stripped) and the auth probe. It appears as `extra-substituters` in the Determinate install step.
- **Upstream-filter URL:** `upstream-url` input, default `https://cache.nixos.org` → `CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL` env. There is a second hardcoded fallback inside the post bundle: `var UPSTREAM_URL_DEFAULT = "https://cache.nixos.org";` used when the env var is absent (relevant only when someone runs the post action standalone).
- **Trusted public key** (for substitution verification): `trusted-public-key` input with the deployment default baked into metadata, injected at install time as `extra-trusted-public-keys`.

The read-auth probe in the Configure step (verbatim, as it's behaviorally load-bearing):

```bash
daemon_netrc="$(nix config show netrc-file 2>/dev/null || echo /nix/var/determinate/netrc)"
probe_code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --netrc-file "${daemon_netrc}" \
  "${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}/0000000000000000000000000000000a.narinfo" 2>/dev/null || echo 000)"
echo "cachet: read auth probe returned ${probe_code} (404 = authenticated, 401 = not)"
```

## 6. Token exchange — none. Direct OIDC-JWT auth on the worker's write endpoints

The action **never calls a token/mint endpoint on the worker**. The GitHub OIDC JWT itself is the Bearer credential for every write and every authenticated probe. Exact requests (all verbatim from `real/upload.ts` section of `post/dist/post.cjs`):

**Whole-object PUT** (objects ≤ 90 MiB):

```js
const response = await fetch(objectUrl(target, plan.object.key), {
  method: "PUT",
  headers: authHeaders(token.value, { "Content-Length": String(plan.object.sizeBytes) }),
  body: new Uint8Array(bytes.value)
});
// objectUrl = `${target.cacheUrl.replace(/\/+$/, "")}/${key}${query}`
// authHeaders = { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, ...extra }
```

**Multipart** (objects > 90 MiB; parts of exactly 64 MiB, final part = remainder; >1000 parts rejected by `planParts`):

```js
// begin:   POST {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploads        header x-cachet-upload-bytes: <totalBytes> -> JSON { uploadId }
// part:    PUT  {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploadId=<id>&partNumber=<n>   Content-Length: <partLen>   -> JSON part descriptor, accumulated
// complete:POST {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploadId=<id>   Content-Type: application/json, body = JSON.stringify(parts)
// abort:   DELETE {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploadId=<id>   fire-and-forget: `.catch(() => { return; })`
```

**Lease renewal:**

```js
const response = await fetch(`${target.cacheUrl.replace(/\/+$/, "")}/roots/${project}`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: authHeaders(token.value, { "Content-Type": "application/json" }),
  body: JSON.stringify({ storePaths, installables })
});
```

**Probes:** `HEAD {upstreamUrl}/{hash}.narinfo` (no auth; 404 → false, 2xx → true, anything else/network error → `undefined` = "unknown"); `HEAD {cacheUrl}/{hash}.narinfo` with `Authorization: Bearer` (same tri-state).

**Staging:** objects are produced by `nix copy --to "file://${stagingRoot}?compression=zstd&secret-key=${inputs.signingKeyFile}"` where `stagingRoot` is `mkdtemp(os.tmpdir() + "cachet-staging-")` and the key file is `$RUNNER_TEMP/cachet-signing.key`. `readStagingDirectory` collects `*.narinfo` files at the root (kind `narinfo`, key = filename) and everything under `nar/` (kind `nar`, key = `nar/<basename>`). **Upload order is all NARs first, then all narinfos** (`uploadOrder`), so a narinfo never lands before its NAR. `planUpload` picks single vs multipart by size; uploads are sequential (one object at a time).

The worker's error vocabulary is mapped in `STATUS_BY_CODE`: `malformed_key/malformed_narinfo/malformed_roots/malformed_auth/part_number_invalid/part_size_mismatch/complete_parts_mismatch → 400`, `unauthorized → 401`, `forbidden_org/forbidden_ref → 403`, `not_found/upload_unknown → 404`, `narinfo_nar_missing → 409`, `length_required → 411`, `body_too_large → 413`, `auth_unavailable/storage_unavailable → 503` — useful for matching server responses in your rewrite.

## 7. Lease renewal

**Gating, two layers:**
- Syntactic: `post-if: success()` on the nested action — renewal (and pushing) happens only on a green job.
- Branch: exact string equality between `GITHUB_REF` and `CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF` (default `refs/heads/main`):

```js
isDefaultBranch: isSameRef(env["GITHUB_REF"], env["CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF"])
...
function isSameRef(actual, expected) {
  if (actual === undefined || expected === undefined) return false;
  if (actual.length === 0 || expected.length === 0) return false;
  return actual === expected;
}
```

PR runs (`GITHUB_REF = refs/pull/N/merge`) and tag pushes never match. The `default-branch-ref` input description notes the worker enforces the ref too; the client check "only avoids a request that would be refused."

**Sequence:** renewal happens *after* the upload succeeds, at the very end of `push()`:

```js
if (!inputs.isDefaultBranch) {
  process.stdout.write(`cachet: not the default branch, so the lease is not renewed\n`);
  return;
}
const renewed = await postRoots(target, inputs.project, rootPaths, inputs.rootInstallables);
if (!renewed.ok) {
  process.stderr.write(`cachet: ${renewed.message}\n`);
  return;
}
process.stdout.write(`cachet: lease renewed for ${inputs.project}\n`);
```

`postRoots` is wrapped in the same 3-attempt retry (`withRetriesUsingRealSleep("renew the lease for ${project}", ...)`), with a fresh OIDC token per attempt.

**Project naming:** if `CACHET_PROJECT` is empty the composite resolves `project="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY//\//-}"` (e.g. `my-org-my-repo`) and exports that; the TS side treats an empty `CACHET_PROJECT` as a configuration error (`missingInputs` lists it) and declines to run at all. Rationale in the YAML comments: a renewal replaces the lease document wholesale, so two same-named repos across orgs would clobber each other's leases and make live paths collectable ("Invariant GC-NEVER-EATS-THE-LIVING").

**Root paths:** each installable in `CACHET_ROOTS` (whitespace-split) is resolved with `nix `path-info <installable>`; failures only log `cachet: could not resolve <i>; it will not be a lease root` to stderr and skip. Root paths are **exempt from upstream filtering** (`filterAgainstUpstream` partitions candidates into `rootCandidates` kept unconditionally vs `probeable`). Server-side constants embedded in the bundle: grace window 14 days, lease retention 30 days, roots cap 4096.

## 8. Error-handling philosophy

**The post step can never fail the job.** There is no `setFailed`, no `process.exitCode = 1`, no thrown escape — every error path does `process.stderr.write(\`cachet: ...\`)` (or `stdout.write` for informational lines) and `return`. Even the top-level `.catch` only logs: `cachet: the push failed unexpectedly: ${String(error)}`. Same for `main.cjs`. Missing snapshot file → empty before-set. Missing OIDC env vars → log and return. Missing required config (`CACHET_CACHE_URL`, `CACHET_PROJECT`, `CACHET_AUDIENCE`) → the composed `missingInputsMessage`:

```js
`cachet: nothing pushed, because ${missing.join(", ")} ` + `${missing.length === 1 ? "is" : "are"} unset. The cachet-setup composite action exports these ` + `to the job environment; if you are running the post action directly, set them yourself.\n`
```

Log vocabulary is a bare lowercase `cachet:` prefix — **no `::warning::` / `::error::` workflow commands anywhere**. Distinct fixed messages: `cachet: store snapshot taken`, `cachet: the job added nothing to the store`, `cachet: N not upstream, M already upstream[, K probes failed (kept)]`, `cachet: N new to cachet, M already cached[, K probes failed (kept)]`, `cachet: uploaded N objects`, `cachet: not the default branch, so the lease is not renewed`, `cachet: lease renewed for <project>`, `cachet: pushing is disabled for this job`, and all failure lines starting `cachet: <message>`.

**The one deliberate exception:** the composite's first step hard-`exit 1`s if `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` is unset — that fails the job, with the remediation printed (`permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }`). FlakeHub logout is explicitly `|| true` ("must not fail a build over a cache it does not even use").

**Retry policy** (verbatim):

```js
async function withRetries(what, attempt, sleep) {
  let last = "no attempt was made";
  for (let tries = 0; tries < UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX; tries += 1) {
    let result;
    try { result = await attempt(); }
    catch (error) { result = fail(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)); }
    if (result.ok) { return result; }
    last = result.message;
    if (tries + 1 < UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX) { await sleep(UPLOAD_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS * (tries + 1)); }
  }
  return fail(`${what} failed after ${String(UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX)} attempts: ${last}`);
}
```

3 attempts, **linear** backoff 500 ms then 1000 ms (not exponential), and each attempt re-mints the OIDC token. Applied to: whole PUT, multipart begin/part/complete, and lease renewal. Multipart part failures also abort the upload (`DELETE ?uploadId=`) before returning the failure. Probe failures are fail-open *toward the cache*: an unparseable path or a network/5xx probe answer is `undefined`, counted as `probeFailures`, and the path is **kept** for upload rather than dropped. Store-diff size over 4096 added paths aborts the push with `this job added N store paths, more than the 4096 cap`.

```yaml
# This is the published, public copy of the cachet-setup action. GitHub blocks a public repository
# from consuming an action that lives in a private one, and cachet is private, so a public consumer
# (for example agx-runtime/substrate-kernels) needs the action to live in a public repository. The
# canonical source and the build that produces post/dist/*.cjs live in the private agx-runtime/cachet
# repository under action/; a change is made there and copied here, so any drift is traceable to that
# one source.
name: cachet-setup
description: >-
    Install Determinate Nix, wire this job into the cachet binary cache, and push what the job builds.
author: loopholelabs
# A composite action cannot declare a post step, which is why the push lives in a nested JavaScript
# action below. This is the same shape cachix/cachix-action uses, for the same reason.

inputs:
    roots:
        description: >-
            Flake installables whose closures this project needs. Their outputs are pushed unconditionally
            and, on the default branch, become the project's garbage-collection lease.
        required: false
        default: ''
    signing-key:
        description: >-
            The NAR signing key, and the only org-level secret cachet needs. Pass the
            CACHET_SIGNING_KEY secret. Nix signs with it on this runner; it never reaches the cache.
        required: true
    cache-url:
        description: The cache's base URL.
        required: false
        # A metadata default, which is the one place a deployment hostname may appear (ADR 0013).
        default: https://pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io
    audience:
        description: The OIDC audience the cache requires.
        required: false
        default: cachet
    project:
        description: >-
            The lease name for this repository. Defaults to the owner and name joined by a hyphen
            (`my-org-my-repo`), which is unique across the organisations this cache serves — two
            repositories sharing a name would otherwise share a lease and overwrite each other's.
        required: false
        default: ''
    upstream-url:
        description: The upstream cache to filter against before pushing.
        required: false
        default: https://cache.nixos.org
    default-branch-ref:
        description: >-
            The ref permitted to renew the lease. The cache enforces this itself; this input only avoids a
            request that would be refused.
        required: false
        default: refs/heads/main
    trusted-public-key:
        description: >-
            The public half of the signing key, in Nix's `name:base64` form, so this job can verify what it
            substitutes from the cache.
        required: false
        # A metadata default, like `cache-url` above: the public key is deployment identity, not a
        # secret, and ADR 0013 makes action metadata the one place deployment identity may appear.
        # Without a default here every consuming repository would have to learn and paste the key,
        # and one that forgot would fail signature verification on every substitution — which Nix
        # reports as a cache miss, so the job would silently compile from source while the cache
        # looked healthy. The login script bakes in the same value (`public_key_default` in
        # scripts/cache-login.sh), so a laptop and a runner learn the key the same way.
        default: pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io-1:JC2XK3HyAUXteubthi/pUEM0iokE6YyOGFURMB4hsRE=
    push:
        description: Set to false to use the cache read-only.
        required: false
        default: 'true'
    determinate-nix-action-version:
        description: Which release of the Determinate Nix installer action to use.
        required: false
        default: v3

runs:
    using: composite
    steps:
        # Provision the cache read credential BEFORE Determinate is installed and its daemon starts.
        # Determinate synthesizes the netrc the daemon reads (/nix/var/determinate/netrc) at daemon start,
        # merging every file listed under authentication.additionalNetrcSources — and that start-up
        # synthesis is the only reliable one on these runners. A later re-synthesis is gated on the FlakeHub
        # login, whose transient failures otherwise leave cache reads at 401 and every build recompiling
        # from source. Writing the credential and the config here, before the daemon exists, means its
        # start-up synthesis merges the credential and the FlakeHub failure never gets to gate it
        # (docs.determinate.systems, migrate-to-flakehub-cache).
        - name: Provision the cachet read credential before Determinate starts
          shell: bash
          env:
              CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
              CACHET_AUDIENCE: ${{ inputs.audience }}
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail

              # The OIDC token authenticates this job; nothing is stored and the runner is authorised
              # because it is provably ours (docs/contracts.md). This is minted here, without Nix, because
              # Determinate is not installed yet.
              if [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ]; then
                echo "cachet: this job cannot mint an OIDC token." >&2
                echo "  Add 'permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }' to the job." >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              token="$(curl -fsSL \
                -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}" \
                "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=${CACHET_AUDIENCE}" | jq -r '.value')"
              host="$(printf '%s' "${CACHET_CACHE_URL}" | sed -e 's#^https\?://##' -e 's#/.*$##')"

              # The credential file: real, outside the Nix store, 0600, root-owned, as Determinate requires.
              sudo mkdir -p /etc/nix /etc/determinate
              printf 'machine %s login cachet password %s\n' "${host}" "${token}" \
                | sudo tee /etc/nix/netrc >/dev/null
              sudo chmod 600 /etc/nix/netrc

              # Register it under authentication.additionalNetrcSources. Determinate is not installed yet,
              # so the config usually does not exist; merge with jq when it does so anything the installer
              # pre-seeds survives.
              if [ -f /etc/determinate/config.json ]; then
                sudo cat /etc/determinate/config.json \
                  | jq '.authentication.additionalNetrcSources = ((.authentication.additionalNetrcSources // []) + ["/etc/nix/netrc"] | unique)' \
                  | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp >/dev/null
                sudo mv /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp /etc/determinate/config.json
              else
                printf '{"authentication":{"additionalNetrcSources":["/etc/nix/netrc"]}}\n' \
                  | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json >/dev/null
              fi
              echo "cachet: read credential provisioned before Determinate starts"

        # Determinate Nix is the one distribution everywhere, including on laptops (ADR 0008).
        - uses: DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@v3.21.9
          with:
              # Add the cache and its trusted key at install time, so the daemon starts already knowing
              # them. Adding them afterwards in the Configure step proved ineffective — the daemon never
              # queried cachet at all — because a substituter and its trusted key reach the daemon only when
              # it reads its config at start. extra-substituters and extra-trusted-public-keys accumulate
              # (they use the extra- prefix), so this adds cachet alongside cache.nixos.org rather than
              # replacing it.
              extra-conf: |
                  extra-substituters = ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
                  extra-trusted-public-keys = ${{ inputs.trusted-public-key }}

        # Log out of FlakeHub, which the determinate-nix-action step above logged into on its own. On a
        # runner granting id-token: write — which this action requires to mint its own cachet OIDC token —
        # Determinate mints a second OIDC token for FlakeHub and logs in, and that login adds
        # https://cache.flakehub.com to the daemon's active substituters. This deployment is not a FlakeHub
        # Cache customer, so every narinfo lookup then answers 401 ("User is not authorized for this
        # resource") before it falls through to cachet: an error-level log line and a wasted round trip on
        # every request, on a build that still succeeds. Logging out returns the substituter set to the
        # logged-out state, in which cache.flakehub.com is absent — verified against a local Determinate
        # install, where `determinate-nixd status` reports logged-out and `nix config show substituters`
        # omits FlakeHub. cachet's own read credential is the netrc merged from additionalNetrcSources and
        # is independent of the FlakeHub login, so the Configure step's auth probe below still reports 404.
        - name: Log out of FlakeHub Cache, which this deployment does not use
          shell: bash
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              # `|| true`: a job without id-token never logged in, so logout is a no-op there rather than a
              # failure, and this action must not fail a build over a cache it does not even use.
              sudo determinate-nixd auth logout || true
              echo "cachet: FlakeHub login status after logout:"
              sudo determinate-nixd status || true

        - name: Configure cachet
          shell: bash
          env:
              CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
              CACHET_AUDIENCE: ${{ inputs.audience }}
              CACHET_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ inputs.trusted-public-key }}
              CACHET_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ inputs.signing-key }}
              CACHET_PROJECT: ${{ inputs.project }}
              CACHET_ROOTS: ${{ inputs.roots }}
              CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL: ${{ inputs.upstream-url }}
              CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF: ${{ inputs.default-branch-ref }}
              CACHET_PUSH: ${{ inputs.push }}
          run: |
              set -euo pipefail

              # The read credential and its Determinate config were provisioned before the daemon started
              # (the first step of this action), so the daemon's start-up synthesis already merged the
              # credential into the netrc it reads. There is nothing to do here for the netrc.

              # The substituter and trusted key are added at install time now (the extra-conf on the
              # determinate-nix-action step above), so the daemon starts already knowing them. They are not
              # written here: a substituter added after the daemon has started is never consulted, which is
              # why the last run authenticated yet never queried cachet.

              # Confirm the daemon's netrc authenticates against cachet, so a regression surfaces in the log
              # rather than as a silent rebuild: a 404 means the credential is present and authenticated —
              # the probed path is simply absent — while a 401 means it is not.
              daemon_netrc="$(nix config show netrc-file 2>/dev/null || echo /nix/var/determinate/netrc)"
              probe_code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --netrc-file "${daemon_netrc}" \
                "${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}/0000000000000000000000000000000a.narinfo" 2>/dev/null || echo 000)"
              echo "cachet: read auth probe returned ${probe_code} (404 = authenticated, 401 = not)"

              # The signing key is written where only this runner can read it, and never leaves it (ADR 0004).
              key_file="${RUNNER_TEMP}/cachet-signing.key"
              printf '%s' "${CACHET_SIGNING_KEY}" > "${key_file}"
              chmod 600 "${key_file}"
              echo "CACHET_SIGNING_KEY_FILE=${key_file}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"

              # Everything the post step reads is exported to the job environment here, and this is the
              # only place any of it is resolved. A step-level `env:` block is scoped to the step it sits
              # on, so passing these to the nested action as `with:` inputs left the post step reading
              # empty strings and declining to push, silently, on every run.
              #
              # The project name defaults to owner-and-name rather than the bare repository name.
              #
              # why: this cache serves more than one organisation, so two repositories can share a name.
              # A lease is filed under the project name and a renewal replaces the previous document
              # wholesale, so two same-named repositories defaulting to one project would overwrite each
              # other's lease — and each would then stop protecting the other's closure, making live
              # paths collectable (Invariant GC-NEVER-EATS-THE-LIVING). Including the owner makes the
              # default unique by construction rather than by everyone remembering to pass `project`.
              project="${CACHET_PROJECT}"
              if [ -z "${project}" ]; then
                project="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY//\//-}"
              fi
              # why: the heredoc form rather than `NAME=value`. `roots` takes several installables and the
              # post step splits it on any whitespace, so a caller writing them one per line with a YAML
              # block scalar is using the documented shape — and a bare `NAME=value` line cannot express
              # a newline. GitHub rejects the whole file with "Invalid format" when it sees the
              # continuation, which fails the step for a reason that points nowhere near the cause.
              #
              # The delimiter is fixed and long enough not to occur in a flake installable, and the
              # values here are action inputs rather than anything a request supplies.
              env_file() {
                printf '%s<<CACHET_EOF_1c7f\n%s\nCACHET_EOF_1c7f\n' "$1" "$2" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
              }
              env_file CACHET_CACHE_URL "${CACHET_CACHE_URL}"
              env_file CACHET_AUDIENCE "${CACHET_AUDIENCE}"
              env_file CACHET_PROJECT "${project}"
              env_file CACHET_ROOTS "${CACHET_ROOTS}"
              env_file CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL "${CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL}"
              env_file CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF "${CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF}"
              env_file CACHET_PUSH "${CACHET_PUSH}"

              echo "cachet: configured ${CACHET_CACHE_URL} as a substituter for project ${project}"

        # The nested JavaScript action: its main step snapshots the store, and its post step, on success
        # only, does the push. It takes no inputs, because the step above resolved all of them into the
        # job environment.
        # why: the full owner/repo/path@ref form rather than `./post`. A composite action resolves a
        # relative `./post` against the consumer's GITHUB_WORKSPACE rather than this action's own
        # directory, so a cross-repo consumer looked for `<workspace>/post` and failed with "Can't find
        # 'action.yml' under .../post". Naming the repository resolves the nested action independently of
        # where the consumer checked out. It is pinned to the v1 major tag, which every release in the 1.x
        # line moves forward, so the composite and its post action always come from the same line.
        - uses: agx-runtime/cachet-action/post@v1
```
