## 2. Nested post action structure and ordering

`/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet-action/post/action.yml` in full:

```yaml
name: cachet-push
description: >-
    Snapshots the Nix store, then on job success pushes what was added and renews the lease. Not meant to
    be used directly — the cachet-setup composite action wraps it.

# why: no inputs. The cachet-setup composite resolves every value and exports it to the job environment,
# which is what both this action's steps read. Declaring them here as well would give the post step a
# second, differently-named source of the same configuration (GitHub exposes an input as `INPUT_<NAME>`,
# not as the name the code reads), and that mismatch is exactly the bug that made this step decline to
# push on every run while reporting success.

runs:
    using: node24
    main: dist/main.cjs
    post: dist/post.cjs
    # why: on success only. A failed build must never populate the cache or refresh a lease — that is what
    # keeps a broken artifact from becoming the one everybody substitutes.
    post-if: success()
```

Ordering within a job:

1. **Main time** (`dist/main.cjs` runs when the nested action step executes, i.e. immediately after "Configure cachet" and **before any of the consumer's subsequent steps**): run `nix path-info --all`, write entire store listing to the snapshot file, print `cachet: store snapshot taken`.
2. Consumer's own steps run (the build).
3. **Post time** (`dist/post.cjs`, only if the whole job succeeded so far — `post-if: success()`): read config from env → bail early if `CACHET_PUSH == "false"` or required vars missing → read snapshot file (missing → treated as empty before-set) → `nix path-info --all` → `storeDiff` (order-preserving set difference) → cap at 4096 paths → mint one OIDC token for probes → resolve each root installable with `nix path-info <installable>` → filter candidates against upstream (HEAD probes) excluding root paths from filtering → filter against cachet itself (HEAD probes, Bearer token) → if anything remains, `nix copy --to file://<staging>?compression=zstd&secret-key=<keyfile>` → upload NARs first, then narinfos → if default branch, `POST /roots/<project>` to renew the lease.

## 3. The OIDC dance

Hand-rolled in both places — **`@actions/core.getIDToken` is not used anywhere**; the bundles have no `@actions/*` imports at all.

**Main/composite mint (bash, before Nix exists)** — fails the step hard if the env vars are absent:

```bash
if [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ]; then
  echo "cachet: this job cannot mint an OIDC token." >&2
  echo "  Add 'permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }' to the job." >&2
  exit 1
fi
token="$(curl -fsSL \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}" \
  "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=${CACHET_AUDIENCE}" | jq -r '.value')"
```

The token goes straight into the netrc: `machine <host> login cachet password <token>` where `host` is `cache-url` with scheme and path stripped via sed.

**Post-step mint (TS, per request)** — verbatim from `post/dist/post.cjs`:

```js
async function requestIdToken(audience, env) {
  const requestUrl = env["ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL"];
  const requestToken = env["ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN"];
  if (requestUrl === undefined || requestToken === undefined) {
    return fail("no OIDC token request variables. Add `permissions: { id-token: write }` to the job.");
  }
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`${requestUrl}&audience=${encodeURIComponent(audience)}`, {
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${requestToken}` }
    });
    if (!response.ok) {
      return fail(`the OIDC token request returned ${String(response.status)}`);
    }
    const body = await response.json();
    if (typeof body.value !== "string" || body.value.length === 0) {
      return fail("the OIDC token response carried no token");
    }
    return ok(body.value);
  } catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "unknown failure";
    return fail(`the OIDC token request failed: ${message}`);
  }
}
```

Audience handling: appended as `&audience=<audience>` (URL-encoded in the TS version, raw in the bash version); the audience value is the `audience` input / `CACHET_AUDIENCE` env, default `cachet`.

Crucially, tokens are **minted fresh per request attempt**, not once per push. The upload target is:

```js
const target = {
  cacheUrl: inputs.cacheUrl,
  mintToken: () => requestIdToken(inputs.audience, process.env)
};
```

and every retried closure (see §6) begins with `const token = await target.mintToken();` — so a retry after a 401/403 gets a brand-new JWT. One exception: the upstream/cachet HEAD-probe pass mints a single token (`probe`) reused for all cachet probes.

## 4. Snapshot mechanism (action-level wiring)

**No `save-state` / `STATE_*` mechanism is used at all** (confirmed by grep — zero occurrences). The hand-off between main and post is a plain file in `RUNNER_TEMP`, which persists for the whole job:

```js
// action/post/src/snapshot-path.ts (duplicated into both bundles)
function snapshotPath(env) {
  return import_node_path.join(env["RUNNER_TEMP"] ?? "/tmp", "cachet-store-before.txt");
}
```

Entire `post/dist/main.cjs` (main-time snapshotter), verbatim logic:

```js
async function main() {
  const snapshot = await run(["nix", "path-info", "--all"]);
  if (!snapshot.ok) {
    process.stderr.write(`cachet: could not snapshot the store — nothing will be pushed. ${snapshot.message}\n`);
    return;
  }
  await import_promises.writeFile(snapshotPath(process.env), snapshot.value, "utf8");
  process.stdout.write(`cachet: store snapshot taken\n`);
}
main().catch((error) => {
  process.stderr.write(`cachet: the snapshot step failed unexpectedly: ${String(error)}\n`);
});
```

Post-side diff wiring:

```js
const before = parseSnapshot(await readFileOrEmpty(snapshotPath(process.env)));  // missing file -> "" -> empty set
const afterOutput = await run(["nix", "path-info", "--all"]);
...
const candidates = boundCandidates(storeDiff(before, parseSnapshot(afterOutput.value)));
```

`parseSnapshot` splits on newlines, trims, drops empties. `storeDiff` is a set-difference preserving first-appearance order. `boundCandidates` fails (swallowed, see §8) if additions exceed `PUSH_PATHS_MAX = ROOTS_PATHS_MAX = 4096`. A missing snapshot file silently makes *everything* in the store a candidate (degenerate push-everything mode), because `readFileOrEmpty` swallows ENOENT.

Supporting constants (`post/dist/post.cjs` top): `UPLOAD_SINGLE_MAX_BYTES = 94371840` (90 MiB), `UPLOAD_PART_BYTES = 67108864` (64 MiB), `MULTIPART_PARTS_MAX = 1000`, `UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX = 3`, `UPLOAD_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS = 500`, `FILTER_CONCURRENCY_MAX = 16`, `UPLOAD_TOTAL_BYTES_HEADER = "x-cachet-upload-bytes"`, `NAR_KEY_PREFIX = "nar/"`, `GRACE_WINDOW_DAYS = 14`, `LEASE_RETENTION_DAYS = 30`.

---

## 5. Cache host/URL and upstream-filter configuration

- **Cache URL:** `cache-url` input, default `https://pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io`. Path: input → `CACHET_CACHE_URL` (step env) → `$GITHUB_ENV` → post reads `env["CACHET_CACHE_URL"]`. Also used in the composite for the netrc `machine` line (scheme/path stripped) and the auth probe. It appears as `extra-substituters` in the Determinate install step.
- **Upstream-filter URL:** `upstream-url` input, default `https://cache.nixos.org` → `CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL` env. There is a second hardcoded fallback inside the post bundle: `var UPSTREAM_URL_DEFAULT = "https://cache.nixos.org";` used when the env var is absent (relevant only when someone runs the post action standalone).
- **Trusted public key** (for substitution verification): `trusted-public-key` input with the deployment default baked into metadata, injected at install time as `extra-trusted-public-keys`.

The read-auth probe in the Configure step (verbatim, as it's behaviorally load-bearing):

```bash
daemon_netrc="$(nix config show netrc-file 2>/dev/null || echo /nix/var/determinate/netrc)"
probe_code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --netrc-file "${daemon_netrc}" \
  "${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}/0000000000000000000000000000000a.narinfo" 2>/dev/null || echo 000)"
echo "cachet: read auth probe returned ${probe_code} (404 = authenticated, 401 = not)"
```

---

## 6. Token exchange — none. Direct OIDC-JWT auth on the worker's write endpoints

The action **never calls a token/mint endpoint on the worker**. The GitHub OIDC JWT itself is the Bearer credential for every write and every authenticated probe. Exact requests (all verbatim from `real/upload.ts` section of `post/dist/post.cjs`):

**Whole-object PUT** (objects ≤ 90 MiB):

```js
const response = await fetch(objectUrl(target, plan.object.key), {
  method: "PUT",
  headers: authHeaders(token.value, { "Content-Length": String(plan.object.sizeBytes) }),
  body: new Uint8Array(bytes.value)
});
// objectUrl = `${target.cacheUrl.replace(/\/+$/, "")}/${key}${query}`
// authHeaders = { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, ...extra }
```

**Multipart** (objects > 90 MiB; parts of exactly 64 MiB, final part = remainder; >1000 parts rejected by `planParts`):

```js
// begin:   POST {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploads        header x-cachet-upload-bytes: <totalBytes> -> JSON { uploadId }
// part:    PUT  {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploadId=<id>&partNumber=<n>   Content-Length: <partLen>   -> JSON part descriptor, accumulated
// complete:POST {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploadId=<id>   Content-Type: application/json, body = JSON.stringify(parts)
// abort:   DELETE {cacheUrl}/{key}?uploadId=<id>   fire-and-forget: `.catch(() => { return; })`
```

**Lease renewal:**

```js
const response = await fetch(`${target.cacheUrl.replace(/\/+$/, "")}/roots/${project}`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: authHeaders(token.value, { "Content-Type": "application/json" }),
  body: JSON.stringify({ storePaths, installables })
});
```

**Probes:** `HEAD {upstreamUrl}/{hash}.narinfo` (no auth; 404 → false, 2xx → true, anything else/network error → `undefined` = "unknown"); `HEAD {cacheUrl}/{hash}.narinfo` with `Authorization: Bearer` (same tri-state).

**Staging:** objects are produced by `nix copy --to "file://${stagingRoot}?compression=zstd&secret-key=${inputs.signingKeyFile}"` where `stagingRoot` is `mkdtemp(os.tmpdir() + "cachet-staging-")` and the key file is `$RUNNER_TEMP/cachet-signing.key`. `readStagingDirectory` collects `*.narinfo` files at the root (kind `narinfo`, key = filename) and everything under `nar/` (kind `nar`, key = `nar/<basename>`). **Upload order is all NARs first, then all narinfos** (`uploadOrder`), so a narinfo never lands before its NAR. `planUpload` picks single vs multipart by size; uploads are sequential (one object at a time).

The worker's error vocabulary is mapped in `STATUS_BY_CODE`: `malformed_key/malformed_narinfo/malformed_roots/malformed_auth/part_number_invalid/part_size_mismatch/complete_parts_mismatch → 400`, `unauthorized → 401`, `forbidden_org/forbidden_ref → 403`, `not_found/upload_unknown → 404`, `narinfo_nar_missing → 409`, `length_required → 411`, `body_too_large → 413`, `auth_unavailable/storage_unavailable → 503` — useful for matching server responses in your rewrite.

---

## 7. Lease renewal

**Gating, two layers:**
- Syntactic: `post-if: success()` on the nested action — renewal (and pushing) happens only on a green job.
- Branch: exact string equality between `GITHUB_REF` and `CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF` (default `refs/heads/main`):

```js
isDefaultBranch: isSameRef(env["GITHUB_REF"], env["CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF"])
...
function isSameRef(actual, expected) {
  if (actual === undefined || expected === undefined) return false;
  if (actual.length === 0 || expected.length === 0) return false;
  return actual === expected;
}
```

PR runs (`GITHUB_REF = refs/pull/N/merge`) and tag pushes never match. The `default-branch-ref` input description notes the worker enforces the ref too; the client check "only avoids a request that would be refused."

**Sequence:** renewal happens *after* the upload succeeds, at the very end of `push()`:

```js
if (!inputs.isDefaultBranch) {
  process.stdout.write(`cachet: not the default branch, so the lease is not renewed\n`);
  return;
}
const renewed = await postRoots(target, inputs.project, rootPaths, inputs.rootInstallables);
if (!renewed.ok) {
  process.stderr.write(`cachet: ${renewed.message}\n`);
  return;
}
process.stdout.write(`cachet: lease renewed for ${inputs.project}\n`);
```

`postRoots` is wrapped in the same 3-attempt retry (`withRetriesUsingRealSleep("renew the lease for ${project}", ...)`), with a fresh OIDC token per attempt.

**Project naming:** if `CACHET_PROJECT` is empty the composite resolves `project="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY//\//-}"` (e.g. `my-org-my-repo`) and exports that; the TS side treats an empty `CACHET_PROJECT` as a configuration error (`missingInputs` lists it) and declines to run at all. Rationale in the YAML comments: a renewal replaces the lease document wholesale, so two same-named repos across orgs would clobber each other's leases and make live paths collectable ("Invariant GC-NEVER-EATS-THE-LIVING").

**Root paths:** each installable in `CACHET_ROOTS` (whitespace-split) is resolved with `nix `path-info <installable>`; failures only log `cachet: could not resolve <i>; it will not be a lease root` to stderr and skip. Root paths are **exempt from upstream filtering** (`filterAgainstUpstream` partitions candidates into `rootCandidates` kept unconditionally vs `probeable`). Server-side constants embedded in the bundle: grace window 14 days, lease retention 30 days, roots cap 4096.

---

## 8. Error-handling philosophy

**The post step can never fail the job.** There is no `setFailed`, no `process.exitCode = 1`, no thrown escape — every error path does `process.stderr.write(\`cachet: ...\`)` (or `stdout.write` for informational lines) and `return`. Even the top-level `.catch` only logs: `cachet: the push failed unexpectedly: ${String(error)}`. Same for `main.cjs`. Missing snapshot file → empty before-set. Missing OIDC env vars → log and return. Missing required config (`CACHET_CACHE_URL`, `CACHET_PROJECT`, `CACHET_AUDIENCE`) → the composed `missingInputsMessage`:

```js
`cachet: nothing pushed, because ${missing.join(", ")} ` + `${missing.length === 1 ? "is" : "are"} unset. The cachet-setup composite action exports these ` + `to the job environment; if you are running the post action directly, set them yourself.\n`
```

Log vocabulary is a bare lowercase `cachet:` prefix — **no `::warning::` / `::error::` workflow commands anywhere**. Distinct fixed messages: `cachet: store snapshot taken`, `cachet: the job added nothing to the store`, `cachet: N not upstream, M already upstream[, K probes failed (kept)]`, `cachet: N new to cachet, M already cached[, K probes failed (kept)]`, `cachet: uploaded N objects`, `cachet: not the default branch, so the lease is not renewed`, `cachet: lease renewed for <project>`, `cachet: pushing is disabled for this job`, and all failure lines starting `cachet: <message>`.

**The one deliberate exception:** the composite's first step hard-`exit 1`s if `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` is unset — that fails the job, with the remediation printed (`permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }`). FlakeHub logout is explicitly `|| true` ("must not fail a build over a cache it does not even use").

**Retry policy** (verbatim):

```js
async function withRetries(what, attempt, sleep) {
  let last = "no attempt was made";
  for (let tries = 0; tries < UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX; tries += 1) {
    let result;
    try { result = await attempt(); }
    catch (error) { result = fail(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)); }
    if (result.ok) { return result; }
    last = result.message;
    if (tries + 1 < UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX) { await sleep(UPLOAD_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS * (tries + 1)); }
  }
  return fail(`${what} failed after ${String(UPLOAD_RETRY_MAX)} attempts: ${last}`);
}
```

3 attempts, **linear** backoff 500 ms then 1000 ms (not exponential), and each attempt re-mints the OIDC token. Applied to: whole PUT, multipart begin/part/complete, and lease renewal. Multipart part failures also abort the upload (`DELETE ?uploadId=`) before returning the failure. Probe failures are fail-open *toward the cache*: an unparseable path or a network/5xx probe answer is `undefined`, counted as `probeFailures`, and the path is **kept** for upload rather than dropped. Store-diff size over 4096 added paths aborts the push with `this job added N store paths, more than the 4096 cap`.

---

## 9. Version pinning / release mechanics

- **dist is checked in.** `post/dist/main.cjs` (56 lines) and `post/dist/post.cjs` (755 lines) are esbuild-style bundles whose headers name the original TS entry points (`action/post/src/main.ts`, `action/post/src/post.ts`). There is **no build or release workflow in this repo** — `.github/` contains only `dependabot.yml`. Canonical source and the bundling live in private `agx-runtime/cachet` under `action/`; changes are copied here (stated in the action.yml header and README).
- **Tags are lightweight** (`git for-each-ref` shows objecttype `commit` for all). Series: `v1.0.0` … `v1.0.13` plus a moving major tag `v1`. Right now `HEAD == v1 == v1.0.13 == 818627b`. The composite consumes its own nested action via `agx-runtime/cachet-action/post@v1`, and the YAML comment states the policy explicitly: "pinned to the v1 major tag, which every release in the 1.x line moves forward, so the composite and its post action always come from the same line." (README's usage example shows `@main`, though.)
- Dependabot watches `package-ecosystem: github-actions` at `/`, weekly on Mondays, label `dependencies`, purely as a stale-reference safety net; bumps are "reconciled by re-syncing from cachet rather than merged on their own."
- Third-party pinning: `DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@v3.21.9` (exact). The `determinate-nix-action-version` input (default `v3`) is dead — it appears nowhere in `runs:`.

---

## 10. Install steps / CLI provisioning

- **No `cachet` binary is installed** — there is no CLI. All cache-write logic is the checked-in node24 bundle; tooling used on the runner is just `nix` (from Determinate), `curl`, `jq`, `sudo`, `determinate-nixd`, and coreutils.
- **Nix itself** is installed by `DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@v3.21.9` with this `extra-conf` (so the daemon starts already trusting cachet):

```yaml
extra-conf: |
    extra-substituters = ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
    extra-trusted-public-keys = ${{ inputs.trusted-public-key }}
```

- The read credential is provisioned out-of-band before that install: `/etc/nix/netrc` (0600, root) plus `/etc/determinate/config.json` amended so `authentication.additionalNetrcSources` contains `/etc/nix/netrc` (jq-merged if the file exists, written fresh otherwise). No checksums anywhere — version pinning of the nested action and of the Determinate installer is by git tag only.

---

If your replacement wraps a released binary, you can keep the same two-file shape (a tiny node wrapper or a composite that downloads the binary into `$RUNNER_TEMP` in `main` and re-invokes in `post`), but the state hand-off model here is deliberately a **file in `RUNNER_TEMP`** (`cachet-store-before.txt`) plus **`$GITHUB_ENV` exports** — reproduce those two mechanisms and everything downstream (post-if: success(), env-based config in `post.cjs`) stays identical.

### Invocation (Justfile lines 98–104)

```

./scripts/cache-login.sh --host pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io --infisical-name CACHET_READ_TOKEN \
    --infisical-path /PUBLIC \
    --infisical-env default \
    --infisical-project-id 7c433b42-4d98-4d30-b3dc-daf7111ef7cc \
```

| Flag | Effect | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--host <cache-host>` | cache hostname | `pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io` (line 89, env `CACHET_HOST`) |

### Usage text (verbatim, lines 37–56, to stderr, `exit 2`)

```
usage: cache-login.sh [--host <cache-host>] [--token-stdin] [--public-key <name:base64>]
                      [--infisical-name <name>] [--infisical-path <folder>]
                      [--infisical-env <env>] [--infisical-project-id <uuid>]

Every value has a default for this org's cache, so no arguments are needed.

  --host             the cache hostname, e.g. pkg-cache.example.com
  --infisical-name   the Infisical secret to read, e.g. CACHET_READ_TOKEN
```

## 2. Device-flow login — does not exist

**There is no GitHub OAuth device flow anywhere in the repo — no endpoints, no client ID, no polling.** Greps for `device`, `client_id`, `oauth`, `github.com/login` over all sources are empty. The worker has no `/api/*` routes of any kind (full route table cited in Q9).

The token flow is Infisical-based (cache-login.sh lines 190–242):

1. `--token-stdin`: `token="$(cat)"`.
2. Otherwise, require `infisical` on PATH (comes from the nix dev shell).
3. Session check: `infisical user get token --silent` — prints the locally-saved login token, empty when logged out. It reads local state, so it answers "logged in?" even offline (comment lines 201–208). If empty:
   - prints `cache-login: this machine is not logged in to Infisical; starting 'infisical login'.` and runs interactive `infisical login` (browser-based, handled by the Infisical CLI, not by this repo's code).
4. Fetch (exact argv pinned by test/fast/login/cache-login.test.ts lines 393–414):
   ```
   infisical secrets get CACHET_READ_TOKEN --plain --silent --env default --path /PUBLIC --projectId 7c433b42-4d98-4d30-b3dc-daf7111ef7cc
   ```
   (`--projectId` omitted when the id is empty; secret name positional, folder via `--path`, env must be explicit because the CLI's fallback is `dev`.)
5. Token sanitized: `tr -d '\n\r'`, then non-empty + no-whitespace enforced.

**Where the token is stored**: there is no per-user file. The token goes only into the daemon's netrc — see Q3/Q8. On **re-login** the script is fully idempotent: the AWK filter (lines 319–322) drops the *entire* `machine <host>` block (including multi-line `login`/`password` continuation lines, and `default` blocks are treated as their own blocks), other machines' entries survive verbatim, the new entry is appended. Same token re-run is byte-identical (test lines 210–218); rotation replaces only this host (lines 220–229). Server-side rotation procedure (docs/operations.md §5): write new token's SHA-256 into the unused digest slot, distribute the token via Infisical, everyone re-runs `cache-login`, then overwrite the old slot.

## 3. setup command — there isn't one; `cache-login` *is* the setup

It never edits `/etc/nix/nix.conf` (Determinate manages that file; the script targets the include). Three host-level writes, all through `install_file` (lines 260–269: `mktemp` → `printf` → `chmod` → `sudo mkdir -p <dirname>` → `sudo cp` → `sudo chmod` → `rm`), i.e. atomic-by-copy, root-owned, `$SUDO` = `sudo` unless overridden.

### (a) `/etc/nix/netrc` — mode 0600 (line 334)

Exact entry format (one line, appended after preserved entries):
```

```
e.g. from the test fixture: `machine pkg-cache.example.com login cachet password the-shared-read-token\n`. **Never `~/.netrc`** — contracts.md §"Nix client behavior" states the daemon's netrc is the only one substitution sees (`~/.netrc` invisible). Login field is always literally `cachet` (decoration; worker ignores it, Q4). Replacement is block-aware (AWK skipping whole `machine`/`default` blocks, lines 315–331) to avoid the orphaned-`password`-line credential leak documented at lines 304–314.

### (b) Determinate Nix branch: `/etc/determinate/config.json` — mode 0644

Detected via `CACHET_DETERMINATE`, else `command -v determinate-nixd` (lines 77–83). `register_netrc_source` (lines 278–302): if the config is absent, creates exactly:
```json

  "authentication": {
```

If present, jq-merges: `.authentication.additionalNetrcSources = ((.authentication.additionalNetrcSources // []) + [$s] | unique)` preserving other sections (builder, garbageCollector); refuses with instructions if the file exists and jq is missing (exit note: returns 1). Merge algorithm (lines 352–419):
- `setting_value $key` = last line matching `^$key[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*` (Nix's own repeated-key rule).
- `merge_value existing wanted` appends `wanted` space-separated iff it's not already a word of the value (dedup, idempotence).
- Managed keys — **all lines matching any of these three keys are deleted** (there are no managed markers; ownership is by key name), along with all blank lines; every other line survives:

  ```
  sed -e '/^netrc-file[[:space:]]*=/d' -e '/^extra-substituters[[:space:]]*=/d' -e '/^extra-trusted-public-keys[[:space:]]*=/d'
  ```
- Then appended at the end, fixed order, one line per key:
  - stock Nix branch:
    ```
    netrc-file = /etc/nix/netrc
    extra-substituters = <existing words…> https://<host>
    extra-trusted-public-keys = <existing words…> <name>:<base64>
    ```

## 4. How nix authenticates on READ (worker auth middleware)

Routes read **only the `Authorization` header** — `c.req.header('authorization')` in `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/worker.ts` lines 56, 87, 205, 217. **No query-param auth, no cookie auth.**

`parseAuthorizationHeader` — `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/core/auth/header.ts` lines 56–110 — accepts exactly two schemes (case-insensitive; max header 8192 bytes, `AUTH_HEADER_BYTES_MAX`):

1. **`Bearer <credentials>`** → `{kind:'bearer', token}`
2. **`Basic base64(login:password)`** → decode base64, split on the **first** colon (a token may itself contain colons, line 103–105), discard the login, keep the password → `{kind:'basic', password}`. Empty password → 401.

Anything else → `malformed_auth` (400), e.g. `unsupported Authorization scheme "<scheme>"`.

`authorizeRead` — `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/core/auth/authorize.ts` lines 133–160 — decision tree:

- **Basic**: `verifyReadToken(password, slots)` first (SHA-256 hex of the password compared, constant-time, against ≤2 configured digests from `CACHET_READ_TOKEN_HASH_CURRENT`/`CACHET_READ_TOKEN_HASH_PREVIOUS`; src/core/auth/token.ts). If no match, the password is tried as a **GitHub OIDC JWT only if it matches** `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` (`isJwtShaped`, oidc.ts line 122–124); otherwise fails 401 `the read token was not recognised`. The JWT-in-Basic path exists because the action writes the job's OIDC token into the runner's netrc as the password.
- **Bearer**: same two-step on the token value (no JWT-shape gate — an unrecognized non-JWT bearer goes through OIDC verification and fails there).

So nix's read path: the daemon turns `machine <host> login cachet password <token>` into `Authorization: Basic base64("cachet:<token>")`, and the worker authenticates the **password** as either the shared read token or a CI OIDC token. Nix's `access-tokens` nix.conf option is not used anywhere.

**Write auth** (`authorizeWrite`, lines 171–187): Bearer OIDC only. A Basic credential fails outright with 401 and message `writes require a GitHub OIDC token presented as a Bearer credential`; the read token is never consulted on writes (real/request.ts lines 94–99).

**Ordering & statuses** (worker.ts header comment, lines 8–12; `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/core/result.ts` STATUS_BY_CODE): key/path validation → auth → body guards. Auth failures: missing/bad credential → **401** (`unauthorized`); OIDC from wrong org → **403** (`forbidden_org`); lease renewal from wrong ref → **403** (`forbidden_ref`); JWKS unreachable with no cache → **503** (`auth_unavailable`); malformed header → **400** (`malformed_auth`). Every client error body is exactly (real/request.ts lines 37–42):
```
<code>: <message>\n
```
with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`.

## 4. How nix authenticates on READ (worker auth middleware)

Routes read **only the `Authorization` header** — `c.req.header('authorization')` in `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/worker.ts` lines 56, 87, 205, 217. **No query-param auth, no cookie auth.**

`parseAuthorizationHeader` — `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/core/auth/header.ts` lines 56–110 — accepts exactly two schemes (case-insensitive; max header 8192 bytes, `AUTH_HEADER_BYTES_MAX`):

1. **`Bearer <credentials>`** → `{kind:'bearer', token}`
2. **`Basic base64(login:password)`** → decode base64, split on the **first** colon (a token may itself contain colons, line 103–105), discard the login, keep the password → `{kind:'basic', password}`. Empty password → 401.

Anything else → `malformed_auth` (400), e.g. `unsupported Authorization scheme "<scheme>"`.

`authorizeRead` — `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/core/auth/authorize.ts` lines 133–160 — decision tree:

- **Basic**: `verifyReadToken(password, slots)` first (SHA-256 hex of the password compared, constant-time, against ≤2 configured digests from `CACHET_READ_TOKEN_HASH_CURRENT`/`CACHET_READ_TOKEN_HASH_PREVIOUS`; src/core/auth/token.ts). If no match, the password is tried as a **GitHub OIDC JWT only if it matches** `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` (`isJwtShaped`, oidc.ts line 122–124); otherwise fails 401 `the read token was not recognised`. The JWT-in-Basic path exists because the action writes the job's OIDC token into the runner's netrc as the password.
- **Bearer**: same two-step on the token value (no JWT-shape gate — an unrecognized non-JWT bearer goes through OIDC verification and fails there).

So nix's read path: the daemon turns `machine <host> login cachet password <token>` into `Authorization: Basic base64("cachet:<token>")`, and the worker authenticates the **password** as either the shared read token or a CI OIDC token. Nix's `access-tokens` nix.conf option is not used anywhere.

**Write auth** (`authorizeWrite`, lines 171–187): Bearer OIDC only. A Basic credential fails outright with 401 and message `writes require a GitHub OIDC token presented as a Bearer credential`; the read token is never consulted on writes (real/request.ts lines 94–99).

**Ordering & statuses** (worker.ts header comment, lines 8–12; `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/core/result.ts` STATUS_BY_CODE): key/path validation → auth → body guards. Auth failures: missing/bad credential → **401** (`unauthorized`); OIDC from wrong org → **403** (`forbidden_org`); lease renewal from wrong ref → **403** (`forbidden_ref`); JWKS unreachable with no cache → **503** (`auth_unavailable`); malformed header → **400** (`malformed_auth`). Every client error body is exactly (real/request.ts lines 37–42):
```
<code>: <message>\n
```
with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`.

1. `--token-stdin`: `token="$(cat)"`.
2. Otherwise, require `infisical` on PATH (comes from the nix dev shell).
3. Session check: `infisical user get token --silent` — prints the locally-saved login token, empty when logged out. It reads local state, so it answers "logged in?" even offline (comment lines 201–208). If empty:

4. Fetch (exact argv pinned by test/fast/login/cache-login.test.ts lines 393–414):

Server-side rotation procedure (docs/operations.md §5): write new token's SHA-256 into the unused digest slot, distribute the token via Infisical, everyone re-runs `cache-login`, then overwrite the old slot.

It never edits `/etc/nix/nix.conf` (Determinate manages that file; the script targets the include). ### (a) `/etc/nix/netrc` — mode 0600 (line 334)

Exact entry format (one line, appended after preserved entries):

e.g. from the test fixture: `machine pkg-cache.example.com login cachet password the-shared-read-token\n`. **Never `~/.netrc`** — contracts.md §"Nix client behavior" states the daemon's netrc is the only one substitution sees (`~/.netrc` invisible). Replacement is block-aware (AWK skipping whole `machine`/`default` blocks, lines 315–331) to avoid the orphaned-`password`-line credential leak documented at lines 304–314.

Detected via `CACHET_DETERMINATE`, else `command -v determinate-nixd` (lines 77–83). `register_netrc_source` (lines 278–302): if the config is absent, creates exactly:
```json
{
  "authentication": {
    "additionalNetrcSources": ["/etc/nix/netrc"]
```

If present, jq-merges: `.authentication.additionalNetrcSources = ((.authentication.additionalNetrcSources // []) + [$s] | unique)` preserving other sections (builder, garbageCollector); refuses with instructions if the file exists and jq is missing (exit note: returns 1). - `setting_value $key` = last line matching `^$key[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*` (Nix's own repeated-key rule).

**No uninstall mode.** Then daemon restart (see Q1). The 401-observed failure that motivated the restart is documented at lines 424–427.

## 4. How nix authenticates on READ (worker auth middleware)

Routes read **only the `Authorization` header** — `c.req.header('authorization')` in `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/worker.ts` lines 56, 87, 205, 217. **No query-param auth, no cookie auth.**

`parseAuthorizationHeader` — `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/core/auth/header.ts` lines 56–110 — accepts exactly two schemes (case-insensitive; max header 8192 bytes, `AUTH_HEADER_BYTES_MAX`):

1. **`Bearer <credentials>`** → `{kind:'bearer', token}`
2. **`Basic base64(login:password)`** → decode base64, split on the **first** colon (a token may itself contain colons, line 103–105), discard the login, keep the password → `{kind:'basic', password}`. Empty password → 401.

Anything else → `malformed_auth` (400), e.g. `unsupported Authorization scheme "<scheme>"`.

`authorizeRead` — `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/core/auth/authorize.ts` lines 133–160 — decision tree:

- **Basic**: `verifyReadToken(password, slots)` first (SHA-256 hex of the password compared, constant-time, against ≤2 configured digests from `CACHET_READ_TOKEN_HASH_CURRENT`/`CACHET_READ_TOKEN_HASH_PREVIOUS`; src/core/auth/token.ts). If no match, the password is tried as a **GitHub OIDC JWT only if it matches** `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` (`isJwtShaped`, oidc.ts line 122–124); otherwise fails 401 `the read token was not recognised`. The JWT-in-Basic path exists because the action writes the job's OIDC token into the runner's netrc as the password.
- **Bearer**: same two-step on the token value (no JWT-shape gate — an unrecognized non-JWT bearer goes through OIDC verification and fails there).

So nix's read path: the daemon turns `machine <host> login cachet password <token>` into `Authorization: Basic base64("cachet:<token>")`, and the worker authenticates the **password** as either the shared read token or a CI OIDC token. Nix's `access-tokens` nix.conf option is not used anywhere.

**Write auth** (`authorizeWrite`, lines 171–187): Bearer OIDC only. A Basic credential fails outright with 401 and message `writes require a GitHub OIDC token presented as a Bearer credential`; the read token is never consulted on writes (real/request.ts lines 94–99).

**Ordering & statuses** (worker.ts header comment, lines 8–12; `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/core/result.ts` STATUS_BY_CODE): key/path validation → auth → body guards. Auth failures: missing/bad credential → **401** (`unauthorized`); OIDC from wrong org → **403** (`forbidden_org`); lease renewal from wrong ref → **403** (`forbidden_ref`); JWKS unreachable with no cache → **503** (`auth_unavailable`); malformed header → **400** (`malformed_auth`). Every client error body is exactly (real/request.ts lines 37–42):
```
<code>: <message>\n
```
with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`.

```sh

nix key convert-secret-to-public < cachet.key > cachet.pub
```

## 6. doctor — does not exist

The documented human diagnostic procedure is two curls (README.md "Using the cache"; ONBOARDING.md troubleshooting table):


The 401-vs-404 distinction is load-bearing: 401 = credential problem, 404 = authenticated but path absent (auth runs before the bucket lookup — smoke test comment at test/smoke/live.smoke.test.ts lines 82–86).

## 9. `/nix-cache-info` body and (non)existence of `/api/public/config`

### `/nix-cache-info` — the only unauthenticated route

Built by `nixCacheInfoText()` in `/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/core/wire/cache-info.ts` (lines 28–35) from constants `NIX_STORE_DIR = '/nix/store'` and `CACHE_INFO_PRIORITY = 30` (src/core/constants.ts lines 23, 26).

Exact body (trailing newline included):
```
StoreDir: /nix/store
WantMassQuery: 1
Priority: 30
```

Response headers (`cacheInfoResponseHeaders`, src/core/routes/read.ts lines 68–73):
```
Content-Type: text/x-nix-cache-info
Cache-Control: public, max-age=300
```

### There is NO `/api/public/config` (or any `/api/*` route)

The worker's complete route table (`/Users/shivanshvij/Development/cachet/src/worker.ts`):

| Method & path | Auth | Handler |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /nix-cache-info` | none | constant body above |
| `GET,HEAD /:file{[^/]+\.narinfo}` | read | `serveObject`/`headObject` from R2 key `<32-nix-base32-hash>.narinfo` |
| `PUT /:file.narinfo` | write (Bearer OIDC) | `putNarinfo` (409 `narinfo_nar_missing` if its NAR is absent) |
| `GET,HEAD /nar/*` | read | NAR key `nar/<52 base32>.nar[.xz|.zst|.bz2|.gz|.br|.lzip|.lz4|none]` |
| `PUT /nar/*` | write | whole object (≤94,371,840 B) or `?uploadId&partNumber` part (fixed 67,108,864 B parts) |
| `POST /nar/*` | write | `?uploads` (create multipart, needs `x-cachet-upload-bytes` header) / `?uploadId` (complete) |
| `DELETE /nar/*?uploadId` | write | abort multipart |
| `POST /roots/:project` | write (default-branch OIDC only) | renew GC lease |
| `GET /roots`, `GET /roots/:project` | read | lease documents (for the verifier; no object bytes) |
| everything else | — | `404` body `not found\n` with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=30` |

Read success headers: `Content-Type: text/x-nix-narinfo` or `application/x-nix-nar`, `Content-Length: <size>`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=2592000, immutable` (both narinfo and NAR TTLs are 2,592,000s; negative-cache 404s are 30s). Unhandled server errors → `500` `internal error\n` (invariants logged at alert level).

So the worker serves no config document of any kind to clients: **deployment identity (hostname, orgs, audience, trusted public key, default branch) is compiled into the CLI script and action metadata as defaults** (ADR 0013 "deployment identity is configuration" applies to the worker; the client sides hardcode it). For the Rust CLI, the equivalents to bake in are: host `pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io`, public key `pkg-cache.loopholelabs.io-1:JC2XK3HyAUXteubthi/pUEM0iokE6YyOGFURMB4hsRE=`, Infisical name/path/env/project `CACHET_READ_TOKEN` / `/PUBLIC` / `default` / `7c433b42-4d98-4d30-b3dc-daf7111ef7cc`, OIDC audience `cachet`, upstream `https://cache.nixos.org`.

### A Rust-rewrite gotcha list distilled from the above

1. Reproduce the netrc **block-aware** replacement (whole `machine`/`default` blocks), not line-based — the orphaned-`login`/`password` leak is deliberate regression-tested behavior.
2. Reproduce the nix.conf merge's exact idempotence semantics: delete all lines for the three keys (and blank lines), merge words, rewrite in fixed order, single line each.
3. Preserve the Determinate/stock divergence exactly (register source + omit `netrc-file` vs. write `netrc-file`) and the detection order (`CACHET_DETERMINATE`→`command -v determinate-nixd`).
4. Client errors on the wire are `<code>: <message>\n`, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, and auth precedes all bucket work (a 404 is only ever returned to an authenticated caller — the smoke suite asserts this).
5. Note the cosmetic bug if you want fidelity: the success message hardcodes "netrc-file" even when it wasn't set (cache-login.sh line 461).</result>

Fixes:

1. login.rs:397 — `server(vec![...])` inside `#[tokio::test]` where `server` local vs the test fn named `server`? I named the constructor `fn server(...)` and inside tests ALSO the variable `let server = server(vec![...])` — second call in same scope: `let server = server(...)` then later `server(vec![...])` AGAIN after shadowing → E0618 "expected function, found FakeServer" (the binding shadows the fn). Fix: rename constructor to `fake_server`.

2. setup.rs:184 — merge_custom_conf netrc_path: I typed the param `Option<&str>` in merge_custom_conf but wrote `path.display()` — signature says `netrc_path: Option<&str>`... I declared `netrc_path: Option<&str>`? Let me check: signature is `netrc_path: Option<&str>` (line ~150: `pub fn merge_custom_conf(existing: &str, netrc_path: Option<&str>, ...`) and inside I call `path.display()`. Then run_setup passes `netrc_line` as `Option<&Path>` → mismatched types at 340; tests pass `Some(Path::new(...))` → mismatched at 405/421. Decide: use Option<&str> everywhere (path passed as string "/etc/nix/netrc"). In run_setup, the netrc path is a PathBuf → pass `paths.netrc.to_str()`? Lossy. Better: merge_custom_conf takes Option<&str> and run_setup converts via to_string_lossy. Tests pass "/etc/nix/netrc" directly.

3. setup.rs:484 closure E0373 — because `Privileged` = dyn Fn + Send + Sync, default object lifetime `'static`? For a `type_alias` used in param position `run: &Privileged` — the default lifetimes for trait objects TYPE ALIASES: `&'a Privileged` where Privileged = dyn Fn+Send+Sync+'static (trait object default in alias = 'static when outside expression). Yes: type aliases get default 'static object bound. So &Privileged requires 'static closure → borrows fail. Fix: make the type alias generic over lifetime: `type Privileged<'a> = dyn Fn(&[&str]) -> Result<(), String> + Send + Sync + 'a;` and sign `run: &Privileged<'_>`.

Same for install dyn param: it's already `&dyn Fn(...) -> ...` inline — inline dyn in param gets the elided lifetime, fine.

Lib errors E0599/E0308: only merge_custom_conf path type. And E0618.

Fix all.

formatted 8 files (6 changed) in 71ms
The cachet command-line client: device-flow login, nix.conf and netrc setup, push, keygen, and the auth-routing doctor probe.

Usage: cachet <COMMAND>

Commands:
  login   Log in to a deployment with GitHub's device flow and store the read token
  setup   Write this machine's nix.conf and netrc so builds substitute from the cache, then restart the daemon. Requires `cachet login` first
  doctor  Probe the read wiring against a deployment and report what holds
  keygen  Generate a deployment's ed25519 signing keypair. Bootstrap only
  push    CI mode: with --snapshot-only the composite's main step (snapshot the store); without it the post step (push what the job added). Reads the job's CACHET_* environment and always exits zero
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

input.content:
# The action consumers wire into their CI: install Determinate Nix trusting
# this cache, provision the job's read credential before the daemon starts,
# download the pinned cachet binary, and hand the push phases to the nested
# main/post action. Signing happens server-side, so the action holds no key
# material; the job's OIDC token is the only credential it ever touches.
name: cachet setup
description: >-
  Install Determinate Nix wired to a cachet deployment, then push what the
  job builds. Needs `permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }`.
author: nox-systems

inputs:
  cache-url:
    description: The cache's base URL.
    required: true
  roots:
    description: >-
      Flake installables whose closures this project keeps. Their outputs
      are pushed unconditionally and, on the default branch, become the
      project's garbage-collection lease.
    required: false
    default: ""
  audience:
    description: The OIDC audience the cache requires.
    required: false
    default: cachet
  project:
    description: >-
      The lease name for this repository. Defaults to the owner and name
      joined by a hyphen (`my-org-my-repo`), because a renewal replaces the
      lease wholesale: two same-named repositories in one org would
      otherwise overwrite each other's.
    required: false
    default: ""
  upstream-url:
    description: The upstream cache to filter against before pushing.
    required: false
    default: https://cache.nixos.org
  default-branch-ref:
    description: >-
      The ref permitted to renew the lease. The cache enforces this itself;
      this input only avoids a request that would be refused.
    required: false
    default: refs/heads/main
  push:
    description: Set to false to use the cache read-only.
    required: false
    default: "true"
  cachet-version:
    description: The cachet release to download and run.
    required: false
    default: 0.0.1

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    # Provision the read credential BEFORE Determinate is installed and its
    # daemon starts. determinate-nixd synthesizes the netrc the daemon reads
    # at daemon start, merging every file under
    # authentication.additionalNetrcSources, and that startup synthesis is
    # the only reliable one on these runners. Writing the credential and its
    # registration here means the daemon's start-up synthesis sees both.
    - name: Provision the cachet read credential before Determinate starts
      shell: bash
      env:
        CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
        CACHET_AUDIENCE: ${{ inputs.audience }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail

        # The OIDC token authenticates this job's reads; the runner is
        # authorized because it is provably the org's CI. Minted here,
        # without nix, because Determinate is not installed yet. This check
        # fails the job on purpose: every later step assumes the token.
        if [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ]; then
          echo "cachet: this job cannot mint an OIDC token." >&2
          echo "  Add 'permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }' to the job." >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        token="$(curl -fsSL \
          -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}" \
          "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=${CACHET_AUDIENCE}" | jq -r '.value')"
        host="$(printf '%s' "${CACHET_CACHE_URL}" | sed -e 's#^https\?://##' -e 's#/.*$##')"

        # The credential file: real, outside the nix store, 0600.
        sudo mkdir -p /etc/nix /etc/determinate
        printf 'machine %s login cachet password %s\n' "${host}" "${token}" \
          | sudo tee /etc/nix/netrc >/dev/null
        sudo chmod 600 /etc/nix/netrc

        # Register it under authentication.additionalNetrcSources, merging
        # when the installer pre-seeded the file.
        if [ -f /etc/determinate/config.json ]; then
          sudo cat /etc/determinate/config.json \
            | jq '.authentication.additionalNetrcSources = ((.authentication.additionalNetrcSources // []) + ["/etc/nix/netrc"] | unique)' \
            | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp >/dev/null
          sudo mv /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp /etc/determinate/config.json
        else
          printf '{"authentication":{"additionalNetrcSources":["/etc/nix/netrc"]}}\n' \
            | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json >/dev/null
        fi

        # The deployment names its own signing key: fetch the public half
        # from the worker rather than asking consumers to paste it. This
        # doubles as the connectivity check: a cache that cannot answer its
        # public config fails the job here, before the build starts.
        public_key="$(curl -fsSL "${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}/api/public/config" | jq -r '.publicKey')"
        echo "CACHET_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY=${public_key}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
        echo "cachet: read credential provisioned before Determinate starts"

    - uses: DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@61cbfe2efc2d4e7a8a6d56967c3c1058e846c858 # v3.21.9
      with:
        # The substituter and trusted key ride the install because a
        # substituter added after the daemon has started is never consulted.
        extra-conf: |
          extra-substituters = ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
          extra-trusted-public-keys = ${{ env.CACHET_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY }}

    # The Determinate installer logged into FlakeHub on this runner (any job
    # granting id-token: write gets one), which adds cache.flakehub.com as a
    # substituter: every lookup then pays a 401 round trip before falling
    # through to cachet. Log out; the cachet credential is independent.
    - name: Log out of FlakeHub Cache, which this deployment does not use
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # `|| true`: a job without id-token never logged in, so logout is a
        # no-op there, and this action must not fail a build over a cache it
        # does not use.
        sudo determinate-nixd auth logout || true
        sudo determinate-nixd status || true

    - name: Download and verify the cachet binary
      shell: bash
      env:
        CACHET_VERSION: ${{ inputs.cachet-version }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        case "${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}" in
          Linux-X64) triple="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;;
          Linux-ARM64) triple="aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;;
          macOS-X64) triple="x86_64-apple-darwin" ;;
          macOS-ARM64) triple="aarch64-apple-darwin" ;;
          *)
            echo "cachet: no cachet release for ${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}" >&2
            exit 1
            ;;
        esac
        base="https://github.com/nox-systems/cachet/releases/download/v${CACHET_VERSION}"
        artifact="cachet-${triple}.tar.xz"
        work="$(mktemp -d)"
        # The checksum verifies before the archive opens: a tampered or
        # truncated download fails the job, it does not limp onward.
        curl -fsSL -o "${work}/${artifact}" "${base}/${artifact}"
        curl -fsSL -o "${work}/${artifact}.sha256" "${base}/${artifact}.sha256"
        (cd "${work}" && shasum -a 256 -c "${artifact}.sha256")
        install_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/cachet-bin"
        mkdir -p "${install_dir}"
        tar -xJf "${work}/${artifact}" -C "${install_dir}" --strip-components=1
        rm -rf "${work}"
        echo "CACHET_BIN=${install_dir}/cachet" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
        "${install_dir}/cachet" --version

    - name: Configure cachet
      shell: bash
      env:
        CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
        CACHET_AUDIENCE: ${{ inputs.audience }}
        CACHET_PROJECT: ${{ inputs.project }}
        CACHET_ROOTS: ${{ inputs.roots }}
        CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL: ${{ inputs.upstream-url }}
        CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF: ${{ inputs.default-branch-ref }}
        CACHET_PUSH: ${{ inputs.push }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail

        # Confirm the daemon's netrc authenticates against cachet, so a
        # regression surfaces in the log rather than as a silent rebuild: a
        # 404 means the credential is present and authenticated (the probed
        # path is simply absent), while a 401 means it is not.
        daemon_netrc="$(nix config show netrc-file 2>/dev/null || echo /nix/var/determinate/netrc)"
        probe_code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --netrc-file "${daemon_netrc}" \
          "${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}/0000000000000000000000000000000a.narinfo" 2>/dev/null || echo 000)"
        echo "cachet: read auth probe returned ${probe_code} (404 = authenticated, 401 = not)"

        # Everything the post step reads is exported here, and this is the
        # only place any of it is resolved. A step-level `env:` block is
        # scoped to its own step, so passing these to the nested action as
        # `with:` inputs left the post step reading empty strings.
        project="${CACHET_PROJECT}"
        if [ -z "${project}" ]; then
          project="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY//\//-}"
        fi
        # why: the heredoc form rather than `NAME=value`. `roots` takes
        # several installables and the post step splits on any whitespace,
        # so a caller writing them one per line with a YAML block scalar is
        # using the documented shape, and a bare `NAME=value` line cannot
        # express a newline: GitHub rejects the whole file with "Invalid
        # format" when it sees the continuation.
        env_file() {
          printf '%s<<CACHET_EOF_1c7f\n%s\nCACHET_EOF_1c7f\n' "$1" "$2" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
        }
        env_file CACHET_CACHE_URL "${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}"
        env_file CACHET_AUDIENCE "${CACHET_AUDIENCE}"
        env_file CACHET_PROJECT "${project}"
        env_file CACHET_ROOTS "${CACHET_ROOTS}"
        env_file CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL "${CACHET_UPSTREAM_URL}"
        env_file CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF "${CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF}"
        env_file CACHET_PUSH "${CACHET_PUSH}"
        echo "cachet: configured ${CACHET_CACHE_URL} as a substituter for project ${project}"

    # The nested JavaScript action: its main step snapshots the store, and
    # its post step, on success only, pushes. It reads no inputs, because
    # the step above resolved everything into the job environment.
    # why: the full owner/repo/path@ref form rather than `./post`. A
    # composite action resolves a relative `./post` against the consumer's
    # workspace rather than this action's own directory, so a cross-repo
    # consumer failed with "Can't find 'action.yml'". The ref names the v1
    # major tag, which every release in the 1.x line moves forward, so the
    # composite and its post action always come from the same line.
    - uses: nox-systems/cachet/action/post@v1

name: cachet push
description: >-
  Snapshots the nix store at main time and pushes what the job added at post
  time, on success only. The cachet setup composite action wraps this; it is
  not meant to be used directly.

1	# The action consumers wire into their CI: install Determinate Nix trusting
2	# this cache, provision the job's read credential before the daemon starts,
3	# download the pinned cachet binary, and hand the push phases to the nested
4	# main/post action. Signing happens server-side, so the action holds no key
5	# material; the job's OIDC token is the only credential it ever touches.
6	name: cachet setup
7	description: >-
8	  Install Determinate Nix wired to a cachet deployment, then push what the
9	  job builds. Needs `permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }`.
10	author: nox-systems
11	inputs:
12	  cache-url:
13	    description: The cache's base URL.
14	    required: true
15	  roots:
16	    description: >-
17	      Flake installables whose closures this project keeps. Their outputs
18	      are pushed unconditionally and, on the default branch, become the
19	      project's garbage-collection lease.
20	    required: false
21	    default: ""
22	  audience:
23	    description: The OIDC audience the cache requires.
24	    required: false
25	    default: cachet
26	  project:
27	    description: >-
28	      The lease name for this repository. Defaults to the owner and name
29	      joined by a hyphen (`my-org-my-repo`), because a renewal replaces the
30	      lease wholesale: two same-named repositories in one org would
31	      otherwise overwrite each other's.
32	    required: false
33	    default: ""
34	  upstream-url:
35	    description: The upstream cache to filter against before pushing.
36	    required: false
37	    default: https://cache.nixos.org
38	  default-branch-ref:
39	    description: >-
40	      The ref permitted to renew the lease. The cache enforces this itself;
41	      this input only avoids a request that would be refused.
42	    required: false
43	    default: refs/heads/main
44	  push:
45	    description: Set to false to use the cache read-only.
46	    required: false
47	    default: "true"
48	  cachet-version:
49	    description: The cachet release to download and run.
50	    required: false
51	    default: 0.0.1
52	
53	runs:
54	  using: composite
55	  steps:
56	    # Provision the read credential BEFORE Determinate is installed and its
57	    # daemon starts. determinate-nixd synthesizes the netrc the daemon reads
58	    # at daemon start, merging every file under
59	    # authentication.additionalNetrcSources, and that startup synthesis is
60	    # the only reliable one on these runners. Writing the credential and its
61	    # registration here means the daemon's start-up synthesis sees both.
62	    - name: Provision the cachet read credential before Determinate starts
63	      shell: bash
64	      env:
65	        CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
66	        CACHET_AUDIENCE: ${{ inputs.audience }}
67	      run: |
68	        set -euo pipefail
69	
70	        # The OIDC token authenticates this job's reads; the runner is
71	        # authorized because it is provably the org's CI. Minted here,
72	        # without nix, because Determinate is not installed yet. This check
73	        # fails the job on purpose: every later step assumes the token.
74	        if [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ]; then
75	          echo "cachet: this job cannot mint an OIDC token." >&2
76	          echo "  Add 'permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }' to the job." >&2
77	          exit 1
78	        fi
79	        token="$(curl -fsSL \
80	          -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}" \
81	          "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL}&audience=${CACHET_AUDIENCE}" | jq -r '.value')"
82	        host="$(printf '%s' "${CACHET_CACHE_URL}" | sed -e 's#^https\?://##' -e 's#/.*$##')"
83	
84	        # The credential file: real, outside the nix store, 0600.
85	        sudo mkdir -p /etc/nix /etc/determinate
86	        printf 'machine %s login cachet password %s\n' "${host}" "${token}" \
87	          | sudo tee /etc/nix/netrc >/dev/null
88	        sudo chmod 600 /etc/nix/netrc
89	
90	        # Register it under authentication.additionalNetrcSources, merging
91	        # when the installer pre-seeded the file.
92	        if [ -f /etc/determinate/config.json ]; then
93	          sudo cat /etc/determinate/config.json \
94	            | jq '.authentication.additionalNetrcSources = ((.authentication.additionalNetrcSources // []) + ["/etc/nix/netrc"] | unique)' \
95	            | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp >/dev/null
96	          sudo mv /etc/determinate/config.json.tmp /etc/determinate/config.json
97	        else
98	          printf '{"authentication":{"additionalNetrcSources":["/etc/nix/netrc"]}}\n' \
99	            | sudo tee /etc/determinate/config.json >/dev/null
100	        fi
101	
102	        # The deployment names its own signing key: fetch the public half
103	        # from the worker rather than asking consumers to paste it. This
104	        # doubles as the connectivity check: a cache that cannot answer its
105	        # public config fails the job here, before the build starts.
106	        public_key="$(curl -fsSL "${CACHET_CACHE_URL%/}/api/public/config" | jq -r '.publicKey')"
107	        echo "CACHET_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY=${public_key}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
108	        echo "cachet: read credential provisioned before Determinate starts"
109	
110	    - uses: DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@61cbfe2efc2d4e7a8a6d56967c3c1058e846c858 # v3.21.9
111	      with:
112	        # The substituter and trusted key ride the install because a
113	        # substituter added after the daemon has started is never consulted.
114	        extra-conf: |
115	          extra-substituters = ${{ inputs.cache-url }}
116	          extra-trusted-public-keys = ${{ env.CACHET_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY }}
117	
118	    # The Determinate installer logged into FlakeHub on this runner (any job
119	    # granting id-token: write gets one), which adds cache.flakehub.com as a
120	    # substituter: every lookup then pays a 401 round trip before falling
121	    # through to cachet. Log out; the cachet credential is independent.
122	    - name: Log out of FlakeHub Cache, which this deployment does not use
123	      shell: bash
124	      run: |
125	        set -euo pipefail
126	        # `|| true`: a job without id-token never logged in, so logout is a
127	        # no-op there, and this action must not fail a build over a cache it
128	        # does not use.
129	        sudo determinate-nixd auth logout || true
130	        sudo determinate-nixd status || true
131	
132	    - name: Download and verify the cachet binary
133	      shell: bash
134	      env:
135	        CACHET_VERSION: ${{ inputs.cachet-version }}
136	      run: |
137	        set -euo pipefail
138	        case "${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}" in
139	          Linux-X64) triple="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;;
140	          Linux-ARM64) triple="aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;;
141	          macOS-X64) triple="x86_64-apple-darwin" ;;
142	          macOS-ARM64) triple="aarch64-apple-darwin" ;;
143	          *)
144	            echo "cachet: no cachet release for ${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}" >&2
145	            exit 1
146	            ;;
147	        esac
148	        base="https://github.com/nox-systems/cachet/releases/download/v${CACHET_VERSION}"
149	        artifact="cachet-${triple}.tar.xz"
150	        work="$(mktemp -d)"
151	        # The checksum verifies before the archive opens: a tampered or
152	        # truncated download fails the job, it does not limp onward.
153	        curl -fsSL -o "${work}/${artifact}" "${base}/${artifact}"
154	        curl -fsSL -o "${work}/${artifact}.sha256" "${base}/${artifact}.sha256"
155	        (cd "${work}" && shasum -a 256 -c "${artifact}.sha256")
156	        install_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/cachet-bin"
157	        mkdir -p "${install_dir}"
158	        tar -xJf "${work}/${artifact}" -C "${install_dir}" --strip-components=1
159	        rm -rf "${work}"
160	        echo "CACHET_BIN=${install_dir}/cachet" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
161	        "${install_dir}/cachet" --version
162	
163	    - name: Configure cachet
164	      shell: bash
165	      env:
166	        CACHET_CACHE_URL: ${{ inputs.cache-url }}

The user is asking about the admin design: CACHET_ADMINS env var vs a database. They noticed from my earlier work (verdict.rs: admins(env) + require_admin; wrangler.toml has ADMINS("lane-dev")) that admins are configured via an environment variable.

Answer plainly and correctly:
- Right: admins are a configuration list, not database rows. CACHET_ADMINS is a comma-separated var of GitHub logins. The worker reads it per request (vars are deployment config set at deploy time via alchemy/wrangler).
- The identity comes from the *authentication layer*, not the env: the session/OAuth or device-flow GitHub token → /user → login; verdict cached in KV. The env var is just the set membership test for admin-gated routes (/api/self/*).
- Why no DB: the whole design says KV for auth verdicts/sessions only, R2 for cache data, no database. Admin changes are rare and operator-owned: changing an admin = redeploy config. That's deliberate per the requirement "KV for auth verdicts and sessions only" and "one deployment serves one GitHub org".
- Consequences: add/remove admin = edit vars + redeploy; no runtime grant flow, no admin API. Auditable in infra code (infra/ module later).

Keep the answer short and in GENERAL mode prose. This is a question, not a task change — answer and continue the work.

content.text:
Yes — admins are deployment configuration, not database rows. `CACHET_ADMINS` is a comma-separated var of GitHub logins, set alongside `CACHET_ORGS` at deploy time (alchemy in `infra/` for real deploys, `[vars]` in `wrangler.toml` for the lane). The request path works like this: the caller authenticates with their GitHub token or browser session, the worker resolves their *login* through the verdict path (GitHub `/user` plus org-membership check, cached in KV), and `require_admin` compares that login against the env list before serving `/api/self/*` routes (GC reports, stats).

Two deliberate consequences: there is no admin-granting API (you can't escalate through the worker by calling it), and adding or removing an admin means editing config and redeploying — which for this system is also the audit trail, since the var lives in infra code. A membership set that changes rarely and is owned by the same person who owns the deployment doesn't want a database; it wants `terraform apply`-style friction.

The one rule to keep straight: it's *logins*, not emails — the verdict resolves a GitHub username, and that's what the list must contain.

              (cd proj-gen && actionlint -shellcheck "" release.yml)

# cargo-deny: the supply-chain gate, run by `just deny`. Every dependency is
# attack surface, so the set is held to four checks: no known advisory, only
# accepted licenses, no banned or duplicated crates, and crates.io as the
# only source.

[advisories]
version = 2
# A new advisory can land against an unchanged tree, so this check is a
# time-varying signal: a `just deny` failure here means triage now, not
# necessarily a regression in the change under review.
yanked = "deny"
# Each ignore is a deliberate, justified triage decision, revisited whenever
# the dependency tree changes. An entry names the advisory and proves the
# vulnerable path is unreachable here.
ignore = [
    # `paste` is unmaintained, not vulnerable: a compile-time proc-macro
    # helper pulled in by hegeltest, the property lane's engine. It is a
    # dev-graph dependency: its generated code appears only in test binaries
    # and never enters the shipped worker. No replacement exists on the
    # pinned hegeltest version; the entry dies with the crate when the tree
    # moves.
    "RUSTSEC-2024-0436",
    # The Marvin advisory covers RSA private-key operations (decrypt and
    # sign) leaking through timing. cachet has no private RSA key anywhere:
    # the only RSA use is PUBLIC-key verification of GitHub OIDC tokens
    # against presented JWKs, so the vulnerable path is unreachable. The
    # `rsa` crate exists for hosts and tests; the deployed worker verifies
    # with workerd crypto, at which point `rsa` leaves the production
    # graph and this ignore dies with it.
    "RUSTSEC-2023-0071",
]

[licenses]
version = 2
# Permissive licenses only. cachet ships as Apache-2.0 open source; copyleft
# and unknown terms are refused so downstream redistribution stays simple.
allow = [
    "MIT",
    "Apache-2.0",
    "Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception",
    "BSD-2-Clause",
    "BSD-3-Clause",
    "ISC",
    "Unicode-3.0",
    "Zlib",
    # why: the BSD Zero Clause license is OSI-approved and strictly more
    # permissive than MIT (public-domain-equivalent, no attribution
    # required), so it carries no obligation at all.
    "0BSD",
    # why: MPL-2.0 is weak, file-level copyleft: obligations trigger only
    # when a covered file is modified and distributed, which cachet never
    # does. Its consumer is webpki-roots, the CLI's certificate bundle.
    "MPL-2.0",
]
confidence-threshold = 0.93
# why: the workspace crates are publish = false; they are the product being
# built, not dependencies, so the license check skips them.
private = { ignore = true }

[bans]
# A duplicate major version is two copies of attack surface and a larger
# bundle; flag it so a single version is chosen deliberately. A wildcard
# version is refused outright: a dependency pins to a real range.
multiple-versions = "warn"
wildcards = "deny"
# The internal crates depend on each other by path, which has no version and
# reads as a wildcard; the ban still applies to external crates.
allow-wildcard-paths = true
# ring and aws-lc do not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown. The C zstd crate
# does not either; ruzstd supplies the worker's only decompression need.
# These crates are banned doc-first and this table is the enforcement: a
# pull request that adds one fails here, before the wasm build would.
deny = [
    { name = "ring", reason = "does not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown" },
    { name = "aws-lc-rs", reason = "does not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown" },
    { name = "aws-lc-sys", reason = "does not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown" },
    { name = "zstd", reason = "C library, does not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown; use ruzstd" },
    { name = "zstd-sys", reason = "C library, does not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown; use ruzstd" },
]

[sources]
unknown-registry = "deny"
unknown-git = "deny"
allow-registry = ["https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"]

# cargo-deny: the supply-chain gate, run by `just deny`. Every dependency is
# attack surface, so the set is held to four checks: no known advisory, only
# accepted licenses, no banned or duplicated crates, and crates.io as the
# only source.

[advisories]
version = 2
# A new advisory can land against an unchanged tree, so this check is a
# time-varying signal: a `just deny` failure here means triage now, not
# necessarily a regression in the change under review.
yanked = "deny"
# Each ignore is a deliberate, justified triage decision, revisited whenever
# the dependency tree changes. An entry names the advisory and proves the
# vulnerable path is unreachable here.
ignore = [
    # `paste` is unmaintained, not vulnerable: a compile-time proc-macro
    # helper pulled in by hegeltest, the property lane's engine. It is a
    # dev-graph dependency: its generated code appears only in test binaries
    # and never enters the shipped worker. No replacement exists on the
    # pinned hegeltest version; the entry dies with the crate when the tree
    # moves.
    "RUSTSEC-2024-0436",
    # The Marvin advisory covers RSA private-key operations (decrypt and
    # sign) leaking through timing. cachet has no private RSA key anywhere:
    # the only RSA use is PUBLIC-key verification of GitHub OIDC tokens
    # against presented JWKs, so the vulnerable path is unreachable. The
    # `rsa` crate exists for hosts and tests; the deployed worker verifies
    # with workerd crypto, at which point `rsa` leaves the production
    # graph and this ignore dies with it.
    "RUSTSEC-2023-0071",
]

[licenses]
version = 2
# Permissive licenses only. cachet ships as Apache-2.0 open source; copyleft
# and unknown terms are refused so downstream redistribution stays simple.
allow = [
    "MIT",
    "Apache-2.0",
    "Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception",
    "BSD-2-Clause",
    "BSD-3-Clause",
    "ISC",
    "Unicode-3.0",
    "Zlib",
    # why: the BSD Zero Clause license is OSI-approved and strictly more
    # permissive than MIT (public-domain-equivalent, no attribution
    # required), so it carries no obligation at all.
    "0BSD",
    # why: MPL-2.0 is weak, file-level copyleft: obligations trigger only
    # when a covered file is modified and distributed, which cachet never
    # does. Its consumer is webpki-roots, the CLI's certificate bundle.
    "MPL-2.0",
]
confidence-threshold = 0.93
# why: the workspace crates are publish = false; they are the product being
# built, not dependencies, so the license check skips them.
private = { ignore = true }

[bans]
# A duplicate major version is two copies of attack surface and a larger
# bundle; flag it so a single version is chosen deliberately. A wildcard
# version is refused outright: a dependency pins to a real range.
multiple-versions = "warn"
wildcards = "deny"
# The internal crates depend on each other by path, which has no version and
# reads as a wildcard; the ban still applies to external crates.
allow-wildcard-paths = true
# ring and aws-lc do not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown. The C zstd crate
# does not either; ruzstd supplies the worker's only decompression need.
# These crates are banned doc-first and this table is the enforcement: a
# pull request that adds one fails here, before the wasm build would.
deny = [
    { name = "ring", reason = "does not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown" },

    { name = "aws-lc-sys", reason = "does not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown" },

    { name = "zstd-sys", reason = "C library, does not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown; use ruzstd" },
]

# CLAUDE.md: the cachet constitution

cachet is a self-hostable nix binary cache on Cloudflare Workers, written
in Rust with workers-rs. This document binds every contribution and every
agent that works in this repository. Every rule carries its reason.

## §0 The prime directive

A gate, lane, or doc name exists in conversation only when it exists in the
flake, the justfile, or the manifest. Suggesting a check that cannot run is
a defect. When you add one, land the verb, the CI job, and the doc row in
one commit.

## §1 The stack

The worker runs on workers-rs compiled to wasm32-unknown-unknown, with R2
as the only cache-data store and KV for auth verdicts and sessions only.
Deployments are provisioned by an alchemy-run program under `infra/`; the
`cachet` CLI ships natively through cargo-dist; the GitHub Action lives in
this repo under `action/`. The three auth flows are GitHub OIDC for
writes, GitHub device flow for laptop reads, and browser OAuth with KV
sessions for the future SPA. Signing is server-side only, and a narinfo is
signed only after its stored NAR verifies byte-for-byte.

## §2 The prose law

PROSE.md governs every Markdown file, comment, and user-visible string in
this repository, including its own README. The doc-manifest gate enforces
that the manifest in §11 loads all of it.

## §3 Clock, entropy, and layout determinism

Time comes from a Clock seam sampled once at request start; entropy comes
from an Rng seam wired only at the worker edge; map layout uses BTreeMap
and BTreeSet. clippy.toml bans the ambient forms and the ban is
mechanical, not advisory. Banned verbatim: SystemTime::now, Instant::now,
thread::spawn, HashMap, HashSet.

## §4 Crate boundaries

The dependency direction is one-way: cachet-core is pure; cachet-crypto
computes; cachet-api describes the HTTP surface and generates the OpenAPI
document; cachet-worker is the wasm32 deployable that owns every binding;
cachet-push and cachet-cli are native writer tools. cachet-worker fails
host builds and is excluded from workspace default-members; its build and
its truth lane are the wasm verbs. A path dependency against this
direction fails review.

## §5 Wasm and crypto hygiene

ring, aws-lc-rs, aws-lc-sys, and the C zstd crate do not build for
wasm32-unknown-unknown and are banned in deny.toml. Hashing uses sha2,
signing uses ed25519-dalek, decompression uses ruzstd, and RS256 uses the
crypto decided in docs/adr. scripts/check-wasm-hygiene.sh scans the shipped
bundle for the banned runtimes and for secret-shaped strings; the gate
protects the artifact, not intentions.

## §6 Dependencies

Versions pin exactly where generation behavior matters and by minor series
elsewhere. New dependencies need one `// why:` comment at their
Cargo.toml entry: what they do and why nothing in the tree already does it.

## §7 Errors and panics

External-input failures are typed errors with the error-code table's
vocabulary; RFC 9457 problem+json bodies leave the worker. Invariant
violations panic with named invariants, and an attacker-reachable
condition never panics. Test code panics on missing fixtures rather than
skipping.

## §8 The manifest gates

Three bijections keep docs and runs honest, all enforced by scripts in
`scripts/`: the §11 manifest against the repo's non-ADR Markdown
(check-doc-manifest.sh), docs/testing/lanes.toml against the lane docs
and CI jobs (check-lane-manifest.sh), and cachet-api's route descriptors
against the committed docs/openapi.yaml (check-openapi-drift.sh).

## §9 The lanes

Every test belongs to exactly one lane, and each lane is job-named the
same everywhere: the lanes.toml row, the docs/testing doc, the just verb,
and the CI job. A failed test that passes on retry is a bug, never a flake:
retries stay zero. The registry docs/testing/lanes.toml is the list.

## §10 Comments

Code comments state why, not what: `// why:` begins every non-obvious
choice so the reason greps. Rustdoc states what a public item does; the
comment beside it states why the code chose this way.

## §11 Required context

The manifest below is the bijection's source. Scripts assert it loads
exactly the repo's non-ADR Markdown, no more and no less.

@README.md
@PROSE.md
@SECURITY.md
@docs/testing/unit.md
@docs/testing/property.md
@docs/testing/golden.md
@docs/testing/kani.md
@docs/testing/workerd.md

---
# The workerd lane's deployment shape (docs/testing/workerd.md): the same
# module directory and module rules the real deployment uses, against
# workerd's local R2 emulation. The compatibility date trails the newest
# workerd in the devshell, and raising it is a deliberate lane decision.
name = "cachet-worker-lane"
compatibility_date = "2026-05-01"
main = "../crates/cachet-worker/build/index.js"
rules = [
  { type = "CompiledWasm", globs = ["**/*.wasm"], fallthrough = true },
]

[[r2_buckets]]
binding = "CACHE_BUCKET"
bucket_name = "cachet-lane"

# Verdicts, sessions, and OAuth state live in KV; the lane namespace is
# local-emulated, so the id is a label rather than an account resource.
[[kv_namespaces]]
binding = "CACHET_KV"
id = "cachet-lane"

# The lane deployment's auth configuration: a fixed org, audience, and
# branch; CACHET_JWKS_URL and CACHET_GITHUB_API_URL join per run via
# `wrangler dev --var`, pointing at the driver's stub services (the URLs
# are transport configuration; the keys authenticate the tokens, not the
# address they came from).
[vars]
CACHET_ORGS = "lane-org"
CACHET_AUDIENCE = "cachet-lane"
CACHET_DEFAULT_BRANCH_REF = "refs/heads/main"
CACHET_HOST = "cachet.lane.invalid"
CACHET_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID = "lane-oauth-client"
# The laptop token's user is the lane's admin; a second member token
# exercises forbidden_admin.
CACHET_ADMINS = "lane-dev"
# The OAuth web endpoints join per run via --var, like the API URL. The UI
# origin is fixed here so the callback's redirect branch is lane-tested;
# absent in a deployment without a UI, where the callback answers 204.
CACHET_UI_ORIGIN = "https://ui.lane.invalid"
# The collector runs armed with grace zeroed: the lane's seeded objects
# are seconds old and must still be sweepable.
CACHET_GC_GRACE_MS = "0"

# The deployment's collector binding; the lane invokes the scheduled
# handler directly over its dev endpoint.
[triggers]
crons = ["0 5 * * *"]
